0.content:
Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome (also: Abyss Corrosion Syndrome, Draught of Lucidity): Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome is an illness caused by direct contact with high concentrations of Abyssal power. It harms body and mind, can leave irreversible mental trauma, and mostly appears as hallucinations. It is named in Natlan during the Abyssal invasion. The worst cases are treated with the Draught of Lucidity.

The name is given by "The Captain" (Capitano) in the Archon Quest interlude "For the Same Land." Iansan later keeps patient records of the many people she finds affected.

In universe: Symptoms include psychosis, often with sight and sound hallucinations and the reliving of past traumas. Severity follows the patient's level of trauma. In "For the Same Land," Atoco relives a childhood near-drowning, and Cochitta's fear of losing her loved ones is triggered by the memory of her parents' deaths.

Mild cases keep some awareness of the outside world and can be broken out of the hallucination by speaking to the person and by physical contact. Deep cases, such as the warrior Ocotlan, are lost in the hallucination and respond only to medicine.

The Captain says the draught was developed for exactly such cases. Later, Paimon compares another episode in Natlan to the syndrome, noting that it can cause hallucinations and mental breakdowns. Saurians may also be susceptible: Ayo was melancholy after the invasion and the deaths of his grandparents, and a small dose of the draught lifted his mood.

During the Cataclysm, endless battles against the Abyss gave Khaenri'ahn soldiers hallucinations, to the point that some attacked each other. That experience led to the draught. See the Abyssal Corruption and Nature of the Abyss entries for other Abyssal harm.

Treatment: Verbal and physical contact for light cases; the Draught of Lucidity for severe ones.

The draught dispels the psychological effects of the Abyss, but its side effects are severe, including chronic migraines for life. It is therefore reserved for the worst cases. It was made for humans and also works on saurians.

Guthred, a respected Khaenri'ahn military doctor and the Captain's trusted second-in-command, developed the draught and used himself as the test subject to hurry the cure. He died shortly after completing it. In Natlan, the Captain supplied doses to the Flower-Feather Clan to cure their afflicted warriors. Ororon says Guthred's sacrifice for Natlan is a well-known tribal legend, and Mavuika believes the figure the Traveler saw in the Captain was Guthred's soul.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray a patient as sincere but locked in the past, answering people who are not there. Treat the draught as a harsh remedy, not a casual cure. Gentle talk and touch are canon for mild cases.

Do not make the syndrome contagious, a Vision effect or a curse. Do not cure it with a simple potion for all patients. Do not claim Guthred still lives as an independent person.

1.comment: Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome: Draught of Lucidity
1.content:
A medicine developed by the Khaenri'ahn military doctor Guthred to treat Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome. It dispels the psychological impact of the Abyss but can cause chronic migraines for life, so it is used only for severe cases. It works on saurians as well as humans.

After the Abyssal invasion of Natlan, the Captain brought it to the Flower-Feather Clan at a critical moment and cured the most severely affected patients.

2.content:
Adeptal Arts (also: Adeptus Arts, adeptal power, adeptal energy, arts of the adepti, adeptal techniques): The Adeptal Arts are the techniques of Liyue's adepti, the illuminated beasts and gods led by Rex Lapis (Morax). They include alchemy for making elixirs, paper sigils that store adeptal power, the creation of pocket-world abodes, and dream arts. The power is generally harmful or lethal to ordinary mortals, and the adepti guard their methods closely.

Rex Lapis is said to have taught these arts to the adepti. Their elemental abilities come with them, since all adepti can command elemental energy. Mortals who learn a technique do not become adepti.

In universe: Adepti can manipulate elemental energy without a Vision, which is why Liyue's people call them the "three-eyed" mighty and illuminated adepti; their Visions, when worn, are shown as a human convention. Beyond that, each adeptus carries adeptal energy with an effect particular to them, which is dangerous to mortals who spend too long near it.

Core techniques named in canon:
- Alchemy (Dandi), used to refine elixirs. The item text on the Mist Veiled Mercury Elixir says that anyone who swallows an elixir meets certain death, since the power in them is lethal to non-adepti.
- Sigils (Fulu), paper talismans that hold adeptal power as symbols.
- Sub-Space Creation (Waijing), the making of autonomous pocket worlds through imagination. Rex Lapis granted this ability.
- Dream Trawler, the giving and receiving of dreams.
- Mortal Lingering, taking a temporary human form after the original body has died.
- The Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering, a yaksha technique that uses the power of a yaksha mask (see System: Karma).

Sacred names are another feature of adeptal culture: most adepti have a four-character name followed by the honorific "Perfected Lord", of which the English game text usually keeps only the first half, as in Moon Carver or Mountain Shaper. Rex Lapis and Xiao's titles follow other patterns. Not every adeptus uses a sacred name; Madame Ping and Ganyu live under ordinary names.

According to Liyue belief, the adepti shaped the landscape, so that rivers are their saliva and grass their hair. Mountain Shaper calls those claims nonsense and explains that the amber of Mt. Hulao comes from a plant called the karst crawler, though he can control it somewhat.

Other Liyue techniques sit near the Adeptal Arts without being the same thing: the Art of Homa, a secret technique for purifying the border between life and death, descends from a member of the Eight Adepts and is carried on by the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, and the Qimen arts of Chenyu Vale's Lan Clan trace to the adeptus Wind Reader. The wiki also treats Liyue exorcist methods, such as Chongyun's, as derived from adeptal arts, though canon says little more.

Alchemy and elixirs: Adeptal alchemy produces elixirs of great power that kill mortals who swallow them. The Mist Veiled Mercury Elixir is the item the game uses to describe this, and the Mist Veiled Gold Elixir is known for giving weapons transcendent powers. Remedium Tertiorum, a medicine Zhongli once offered for Xiao, temporarily eases the pain of karma and follows the same rule: in his words, nothing of this world can withstand it.

In gameplay, the Parametric Transformer in the Dunyu Ruins turns items into other items; canon says nothing about how it works or where it came from.

Sigils: Sigils (Fulu) store adeptal power in symbols and typically appear as paper talismans. Qiqi wears talismans that hold in the adeptal power inside her body; without them, her profile says it would send her into a berserk state.

Sigils of Permission (Talisman of Nonrestriction) were made by Rex Lapis and carried adeptal power. During the Archon War, mortals used them to channel that power in battle; today most of the power has faded, but adepti still refrain from harming the holder, and Cloud Retainer remarks on them in Custodian of Clouds. In the Archon Quest, the Fatui studied the patterns and made copies; Tartaglia used many at once, together with his Harbinger power, to wake Osial for a short time.

Abodes and dreams: Sub-Space Creation lets an adeptus build a small pocket world, usually a home for themselves. Madame Ping's teapot and the Serenitea Pot are examples; larger abodes such as the Realm of Clouds and the Sea Gazer's Abode were made the same way. Adepti may also make teapot spirits to run an abode, and the spirits receive adeptus names.

The ability has limits: the Serenitea Pot is not a true world, so a whole city cannot be built inside it. It is also regarded as lesser than Rex Lapis's power to move mountains and seas. Energy from Sub-Space Creation gives objects special properties, including soil that stays fertile and warm water all year. The Traveler can use it too, and the wiki suggests this may be because the adepti lent power to them in Turning Point, though canon does not say.

Dream Trawler lets the user enter another person's dream or give them a dream of the user's design. Known practitioners are Rex Lapis and Xiao. Mortal Lingering is attributed to Pervases. In The Purging of Evil, Xiao and the Traveler use Dream Trawler to call up the spirit of the fraud Starsnatcher.

Adeptal energy and mortals: Adeptal energy gives each adeptus a particular effect. In Turning Point, when the Traveler was lent power from Madame Ping, Ganyu and Xiao, Ping's gave shockwaves with attacks, Ganyu's gave healing and Xiao's gave extra speed. Ordinary mortals cannot endure too much of it: their souls are not as robust, and with enough time it overwhelms them.

Qiqi's story shows the danger. When a herb-picking girl was mortally wounded in a clash between adepti and demons, the adepti each gave her a portion of their strength to bring her back. She revived as a zombie, but could not control the adeptal energy raging in her and went berserk, so Mountain Shaper sealed her in amber for hundreds of years. The same profile says a Vision appeared to her as she was dying, and that the adepti accepted this as a valid form of illumination. Zibai's voice-over later calls her an odd case, a girl with the body of an adeptus but not the soul.

The wiki notes that Qiqi can still manipulate the adeptal energy centuries later. Do not describe her as an adeptus; canon calls her a zombie who was kept from death by adeptal power.

Devices and compass: Adepti have also put their arts into devices. Cloud Retainer (Xianyun) believes the laws of nature can be invested in ingenious devices, so she builds mechanisms for the people of Liyue; Zibai notes that she would rather tinker than use her powers. The Fantastic Compass, made by the adeptus Sea Gazer to seal away monsters, is a catalyst that shines when an adeptus and a mortal use it together.

The book that comes with the Compass says that when mortal and adeptal power combine, one can move the heavens and shake the earth. Ancestors of Yelan used it with the yaksha Bosacius to seal the Chasm's Bed during the cataclysm. In Perilous Trail (Interlude Chapter, Act II), Yelan and Xiao activate a conjured version to escape the Chasm's Bed, and Yanfei, who has both human and adeptal ancestry, makes it flicker.

Limits: Adeptal power harms mortals and is not given freely. Humans can learn some adeptal arts, but they do not become adepti, since canon applies the word to non-humans (half-humans can qualify).

Adeptal abilities do not remove limits: the Serenitea Pot cannot hold a city, and not even Sub-Space Creation can restore Padisarah flowers that died out when the Goddess of Flowers fell. Dream arts and sigils take effort and are often kept secret from the public.

Most adepti withdrew to Jueyun Karst after the Archon War, so ordinary people rarely see these arts. Only mortals with a Sigil of Permission may approach the adepti's land without offence, and the Sigil's power has mostly worn off.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): adeptal-themed content includes the Serenitea Pot realm, adeptal-themed furnishings, the Mist Veiled elixirs as weapon-ascension materials, adeptal-themed talents such as Qiqi's Adeptus Art: Preserver of Fortune, and Xiao's Bane of All Evil.

Ganyu, Xiao, Yanfei, Xianyun, Qiqi and other Liyue characters use these themes in their kits. Treat kit names as flavor, not as a full account of the canon arts.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show adeptal power as quiet and costly rather than flashy. A simple talisman glow, a hush, a chill or warmth in the air, or a hint of old incense fits. Adepti guard their methods, so a character who asks about the arts should usually get a partial or indirect answer.

Remind mortals of the danger: elixirs are not for drinking, and long contact with an adeptus leaves the weak-souled uneasy. Do not let an ordinary human perform the highest arts such as Sub-Space Creation unless canon supports it (the Traveler is an unexplained case).

Avoid portraying adeptal energy as an element of its own with fixed rules, or giving every adeptus the same arts; canon shows different effects for Madame Ping, Ganyu and Xiao and says only a few adepti use certain techniques. Keep Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya material out unless a scene needs it.

3.content: Waijing is the adeptal ability to build small, self-contained pocket worlds through imagination. Rex Lapis granted it, and it has been used for abodes: Madame Ping's teapot, Cloud Retainer's Realm of Clouds, Sea Gazer's Abode and the Serenitea Pot. The result is not a true world and cannot hold a whole city, but its energy can make soil fertile and water warm and clear. Adepti also make teapot spirits to manage these homes.

4.content: A talisman made by Rex Lapis and charged with adeptal power. In the Archon War mortals used such sigils to channel power in battle; by the present most of the power has worn off, yet adepti will not harm a holder, and a holder is said to be able to enter Jueyun Karst without offending them. The Fatui copied the design and used the copies to briefly free Osial during the Archon Quest.

5.content: A catalyst made by the adeptus Sea Gazer to seal away monsters, later passed to a human friend and used to exorcise demons together. In the cataclysm, Bosacius and Boyang used it to seal the Chasm's Bed. Its power needs both an adeptus and a mortal; Yanfei, who has both ancestries, can briefly wake it.

6.content:
Aggravate (also: Aggravate reaction, Electro Catalyze reaction): Aggravate is the Electro half of the Catalyze family. First an Electro hit and a Dendro hit meet and put a Quicken aura on the target; after that, further Electro hits on the Quickened target trigger Aggravate, which makes each of them hit harder by a flat amount. It is a combat rule rather than a story event, and the reaction arrived with Version 3.0.

Aggravate does not consume the Quicken aura, so it can fire again and again until the aura runs out. Dendro attacks on the same aura trigger Spread instead, which gives a larger bonus.

In universe: Canon presents Aggravate only through the Elemental Trial tutorial and gameplay text. The wiki records that the Electro and Dendro reaction is said to have a deep connection to the history of Sumeru, but no source read for this entry explains how.

Any link between Electro and Dendro in Sumeru's past, including claims about Nabu Malikata, is inference by wiki editors, not stated canon. Keep scenes from asserting one.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): an Electro attack on a target with a Quicken aura triggers Aggravate and adds an Additive Base DMG Bonus to that attack's damage. Aggravate does not consume the aura.

The bonus is 1.15 times the level multiplier of the character, increased by a percentage from Elemental Mastery and any Reaction DMG Bonus, and then added to the attack's base damage before the usual damage bonuses, CRIT, DEF and RES. Spread is the Dendro version, with coefficient 1.25.

Quicken itself is created when Electro and Dendro meet. Its duration is 6 seconds plus 5 seconds for each gauge unit of the weaker of the two elements involved. Applying Pyro or Hydro to a Quicken aura consumes it and triggers Burning or Bloom instead. A Swirl can also trigger Aggravate secondarily, using the Anemo character's level and EM. Talents and artifact sets exist that increase the bonus.

The wiki gives the Elemental Mastery bonus for Catalyze reactions as approximately 5 x EM / (EM + 1200), applied to the base coefficient times the level multiplier. The final Additive Base DMG Bonus is added to any bonus the attack already had. Enemies and the environment use a slightly different level multiplier above level 60 than characters, and the wiki's table lists no character values for level 100.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show a Quickened target as crackling with green-violet energy, so that each Electro strike lands with extra bite as lightning bites into the growing charge. Keep it a rising intensity, not a new effect.

Narrate Aggravate as repeated strikes getting stronger while the Quicken lasts. Do not describe the plant energy as consumed by the lightning; the aura stays until it decays or Pyro or Hydro ends it.

Limits: Aggravate needs an existing Quicken aura and an Electro attack that can apply Electro; Dendro attacks trigger Spread instead.

The bonus belongs to the attack that triggers it, so Aggravate does nothing on its own and adds nothing to a skill that deals no damage.

The two catalyze bonuses depend on the triggering character: the Electro user's stats count for Aggravate. Gameplay values here are as listed by the wiki as of Version 7.1.

7.content:
Aggravate is the Electro Catalyze reaction (Version 3.0). An Electro attack on a Quickened target gains a flat damage bonus without using up the Quicken aura.

Quicken lasts 6 seconds plus 5 seconds per gauge unit of the weaker element. Dendro attacks on it trigger Spread (coefficient 1.25) rather than Aggravate (1.15), and Pyro or Hydro would instead consume it into Burning or Bloom.

8.content:
Alchemy (also: alchemist arts, Bio-Alchemy, biological alchemy): Alchemy in Teyvat is the art of transmuting and combining matter. In its everyday form it mends, brews and refines; at its peak it can reshape living things, even create them. Mondstadt practises it openly (the Knights of Favonius employ a Chief Alchemist, Albedo), Sumeru's Akademiya studies it in its Spantamad Darshan, Liyue's adepti keep a private version, and Snezhnaya forbids it. The pinnacle is Khaenri'ah's Art of Khemia, which creates life and is tied to the Cataclysm.

This entry covers alchemy as a whole. The Art of Khemia has its own entry, as do individual characters such as Albedo and Sucrose. The same word also names the game's crafting system, which is only a loose reflection of the lore (see gameplay).

In universe: Alchemy is a body of techniques for transforming materials and living things by controlled processes: potions, solutions, transmutation arrays, cauldrons. It does not require a Vision; Sucrose received hers in the middle of an alchemy experiment, not before it. Alchemy comes in levels: ordinary alchemy is limited, while the deepest forms touch the nature of life itself.

Albedo's Character Details say that, to most Mondstadters, alchemy meant little more than mending broken odds and ends, until Albedo arrived and showed what it can do, bringing a corpus of knowledge the Sumeru Akademiya did not have. He describes dust as the most basic form of complex life and demonstrated this by growing a Cecilia from the burnt ash of a flower. The sub-categories most often named are bio-alchemy (modifying or transforming existing life), the Art of Khemia (creating new life) and, in Sumeru, alchemical divination and potion-craft.

Alchemy and the wider mystic arts overlap. The same people often practise astrology, engineering and magic alongside it (Alice is credited with alchemy, astrology, engineering, magic and medicine). The Akademiya treats alchemy as one discipline among many, while Liyue's adepti and Khaenri'ah's alchemists treated it as something closer to a guarded craft.

Mondstadt: Mondstadt practises alchemy openly. The Knights of Favonius count a Chief Alchemist among their ranks; Albedo holds that post, with Sucrose and Timaeus as his assistants. Sucrose practises bio-alchemy, working to modify existing life.

Albedo came to Mondstadt with a recommendation letter from his master Rhinedottir, addressed to Alice, who placed him with the Knights of Favonius, believing they could provide the large laboratory he needed. He prefers fundamental questions: the nature of things and the creation of life. Sucrose's interest runs the other way: using alchemy to modify existing life and add variety and colour to the world. Her results include a special potion that raised the nectar output of Sweet Flowers by 70 percent and a spray that keeps Sunsettias fresh for a month; she treats these as incidental steps toward a larger, still secret, goal.

Sucrose's work is methodical to the point of comedy: she devised thirty-odd rearing plans for the Sweet Flower alone, with control groups for temperature and other conditions, and each result raised more questions. She collects fresh bones from butchers and hunters for skeleton-assembly projects, and her Mist Flower Project (numbered versions of enlarged, tagged specimens) is her private paradise of plants.

Lisa, the Knights' Librarian, is a former member of Sumeru's Spantamad Darshan (the wiki records her as the Akademiya's most distinguished graduate in two centuries). Albedo's Character Story 1 says he is sincerely disappointed that so gifted a person chose to remain a librarian.

Liyue: Liyue's adepti practise their own alchemy, a closely guarded secret that most people do not know exists. The adepti use it to make elixirs. Item text for the Mist Veiled Mercury Elixir says the power in these elixirs is lethal to anyone who is not an adeptus, and the wiki records that Mist Veiled Gold Elixir text says such elixirs can give weapons transcendent power.

Adeptal alchemy is one of the Adeptus Arts, taught to the adepti by Rex Lapis according to the wiki. See the Mystic Arts and Adeptal Arts entries for how it sits among the adepti's other techniques. Canon does not say how it relates to the alchemy of Mondstadt or Sumeru.

Sumeru: At the Sumeru Akademiya, alchemy is one of the fields of the Spantamad Darshan, which specialises in subjects connected with ley lines and the elements. Some scholars of the Amurta Darshan are also skilled in potion-craft.

Two Sumeru developments are named. Alchemical divination is studied by Kimiya of Spantamad; he says Lesser Lord Kusanali invented it, and that it reads the ashes left by a failed, random transmutation as one might read tea leaves, with results such as "the Moon" standing for illusions and lies. The Remelting Effect is a battlefield alchemy invented by the Spantamad alchemist Hajanad, using explosive "Remelting Tablets" that the wiki compares to the Smoldersleet Elixir, which originated in Liyue.

Khaenriah: The Art of Khemia is Khaenri'ah's form of alchemy. Because Khaenri'ah was an underground nation with little natural life, it focused on creating life, and it began as a way to make plants grow without sunlight. It later grew advanced enough to create far more complex beings, and it contributed to the nation's downfall in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. See its own entry for the details.

Albedo learned the art from his master Rhinedottir (Gold), who created him as her masterpiece, a synthetic human, and who taught him in the field. The art can also make ordinary objects such as chairs, replacing the usual manufacturing process. Venti and Dainsleif, who were present when Khaenri'ah fell, are uneasy about Albedo's practice of it.

Snezhnaya: Snezhnaya once practised alchemy freely under the Belyi Tsar, and later banned it. The Tsaritsa now forbids the populace from using alchemy, and the Harbingers enforce the ban. The wiki connects the old freedom to the creation of the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters, which alchemists made by recklessly combining forms of life.

Item text for the 7.0 artifact "Moment That Ceased Upon Waking From Grand Dreams" describes the period before the Tsaritsa took the throne as one in which alchemy was still free, under the long shadow of the Belyi Tsar. The ban therefore dates from after his era, but canon gives no more precise date.

Koshchei and hvergelmir: Koshchei (the Deathless) was a Snezhnayan bio-alchemist and a member of Hvergelmir, the Belyi Tsar's institute for bio-alchemy and Shadow Realm research. He regarded life as a puzzle to be taken apart and reassembled at will. By the account of item text and the wiki, he created the first Aberrant Chimeric Monsters by joining animals, which earned him praise; unsatisfied, he then turned to the Snowland fae, a crime that brought him to the Belyi Tsar's attention, and the Tsar put him to work at Hvergelmir instead of executing him.

At Hvergelmir he met Aksinya, to whom the institute had been entrusted. When he answered her gentleness with a cruel prank (growing an ear in her palm), she replied with calm instructions to submit a request first and gave him a timepiece for his schedule. The encounter left him in a daze and stirred an unfamiliar longing. The wiki's summary of the 7.0 world quests "The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated" and "Chorus of Solace" credits him with the intelligent Chimeric Winged Lion Zver's origin among his abandoned creations and with the Immortal Constructs, and with a later experiment in the village of Okurov in Flamefeather Valley under the name Doctor Moreau. These are summarised from a wiki page; check them against the quests before relying on specifics.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Alchemy is a crafting system used at a Crafting Bench. It combines three lower-tier materials with Mora to make one higher-tier material, and it also produces some potions and gadgets such as Condensed Resin. Adventure Rank unlocks certain recipes.

The Dust of Azoth converts a gem or fragment of one element into another of the same quality. The Dream Solvent converts weekly-boss drops from the same boss into one another, and converts Northlander Billets into Midlander or Borderland Billets and back. The Parametric Transformer, a device found in the Dunyu Ruins and powered by elemental energy, can also transform materials but not in a wholly controllable way. The game's three crafting methods are Crafting, Converting and Mystic Offering.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show alchemy as patient, hands-on process: weighing, dissolving, simmering, chalked arrays, cauldron steam and notebooks of failed trials. Mondstadt alchemists are scholars, not villains; their danger is curiosity, not malice. A Snezhnayan scene should treat alchemy as forbidden and spoken of carefully.

Keep the levels distinct: a common alchemist can mend, brew or purify; modifying living things (bio-alchemy) is a rare skill; creating a life form belongs to Albedo and Rhinedottir. Do not let ordinary alchemists produce homunculi or revive the dead on request. Alchemy is not elemental power and needs no Vision.

Do not say that Albedo makes golems at will or that Khemia was a common Khaenri'ahn skill. Do not blur the adepti's lethal elixirs with Mondstadt's potions. Do not have Sucrose reveal her secret aim, which canon never states.

Limits: Canon never lists exactly what alchemy cannot do. It is shown as skilled, not omnipotent: Sucrose's experiments often fail (her Vision came from one that burned her dandelion seeds to a crisp), and the Remelting Effect and alchemical divination have narrow uses.

The highest feats are tied to one master (Rhinedottir) and her student. The Art of Khemia's creations are not guaranteed to be safe: Rhinedottir's creations helped bring about the Cataclysm, and failed experiments existed alongside her masterpieces.

9.content:
Bio-alchemy focuses on changing existing life. In Mondstadt its practitioners are Sucrose and, according to the wiki, Rhinedottir; Sucrose most likely learned it from Albedo. Sucrose uses it to improve plants and preservation, not to create new beings. Snezhnaya's bio-alchemists, such as Koshchei, went much further and were suppressed.

Sucrose's approach is curiosity-led: she asks why a living thing behaves as it does, then designs experiments. Canon does not say that she has attempted anything like creating life.

10.content:
The Aberrant Chimeric Monsters are an enemy group found in Snezhnaya. The Adventure Handbook calls them creations of the biological alchemy that once flourished there before it was forbidden. They were made in the Belyi Tsar's reign by alchemists, above all Koshchei, who combined many forms of life. Most were consumed in the war against the Onslaught of Dark Beasts, and the few survivors are rare and dangerous. Named types include the Chimeric Armored Beast, Burrowbeast, Winged Elephant, Horned Bear and Winged Lion, and the Immortal Construct.

Item text describes the earliest creations as winged four-legged beasts, and insect-winged, casqued tigers and leopards. Many were deemed failures and abandoned. One Chimeric Winged Lion gained a degree of intelligence and was taken in by the Belyi Tsar, who named it Zver.

11.content: Two Sumeru alchemies from Spantamad: alchemical divination (reading the ashes from a failed transmutation, said to have been invented by Lesser Lord Kusanali) and the Remelting Effect, which uses explosive Remelting Tablets invented by Hajanad. Both appear in Akademiya-related quests.

12.content:
Anemo (also: Anemo element, element of wind): Anemo is the element of wind, one of Teyvat's seven elements. Its Archon is Barbatos, who lives in Mondstadt as the bard Venti; Mondstadt is the nation of wind and freedom. People with Anemo Visions raise gusts and updrafts, pull or push things with vortices, and glide on the wind. The Anemo Dragon Sovereign is Dvalin, once called Stormterror. The Harbinger Signora took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti for the Tsaritsa.

Neuvillette calls Barbatos "the God of Breeze and Hope." Anemo ascension gems are Vayuda Turquoise.

In universe: Most people cannot use Anemo. Those who can usually hold an Anemo Vision. Venti draws on the Anemo Authority of his divine throne in Celestia instead; the "Vision" on his hip is, in his words, "a glowing glass ball I carry around to avoid suspicion."

Legend says that after Barbatos became Archon about 2,600 years ago, he blew away the ice and snow left by the Archon War, scattered mountains, flattened cliffs into plains and guided warm monsoons into Mondstadt. Legend also credits his blessing with making the first wind gliders fly. Mondstadters call their wine a "gift from the Anemo Archon."

Anemo is tied to the old idea of "the thousand winds." In Mondstadt the phrase means the named, personified winds said to protect the land. Venti was once "a single thread" of them, a tiny nameless wind spirit, before he gathered power and rose to godhood, and his power over wind is often described as calling on the thousand winds. In Enkanomiya belief, though, "the thousand winds of time" means Istaroth, the Ruler of Time. Sacrificial Bow text records that ancestors on the eastern cliffs worshipped "the masters of Time and Anemo together", with the saying "Anemo brings stories while Time nurtures them." Canon leaves the exact relationship between wind and time open.

Origins: Origins, as canon tells them. The elemental Authorities first belonged to the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons of the old world. The Heavenly Principles stole part of that power and tied it to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (revealed in the Fontaine Archon Quest, 4.1); Visions also derive from these Authorities. In the Natlan Archon Quest (5.1), the Lord of the Night reveals that the Heavenly Principles created elemental energy by dividing the raw elemental currents of the Light Realm into seven, using Phlogiston, Teyvat's primordial energy, as a base; the result was easier to control and meant to better counter the Abyss. How an Archon relates to their element, and why a nation takes on its element's character, is still unexplained.

Archon and nation: Archon: Barbatos (Venti), the God of Freedom, who with Morax is one of the two surviving original members of The Seven. Nation: Mondstadt, which he deliberately leaves to govern itself.

He became Archon about 2,600 years ago after the rebellion against Decarabian, the God of Storms, then withdrew from rule for fear of becoming a tyrant. Few Mondstadters know that the bard Venti is their god. Venti calls himself the weakest Archon, because Archons draw power from how much control they hold over their nations.

The Anemo throne was contested. In the Age of Kings, Decarabian, behind his storm wall, and Boreas, a wolf-god from the north whose blizzards engulfed the land, were locked in a stalemate. After Vennessa's rebellion against the aristocracy a thousand years ago, Barbatos established the Four Winds as Mondstadt's protectors: the Wolf of the North, the Lion of the South, the Dragon of the East and the Falcon of the West. They were worshipped for about 500 years before people forgot them. Mondstadt is governed by the Knights of Favonius, and the Church of Favonius tends his worship. According to the Biography of Gunnhildr, the wind spirit who would become Barbatos answered the prayers of the Gunnhildr Clan (Jean's family line) in the blizzards, sheltered them and gave Gunnhildr "the power to protect."

Succession: Varka's Story Quest (Version Luna V, 6.4) reveals that after Decarabian fell, Boreas judged himself unworthy to be the Anemo Archon because he lacked a god's love for humanity. Boreas was a wolf from Snezhnaya made a god by Koitar's blessing in Nod-Krai. He returned to the Royal Court of the Seelie in Nod-Krai and went into slumber. The wind spirit became Barbatos and (per Venti's character stories) took the form and name of his fallen friend, the bard Venti. Boreas's later manifestation at Wolvendom, Andrius, is a temporary form made of ice and wind.

Gnosis and authority: In Ending Note (Prologue, 1.0), Signora ambushed a weakened Venti and pulled the Anemo Gnosis from his chest. A Gnosis, Venti explained, is an Archon's internal focus that resonates directly with Celestia. Later canon shows that Archons keep their divine thrones and their elemental power without a Gnosis.

Venti also told the Traveler that Vision holders are "allogenes" who may one day ascend. Besides her own Cryo Gnosis, the Tsaritsa gained the Anemo and Geo Gnoses first, then the Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses; the Pyro Gnosis never reached her. In the official teaser "A Winter Night's Lazzo", in which the Harbingers gather to mourn Signora, the Anemo and Geo Gnoses appear as pieces on Pierro's chessboard.

Gnosis event note: During the limited-time event "Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind" (6.4, part "For a Reunion Without Tears"), Venti said he had deliberately held back against Signora, since fighting her at greater strength would likely have destroyed the city.

Gnosis status: In the 7.1 Archon Quest "A Rekviem for the Underworld", Anastasya (the Tsaritsa) used her Cryo mastery together with the six Gnoses, the Anemo Gnosis among them, to slow time within a room of her palace and stall Rhinedottir. As of 7.1 the Anemo Gnosis remains in her possession.

Elemental beings: Dvalin, the Anemo Dragon Sovereign, and Anemo elemental lifeforms such as slimes, specters and the Anemo Hypostasis.

Dvalin, Dragon of the East, was born from a convergence of elemental energy in the high heavens and succeeded an unnamed, dead Anemo Sovereign. Anemo Samachurls are hilichurl shamans who command the winds.

- Dvalin befriended Barbatos and has full command of sky and wind.
- Anemo Slimes form when Anemo scattered through nature coalesces, and float on the wind. Anemo Specters live on Seirai and Watatsumi in Inazuma. The Samachurls' power over the flowing winds "stems from dark, forgotten memories."
- Gods of wind: Barbatos himself began as an elemental wind spirit. Decarabian, the God of Storms, ruled Old Mondstadt behind a storm wall.
- Anemoculi: consolidated winds that, according to The Blessings of The Seven, only allogenes and the Traveler can see.

Known uses: Gusts and updrafts, gliding, whirlwinds that gather foes or debris, and pushing things away. Anemo also scatters other elements.

Anemo also raises barriers: Decarabian's storm wall resisted even Boreas, and a storm barrier sealed Stormterror's Lair in the Prologue. It can sharpen the senses: Kazuha reads the sounds of nature to sense rain or snow from a single gust.

- Reshaping land and climate: Barbatos moved mountains and brought warm monsoons to Mondstadt.
- The Wanderer first "could hear the wind's voice" at the moment his Vision came.
- The Traveler: in Bird's Eye View, Paimon takes the Traveler to the Statue of The Seven of the god who "controls the wind", and Anemo is the first element they wield. In the Prologue their Anemo power suddenly flares near Venti and Dvalin, startling the dragon and breaking Venti's attempt to heal him.
- Recovery: Venti purged Abyssal magic he had caught from Dvalin with the help of the great oak at Windrise, and returned there to recover after losing his Gnosis.

- Visions are personal: Sucrose's Anemo Vision appeared in her cauldron during her 159th dandelion-seed simmering experiment, and Kazuha, who holds an Anemo Vision, once briefly awakened his late friend's Masterless Electro Vision.

Limits: Anemo does not react with Geo or Dendro.

Swirl spreads an element that is already present; it does not create one. A Vision fixes its holder to one element: Kazuha's brief Electro use came from a second, borrowed Vision.

Gameplay: an Anemo aura cannot be applied by attacks; the exception is the Anemo Hypostasis, which coats itself in Anemo while its core is exposed. Masterless Visions lose their element and power when their holder dies, though some later resonate with a new person.

Interactions: Swirl: when Anemo meets Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo it spreads that element to nearby targets (own entry).

Elemental Absorption: many Anemo skills take on Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo on first contact and deal that element's damage as well.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Anemo is a damage type and the element of characters such as Venti, Jean, Sucrose, Xiao, Kaedehara Kazuha, the Wanderer and Xianyun.

Anemo elemental enemies are immune to Anemo damage, and Anemo Samachurls resist it. The Elemental Resonance "Impetuous Winds" (two or more Anemo characters) cuts stamina use by 15%, raises movement speed by 10% and shortens skill cooldowns by 5%. Many Anemo talents create Vacuum Fields that pull or push targets. Anemoculi raise the Statues of The Seven in Mondstadt, and Anemo Sigils are a Mondstadt currency. Exploration includes Wind Currents (updrafts), Storm Barriers around objects and Anemo Ambers that release an updraft when broken. Swirl damage scales with the Anemo user's level and Elemental Mastery rather than ATK. Every Traveler begins as Anemo, resonating with a Statue of The Seven in Mondstadt in Bird's Eye View (Prologue Act I).

Gameplay recent: Gameplay, recent additions: Stellar Swirl (7.0) is a Stellar Glimmer reaction pairing Anemo with Cryo. It deals Anemo damage and leaves a Stellar Vortex that bursts for Cryo area damage, grows stronger with repeated triggers and briefly boosts jump height (own entry). Recent Anemo characters include Chasca, Varka (6.4) and Vesna (7.1); the Elements page lists Vesna's element source as a Stellar Linchpin rather than a Vision.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Anemo as pressure, sound and motion: cloaks snapping, grass flattening in a ring, dust spiralling. Teal or aqua-green light is a safe cue; Venti's braids glow Anemo-aqua when he uses his power. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can knock people down or glide from a cliff, but reshaping mountains is an Archon's work.

Wind users can plausibly notice weather, scents or sounds carried on a breeze, as Kazuha does. Narratively, Anemo carries things: other elements, voices, seeds, songs, news. A Swirl should visibly carry flame, water, sparks or frost outward. Mondstadters associate the wind with freedom and their god, so a sudden favourable breeze reads as a good omen. Do not have an ordinary Mondstadter recognise Venti as Barbatos.

Avoid portraying Anemo as weather control for any Vision holder, or as able to suffocate people by removing air; canon shows neither. Do not give the Anemo Gnosis back to Venti or place it anywhere except with the Tsaritsa as of 7.1.

13.content:
The Anemo Dragon Sovereign today is Dvalin, who succeeded an earlier, unnamed Anemo dragon who died before the game's events. Dvalin was born from a convergence of elemental energy in the high heavens and drawn to Barbatos's lyre. He became the Dragon of the East of the Four Winds after Vennessa's rebellion.

500 years ago, during the Cataclysm, Dvalin killed the black dragon Durin over Dragonspine but swallowed its poisoned blood. He slept in Decarabian's Tower, and the Abyss Order exploited his pain. The Traveler, Venti, Jean and Diluc freed him in the Prologue, and he is now Mondstadt's ally again.

14.content: Anemoculi are consolidated winds found across Mondstadt. According to The Blessings of The Seven, only allogenes and the Traveler can see them. They are offered at Statues of The Seven, which legend says once had gem eyes that swallows carried off, in exchange for The Seven's blessing. Item text describes the Anemoculus as a substance "that has accumulated intense Anemo energy", offered to help a statue regain power it has lost.

15.content: "The thousand winds" is an old phrase with competing meanings. In Mondstadt it names the personified winds that protect the land; Venti was once a single nameless thread among them. In Enkanomiya belief, "the thousand winds of time" refers to Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, and the Thousand Winds Temple keeps carvings linking the gods of Time and Anemo. Legend says the original Skyward Atlas recorded the names of all the thousand winds. Treat the link between wind and time as unresolved.

16.content: Anemo Slimes form when Anemo scattered through nature coalesces. They puff up and drift down when knocked into the air. Anemo Specters haunt Seirai Island and Watatsumi Island in Inazuma. The Anemo Hypostasis is a boss made of shell pieces around a core; it builds vortices and tornadoes that absorb other elements. Anemo Samachurls are hilichurl shamans who call up small tornadoes and vacuum traps. In gameplay, the elemental lifeforms are immune to Anemo, and Samachurls resist it.

17.content:
Archaeolune Energy (also: Archaeolune, ancient moon energy, ancient moon's power, Blue Kuuvahki, Moonvein Suffusion, Archaeolune Ripples): Archaeolune Energy is an ancient, primordial power found on the Frost Moon, the one intact moon above Nod-Krai. It is closely tied to kuuvahki, the moonlight-power of Nod-Krai, and is considered kuuvahki's primordial form; characters in the story usually call it "ancient moon energy". It fills the moon's core, powers the dragon-built machines on the moon, and can create life. It first appeared in the Moon Gazing quests (Version 6.7).

In game terms it is the basis of exploration on the Frost Moon: absorbing it puts the Traveler into a state called Moonvein Suffusion, which makes the body lighter and jumps higher and lets them fire Archaeolune Ripples. The wiki reports that Columbina simply calls it "Blue Kuuvahki".

Its loading-screen description calls it an ancient power found on the Frost Moon, deeply connected to kuuvahki. Concentrated or stormy surges of it are dangerous to living things other than kuuhenki, the moon spirits.

In universe: Kuuvahki, the power of the Three Moons, is a primordial form of elemental energy that belongs to the Light Realm. Columbina says kuuvahki and the ancient moon's energy are both, in essence, the power of the Light Realm. The wiki describes Archaeolune Energy as the primordial form of kuuvahki that shares the properties of two other primordial energies: phlogiston (programmable matter, an energy source, and a medium for storing and recording information) and the Primordial Sea (the power of creation, including the creation of life).

Dragon-era engineers built facilities on the moon around it. Pioneer Source Structures, said to be constructs of the dragons of Natlantea, store it. Ancient Moon Pearls are spherical energy vessels, pearl power stations feed it through energy pathways to doors and machines, and Archaeolune Energy Barriers guard dragon facilities linked to the moons. A deep base on the moon is powered by a stream of the energy rising from a fissure that leads to the moon's core. Eggie explains that this base was meant to turn the moon into a space-based weapon; Columbina describes it as the work of the returning dragon king Nibelung, who reforged the moon into a weapon whose core energy would become artillery fire aimed at Teyvat. That ruler was defeated by the Heavenly Principles, and Columbina says the site is no longer a threat.

Creation and life. In the Moon Gazing finale, the recorded mark of the researcher Nin-Kiggia explains that the Three Moon Sisters allowed the researchers to borrow "the power of creation from the moon's very origin". When that primordial power of creation was triggered in the sea at the moon's core, a black kuuhenki was born, which is how Eggie came to exist. In an earlier episode, the scientist Maagees used an experimental technique to convert the dying Ungien into a being of pure ancient moon energy, creating Ungie, the first artificially birthed kuuhenki on the moon. Paimon compares this to the dragons' phlogistonization.

Information. Because the energy can store and record information (the phlogiston-like property), the researchers' data was collated into the moon's core. Nin-Kiggia's recording and Columbina explain that the researchers' data merged into this ocean and that, by the will of the moon, they are reborn in forms akin to Eggie, the cycle having possibly repeated more than once. Columbina also says she can infuse her own Light Realm power into transmitted messages to shield them. Do not present the cycle as fully explained: canon leaves its mechanism open.

Dangers: Archaeolune Storms. When the lunar sea beneath Ungien's Circle is disturbed, highly concentrated energy leaks out as an Archaeolune Storm, which Columbina says harms all living beings other than kuuhenki. An occlusion field can temporarily hold the storms back. Blue areas of high concentration are best avoided.

Knotted Moonlight Vines grow where the ancient moon's power has been thrown into turmoil, according to Eggie, and the Moonlight Dash can break them. Gameplay: standing in a storm or disturbance zone fills a bar, after which the player is incapacitated and returned to the last safe zone without HP or Energy loss.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore). Absorbing Archaeolune Energy from a source puts the Traveler in the Moonvein Suffusion state, which raises jump height, grants Archaeolune Ripples, and (per the wiki, flagged for verification) after a certain point in Pioneers (Part 2) also grants Moonlight Dash charges. Sources: Ancient Moon Pearls, Archaeolune Energy Nodes, Archaeolune Energy Surges, Pioneer Source Structures that are not on alert, and Wondrous Black Kuuhenki.

Archaeolune Ripples can be aimed and detonated to damage objects in the blast area and to change the gravity acting on Archaeolune-affinitive materials. Energy Nodes work like quick-travel points and refill Ripple and Dash charges. Moonlight Dash turns the player into a black kuuhenki to dash quickly and ram Knotted Moonlit Vines. The Ripples can also hit Archaeolune Energy Barriers to open a temporary hole, activate Backup Power Generators, and make Archaeolune Energy-Affinitive Materials float or fall. Outside Ungien's Circle, the Frost Moon's turbulent energy makes jumps higher and falls slower, which lowers fall damage, although skill jumps and gliding are unaffected.

Limits: Pearls cannot move once packed into a container, and barriers regenerate shortly after a hole is made. The energy is not one of the seven elements, and canon gives it no Vision or elemental reactions. Pioneer Source Structures can be drained only when not on alert, and then power back up after a short time.

Kuuvahki and Archaeolune Energy are distinct in use: Wondrous Black Kuuhenki draw their power from Archaeolune Energy, not kuuvahki, while ordinary kuuhenki and Moon Wheel wielders work with kuuvahki.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text). Archaeolune Energy is quiet and cold: blue-lit machinery, floating stones, slow falls and a faint sense of lightness. It belongs to the Frost Moon, not to ordinary Teyvat, and outsiders should treat it as unfamiliar and potentially harmful in high concentration.

A character in a scene should not casually wield it unless they are Columbina, a moon-born being, or the Traveler with her grant. Scenes can use it as a clue source: pearls, power stations and terminals hint at a long-lost dragon-era project. Keep its Light Realm kinship with kuuvahki and phlogiston as hints, not a stated rule, and do not give it an element.

Examples: - Columbina gives the Traveler the power to fire Ripples at a dormant generator on the Frost Moon, reactivating a broken energy pathway (Pioneers, Part 1).
- Eggie explains that Knotted Moonlight Vines grow where the ancient moon's power has been disturbed, and that a sea of concentrated energy beneath Ungien's Circle powers the facility (Visitors From the Stars, Part 1).
- Maagees converts Ungien's failing body into pure ancient moon energy, creating the first artificial kuuhenki (Visitors From the Stars, Part 2).
- Nin-Kiggia's recording reveals that the primordial power of creation made Eggie (Project Moongazer, Part 2).

18.content: Moonvein Suffusion is the gameplay state entered by absorbing an object filled with Archaeolune Energy: the body feels lighter and jumps are higher, and the player can fire Archaeolune Ripples that detonate to damage objects and alter their gravity. The wiki notes that Moonlight Dash, which turns the player into a black kuuhenki for fast movement, is also granted after a certain quest step. Pressing the Elemental Burst button exits the state.

19.content: Ancient Moon Pearls are energy vessels for Archaeolune Energy, found on the Frost Moon and in Dunanna Pit. Their loading-screen description calls them wondrous spherical devices that roll, whose true function is to store energy. Pushing a pearl into a power station transfers its energy, which flows along pathways to power machinery; a launcher can throw a pearl (or a standing character) to a distant spot. Pioneer Source Structures, built by the dragons of Natlantea according to the wiki, are fed by the same energy and have modules for edict, stasis, transmission and annihilation.

20.content: An Archaeolune Storm is a surge of highly concentrated ancient moon energy that spreads when the lunar sea at the moon's core is disturbed. Columbina says it harms all living beings other than kuuhenki. Eggie notes that an occlusion field can hold such storms back for a while, and that the facility beneath Ungien's Circle draws its power from the lunar sea.

21.content:
Arkhe (also: Pneuma, Ousia, Pneumousia, Pneuma and Ousia, Pneuma-Ousia Annihilation, Arkhe alignment): Arkhe is a pair of opposing energies native to Fontaine: Pneuma and Ousia. When one meets the other, the two annihilate and release a greater burst of energy. This Pneuma-Ousia Annihilation is what powers most of Fontaine's Clockwork Meka. Arkhe is not one of the seven elements. It is a separate, Fontaine-specific energy, and most Fontainian characters carry one alignment of it.

The two names are often joined as "Pneumousia" in Fontaine's engineering and environment text. A hit of one alignment on something charged with the other disrupts it, so a machine's own power supply can be turned against it.

In universe: In-game tutorials describe Pneuma and Ousia as properties found in the life-forms, earth, air and watery veins of Fontaine. When energies of different properties collide they annihilate and yield greater energy. This is the principle that powers many Clockwork Meka.

Meka power supplies are unstable and settle into a Pneuma-aligned or Ousia-aligned state. An attack of the opposite alignment overloads the supply and disables the machine for a time. Combat-oriented meka keep a backup system for low-end fighting, while utility meka lose their combat functions entirely.

Meka refine the naturally occurring pneumousia around them using components called Repeaters. That is convenient inside Fontaine and a limitation elsewhere. Pneumousia Blocks can stand in as a substitute energy source, but only for brief periods. Fontaine loading-screen text credits Alain Guillotin with inventing artificial blocks more than 400 years ago.

Ancient Logs described on the wiki place Alain and his peers, around 400 to 500 years ago, turning what had been seen as a latent environmental threat into a controlled but unstable power source, the kinetic core. Arkhe in nature is therefore both a hazard and a resource. The Fontaine Research Institute, which Alain founded, still leads meka development today.

Character alignment: Most Fontainian characters, and the Hydro Traveler, have an innate Arkhe alignment, reflected in the shape of their Vision. Pneuma belongs to Neuvillette, Lyney, Freminet, Charlotte and Emilie, and to the Hydro Traveler. Ousia belongs to Navia, Clorinde, Wriothesley, Sigewinne, Lynette, Chevreuse and Escoffier. Furina is listed under both and can alternate between the two.

An aligned character can release a follow-up from one of their combat talents: Pneuma users spawn Spiritbreath Thorns and Ousia users spawn Surging Blades. These do not apply an element and have their own fixed cooldown, separate from the talent's. Alignment is a fact of design and not a personality trait; canon draws no link between temperament and alignment.

Known uses: Disabling Clockwork Meka by striking with the opposite alignment, solving Fontaine puzzles, and stunning Breacher Primuses in their stressed state.

Pneumousia Blocks found in the wild can be picked up and released on the next attack. The underwater tutorial notes that most Fontainian characters can trigger their own alignment underwater without blocks. Enhanced Pneumousia Amplifiers apply an elemental aura to nearby enemies, and an opposite-Arkhe hit disables one for the rest of the fight.

- Prototype Cal. Breguet, the Experimental Field Generator, ends its Gravity Reduction Field after taking three Pneuma-aligned hits (see Arkhium).
- Meka are colour-coded: bright white clockwork is Pneuma, dark blue is Ousia. Stronger meka take more opposite hits to weaken: one for common meks, two for specialist meks, three for boss-class meka.
- Outside Fontaine, meka lean on Pneumousia Blocks because local pneumousia is unavailable.

Limits: Arkhe is not an element and does not react like one.

An Arkhe hit does not apply elemental effects. Annihilation needs two opposite alignments; matching alignments do nothing special.

Canon does not say what Arkhe is at root or where it comes from. Do not tie Pneuma and Ousia to Hydro, the Heavenly Principles or the Prophecy of Fontaine unless a scene is clearly speculation.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Arkhe is a combat and exploration mechanic introduced in Version 4.0. Pneuma and Ousia talents trigger on a fixed Arkhe interval, and some weapons have passives that depend on Arkhe alignment. While diving, a character's attacks default to their own alignment, since they have no access to their combat talents.

Normal, Charged and Plunging attacks carry the energy of a picked-up block. The Genius Invokation TCG also uses a Pneuma-Ousia Annihilation reaction, and Furina's TCG passive "Arkhe: Seats Sacred and Secular" (4.7) is named for her Arkhe.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat Arkhe as a Fontainian thing, a quiet hum of mutual opposition. Pneuma reads as sharp, thorn-like and spirit-like; Ousia reads as heavy, surging and substantial, echoing the in-game thorn and blade effects. Keep it distinct from elemental power: a Fontainian can have a Vision element and an Arkhe alignment at once.

Visitors from outside Fontaine will often not know the terms. A Fontainian engineer might say "pneumousia" casually, while a visitor needs it explained as two opposing energies that cancel into power. Do not assign alignments to non-Fontainians, and do not present Pneuma as good and Ousia as bad.

22.content:
Pneuma is one of the two Arkhe energies. In gameplay it appears as the Spiritbreath Thorn follow-up and as white-clockwork meka. Characters aligned with Pneuma include Neuvillette, Lyney, Freminet, Charlotte, Emilie and the Hydro Traveler, and Furina can use Pneuma as well. A Pneuma meka is weakened by an Ousia hit.

The Chinese name for Pneuma translates roughly as "thorniness", and the English name comes from the Greek word for "breath" or "spirit". This is etymology, not in-game explanation.

23.content:
Ousia is the other Arkhe energy. In gameplay it appears as the Surging Blade follow-up and as dark-blue-clockwork meka. Characters aligned with Ousia include Navia, Clorinde, Wriothesley, Sigewinne, Lynette, Chevreuse and Escoffier, and Furina can use Ousia as well. An Ousia meka is weakened by a Pneuma hit.

The Chinese name for Ousia translates roughly as "wildness", and the English name comes from the Greek word usually rendered "essence" or "substance".

24.content: Pneumousia Blocks are energy blocks found in Fontaine's wilderness, in Pneuma and Ousia varieties. Once picked up, the next Normal, Charged or Plunging attack releases the stored energy, including underwater. Alain Guillotin is credited with inventing artificial blocks over 400 years ago, which he used to power his meka. Blocks also let meka run outside Fontaine, though only briefly.

25.content: When Pneuma and Ousia meet, they annihilate and produce a greater energy. Fontainian engineering harnesses this in controlled form inside kinetic cores, and it can overload an opposite-aligned meka. Fontaine Research Institute researchers found Arkhium's energy potential to be far greater than this reaction's.

26.content:
Arkhium (also: Arkhium crystal, Arkhium ore, Arkhium Kinetic Core, Arkhium Stock, Arkhium Lumenite): Arkhium is a yellow, green and blue crystalline ore that occurs in parts of Fontaine and works as an extremely potent energy source. The Fontaine Research Institute tried to use it to counter gravity so that a "city in the sky" could ride out the prophesied flood. A mechanical malfunction overloaded the Arkhium Kinetic Core, and the explosion destroyed much of the old Institute grounds.

Arkhium is distinct from Arkhe, the Pneuma and Ousia energy pair, though the Institute's researchers compared the two. Its energy potential far surpasses the controlled Pneuma-Ousia Annihilation reactions that power Clockwork Meka.

Properties: Arkhium separates matter, or certain things outside of matter, according to archive text; the separation can apparently be reversed, though there has been little interest in doing so. It is either inert, stable and giving off no energy, or activated, unstable and emitting powerful pulses.

Inert Arkhium can be activated in a catalytic environment, and activated Arkhium can be made inert with a specialised inhibitor. Activated crystals can set off a resonance that activates other crystals in range, risking an explosive chain reaction. After enough activation, a crystal's energy-generating potential runs out and it becomes permanently inert.

Residual Arkhium energy in the environment does not dissipate quickly. Refined ore may give off heat, light or a buzzing sound. Under particular conditions raw ore can fuse naturally. Item text on Arkhium Stock describes it as the raw form that can come together naturally, and the Arkhium Lumenite made from it as emitting an unusual energy and light.

Direct exposure is dangerous. Reported symptoms include nausea, vomiting, subcutaneous bleeding and even coma, and most people need medication or other precautions. The Traveler and Paimon are notably resistant. A memo in the abandoned Meropide production zone mentions Arkhium powder having a "rich distinctive flavor", but the consequences of consuming it are unclear.

Fontaine research institute: The Fontaine Research Institute became interested in Arkhium because its energy potential far exceeded Pneuma-Ousia Annihilation. The goal was to counteract gravity and build a city in the sky so that Fontaine's people could survive the prophesied flood. Another proposed use was a ship lift at Romaritime Harbor. The Arkhium Research Project was led by Edwin Eastinghouse, a senior researcher specialising in Arkhium and gravimeters, with Nacker and Raimondo as collaborators.

Edwin built the Experimental Field Generator, a huge device that creates a Gravity Reduction Field. He and Raimondo developed the Arkhium Kinetic Core, an energy source powered by a large chunk of ore, plus a suppression device to control it. Edwin personally trained Nacker to operate it. At some point a mechanical malfunction overloaded the core and the resulting explosion destroyed much of the Institute grounds. It also created the Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies, large cubes of water suspended in the sky around the Central Laboratory Ruins.

Afterwards nearly all Arkhium crystals nearby shattered into fragments. Because fragments can still be activated by resonance, the Institute used the Experimental Field Generator to gather and restrain them, and placed Survey Anchors to monitor residual radiation. Arkhium mining in the Geode Mine Shaft beneath the Fortress of Meropide was terminated. The Institute relocated to a new site near the old ruins.

Chronicles: In the world quest series Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles, the Traveler helps the Institute. Nacker caused a smaller explosion, which Raimondo suspected was a bid to sell the Arkhium core for a fortune, and his tampering reactivated the prototype generator. The Traveler shut it down and installed inhibitors to stabilise the traces of Arkhium in the ruins. The Traveler was named Honorary Senior Researcher, with Paimon as their assistant.

The Traveler later tracked Nacker to a new benefactor named Concini, and discovered that Edwin was also alive, both men still pursuing Arkhium research. Their plans were foiled, and both were returned to the Institute, fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide.

Locations: Arkhium occurs naturally in parts of Fontaine, such as the Geode Mine Shaft beneath the Fortress of Meropide, which holds an inert vein. The ruined Central Laboratory Ruins, with their floating water cubes, mark where the Institute's core exploded.

The Fortress of Meropide's resources were used to build The Wingalet, a giant flying ship. Edwin speculates that it is powered by Arkhium, and the ship was designed by one of his former assistants. This is not confirmed.

Quest items: A world-quest chain has the Traveler gather seven Mysterious Ore pieces across Fontaine, which combine into Arkhium Stock. Forged at Bravais' Press Works, the stock becomes Arkhium Lumenite, which powers a door mechanism for the hidden objective "Arkhium Forge".

Limits: Arkhium is not a Vision element, and not the same thing as Arkhe.

Canon does not explain its origin or why it is concentrated at particular sites. It is dangerous without protection, and a depleted crystal is permanently dead.

Do not claim that Arkhium powers all of Fontaine's machines; Clockwork Meka run on controlled Pneuma-Ousia Annihilation, not Arkhium. Do not treat the Wingalet's Arkhium power source as established.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present Arkhium as an unstable laboratory hazard, with a dull buzz, warm glow and a sense of restrained danger, and as something researchers handle with detectors, inhibitors and nerves rather than bravado. Researchers might talk about "resonance", "inhibitors" and "radiation levels".

Most Fontainians know of the explosion and the floating water cubes, not the details. Edwin Eastinghouse's attitude to risk is part of the canon account. An ordinary NPC should not give a casual speech on how to activate or weaponise Arkhium.

27.content: The Arkhium Kinetic Core was a concentrated energy source built around a large chunk of Arkhium ore, developed by Edwin Eastinghouse and Raimondo with a suppression device to control it. It fed the Experimental Field Generator. Its overload caused the explosion that destroyed much of the Fontaine Research Institute.

28.content:
The Experimental Field Generator is a huge device created by Edwin Eastinghouse that produces a Gravity Reduction Field. The wiki lists the machine as Prototype Cal. Breguet, a Clockwork Meka. In combat the field greatly raises jump height, and three Pneuma-aligned hits end it.

After the explosion the Institute reused it to gather and restrain shattered Arkhium. During the Chronicles quests Nacker's tampering reactivated it, and the Traveler shut it down and installed inhibitors.

29.content: Large cubes of water suspended in the sky around the Central Laboratory Ruins. They were created by the Arkhium explosion that destroyed the old Institute grounds.

30.content: A mine shaft beneath the Fortress of Meropide that contains a vein of inert Arkhium. Mining there ended after the Institute disaster. A Meropide inmate named Lechlade complains of headaches, palpitations and cold extremities near it, but the doctor dismisses this; it is unconfirmed whether this is exposure.

31.content: Edwin is a former Senior Technician of the Fontaine Research Institute, widely acknowledged as a genius and obsessively committed to research results, including at heavy cost to people. He led the Arkhium Research Project and built the Experimental Field Generator. He was presumed dead after the explosion; the Traveler later found him alive and still continuing Arkhium work, and he was fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide.

32.content:
Art of Khemia (also: The Art of Khemia, Khaenri'ahn alchemy, Khemia): The Art of Khemia is the alchemy of Khaenri'ah. Because Khaenri'ah was an underground nation with little natural fauna, its alchemy centred on creating life, and it is quite different from the alchemy practised in the Seven Nations. Its master was "Gold" Rhinedottir, who made the dragon Durin, the synthetic human Albedo and many monsters. The Art played a major role in the fall of Khaenri'ah in the Cataclysm 500 years ago.

Albedo, Rhinedottir's creation and student, is the main living practitioner shown. Venti and Dainsleif, who were present at Khaenri'ah's fall, are uneasy about Albedo's use of it.

The name comes from the Greek root for "black earth", reflected in the Chinese and Japanese names (Art of Black Earth). Soil and chalk are the central images in Rhinedottir's lessons to Albedo.

In universe: Khemia sits at the far end of alchemy: those who combine the pinnacle of alchemical skill with vast learning can create synthetic life, which Albedo calls the "apex achievement". Canon names only Rhinedottir as having reached that level. Its inner workings and history are not explained in canon.

Rhinedottir's demonstration to the young Albedo (Character Story 3) ties life to earth: the universe is the dark essence of the starry sky, the earth is the accumulated memories of time and lives, and the "chalk" is the one being taught. Albedo learned of the Art from his master's notes and was taught that after "soil" comes "chalk", the spotless soil used to make primordial man. His star-shaped neck mark is left where life force was sealed into his vessel; he compares it to a birthmark and to a pontil mark on blown glass.

Rhinedottir sorted creations into pedigrees that appear to name the "soil" they came from: Alfisol for the riftwolves, Humus for Durin, and Cretaceus (chalk) for Albedo, the last said to be of highest quality. Her creations appear to draw on the power of the Ruler of Life among the Four Shades (now Naberius's function, which Rhinedottir took over), giving them a degree of immortality; some, like the Bakunawa, are further strengthened with Abyssal power.

Albedo uses the Art in Mondstadt in ways he describes in plain terms, such as building a human body for Durin from the flesh of the immortal Bakunawa, blood taken from Durin's Core, and a portion of the embryo material his mother left behind. Alice remarks that little of that raw material remains. Khemia is distinct from ordinary alchemy as a game system (crafting, conversion), which the Alchemy entry covers.

History: The Art of Khemia grew in Khaenri'ah and was the alchemy that sustained the nation. Rhinedottir, an alchemist who served the Eclipse Dynasty in its closing years, became one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. Tempted by the Abyss, she took a share of the Abyssal power Irmin had given the Traveler's Sibling. Her monster armies then invaded Khaenri'ah and the seven nations in the Cataclysm.

Not all of her creations were malicious. Durin and Elynas show an almost childlike delight in the new world and, in their memories, were unaware of or distressed by the harm they caused. Durin claims Rhinedottir sent him from Khaenri'ah to "display his beauty", with other motives left ambiguous, and the riftwolves invaded of their own will. After the Cataclysm she made her breakthrough in the Primordial Human Project and produced Albedo, then left him a last assignment (to find the truth and meaning of the world) after devouring the Heart of Naberius.

Earlier iterations of the project produced failures. Subject Two was an abandoned experiment, apparently left in Durin's stomach, who later escaped on Dragonspine and taught himself from Albedo's stolen research materials. His work with Durin's blood mutated a Whopperflower into Fellflower, which Albedo says can still count as Rhinedottir's creation. The Bakunawa slipped her control and swallowed part of her body, though she survived. Rhinedottir later takes part in recent Snezhnaya events (intervening over the Seals of Life and meeting the Tsaritsa), which show she and her Art are still active as of 7.1.

Known creations: Durin (dragon), Albedo (synthetic human), the riftwolves, Elynas, the Bakunawa, Sebas and the False Horned Steed.

Rhinedottir called only two of her works "miraculous beings": Durin and Albedo. Durin terrorised Mondstadt's skies until Dvalin killed him over Dragonspine; Elynas polluted Fontaine until its armada wounded him fatally; the Bakunawa devoured the Tenochtzitoc tribe in Natlan before Tenoch and Sanhaj's sacrifice broke it apart.

- Unintended: the Golden Wolflord and its Abyss-corroded form (killed by the Traveler and Paimon in Revelations from the Past).
- Related lifeforms, not made directly by Rhinedottir: Breacher Primus (indirect creations of Elynas), melusines, Fellflower (made by Subject Two).
- The Durin who lives in Mondstadt today was created by the witch Andersdotter in the storybook world of Simulanka, modelled on the original; Albedo gave him a synthetic human body via the Art.

Practitioners: Main practitioner: Rhinedottir (Gold). Her creation and student Albedo (Cretaceus) is the active practitioner. Sucrose (bio-alchemy) and Timaeus are Albedo's assistants and students but are not described as practising Khemia itself. Jakob Baker of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo is a possible practitioner: he researched alchemy extensively, with special interest in Khaenri'ahn Khemia and Rhinedottir's work.

Subject Two taught himself from stolen notes and was killed by Albedo after The Shadows Deepen; the wiki records that he had been resurrected before Paralogism and that his current fate is unknown.

Limits and cautions: Do not treat Khemia as ordinary Mondstadt alchemy or as a Vision power. It is not an element. It is slow, material and dangerous: Venti calls its power ancient and unmistakable and says he fears what would happen if someone lost control of it in the city.

Canon does not give a method, so do not invent formulae or "recipes" beyond soil, chalk, embryo material, arrays and the stages above. Albedo's Khemia is not fully trusted by those who lived through Khaenri'ah's fall: Dainsleif and Venti both voice concern.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Khemia as quiet, exact craft, with chalk-drawn or glowing arrays, specimen notes, and a clinical calm. Its practitioners (Albedo especially) speak of creation as study, not conquest. Avoid portraying it as flashy combat magic.

Keep the Cataclysm's shadow: anyone who knows Khaenri'ah's history may react to the word "Khemia" with unease. Ordinary Mondstadters know Albedo as the Chief Alchemist and Kreideprinz, not the lineage of his art.

Do not make Albedo the Art's inventor or Rhinedottir a villain without nuance: Albedo says she did not always have a "penchant for madness", and her creations vary in intent.

33.content:
Rhinedottir, called Gold, is a Khaenri'ahn alchemist, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah and a Hexenzirkel mage ("R"). She is the foremost known master of the Art of Khemia. After the Cataclysm she created Albedo and, after devouring the Heart of Naberius, took over Naberius's function as the Ruler of Life.

Her own entity entry carries her full biography. Skirk knows her name only through her master Surtalogi, another of the Five Sinners.

34.comment: Art of Khemia: Primordial Human Project
34.content:
Rhinedottir's long project to create a human being through alchemy. Subject Two was an earlier failed result; Albedo, classed as Cretaceus, was the success. Albedo says the apex of alchemy is the creation of human life.

The project's discarded product, Subject Two, later wished to live among humans as Albedo does and was killed by Albedo; see The Shadows Deepen and The Hunger of Many.

35.comment: Art of Khemia: Durin's synthetic body
35.content: Albedo made a human form for Durin using the Art of Khemia: Bakunawa flesh from Mare Jivari, blood extracted from Durin's Core, and part of the embryo material left behind by Rhinedottir. Durin then used the body to live in Mondstadt. This Durin was made by Andersdotter in Simulanka and is distinct from the original Durin killed by Dvalin.

36.comment: Art of Khemia: Narzissenkreuz Ordo and Khemia
36.content: The Ordo's leader Jakob Baker left notes on Khaenri'ahn Khemia and the importance of studying Rhinedottir's work. Notes in the Tower of Ipsissimus criticise the Eclipse Dynasty's alchemists for moving the final stage of the Magnum Opus from red to yellow, saying yellow is bait and red is the true goal. Albedo's voice-over puts yellow after red. Treat the dispute as open.

37.content:
Ascension Phase (also: character ascension, weapon ascension, ascending a character): Ascension Phase is a game-mechanics term: the number of times a character or weapon has been ascended. It determines the maximum level the character or weapon can reach; the highest phase, 6, allows level 90. It is not something characters experience in the story.

Each phase must be unlocked by reaching a required Adventure Rank (the player's account progress) and by spending materials. It has existed since version 1.0.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): ascending raises the level cap. Characters need level-up materials, enhancement materials and local specialties; weapons need weapon ascension materials and enhancement materials.

For characters, each Ascension Phase also unlocks new Passive Talents, raises the maximum level of Combat Talents, and unlocks further Character Stories and voice-overs in their profile. This is why a character's deeper backstory is revealed in stages in the game.

The prerequisite is player-side: the Adventure Rank gate belongs to the account, not to the character. Because ascension needs local specialties from specific regions, each character is loosely tied to a region's resources, a gameplay convention rather than a lore statement.

Ascension is listed among the game's systems alongside Talents and Constellations. Its page records only that it came in with 1.0 and has no later change history; nothing about it changed through 7.1 on the wiki.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): do not have characters talk about their own "Ascension Phase" or "level 90". If a scene needs the idea, describe it as growth through training and experience. Do not conflate this mechanic with a mortal ascending to godhood, which is an in-world concept.

Passive Talents may be portrayed as skills a character picks up with experience, but avoid assigning specific phase numbers to story events.

Limits: Applies to playable characters and weapons only; it has no canonical in-world explanation.

The cap of 6 phases and level 90 are the figures given for the mechanic as of 7.1; individual material costs are not recorded here.

38.content:
Azosite (also: Azosite energy, Azosite system, Azosite-powered system, Azosite smelting): Azosite is an ancient form of energy used by the Khaenri'ahns. It was made by extracting pure elemental energy from ley lines and smelting it into solid Energy Blocks, and it powered everything from ordinary ruin machines to large weapons-testing facilities. Over time the Khaenri'ahns found more effective sources, such as Abyssal energy, which gradually replaced it.

Azosite is described as convenient, stable and safe, but, in the view of a Fontainian researcher who studied it, lacking "will." Players first meet it in the Khaenri'ahn ruins beneath Sumeru's desert (Version 3.6).

In universe: The Khaenri'ahns refined elemental energy out of the ley lines and processed it into Energy Blocks. Azosite is not a separate force: notes found in the ruins say it is not fundamentally different from elemental energy and cannot break the rules that elemental energy must follow.

Because it is elemental energy, Azosite shares its properties, including the ability to reverse Abyssal influence. The same notes place the Abyss higher in the order of rules, since it can distort and pollute the elements of the gods. Energy Blocks fuel the backup power systems of Ruin Golems, and a quest item, the Mysterious Energy Block, is described in-game as a refined Azosite block formed by condensing pure elemental energy, usable for large-scale power systems.

One Khaenri'ahn engineering log describes smelting runs pushing the Azosite concentration of a batch past 60%, and forming the resulting energy alloys into a matrix, which was thought enough to meet the energy demands of the large "Mechanical Wardens" (Ruin Golems). The same log admits it compared poorly with a newly found "perpetual" source. The author also frames the work as relying on human ingenuity rather than "dogma from beyond the heavens."

Azosite, as these notes present it, is a processing method rather than a material gathered from the ground: the ley lines hold elemental energy, and smelting extracts and concentrates it. Which elements, in what proportions, or how Energy Blocks differ by element is not stated in canon.

History: The Khaenri'ahns used Azosite to power machines from common Ruin Guards up to sites such as Madinat al-Nuhas.
