The wiki also credits Eitr research with influencing the decision to create the Wildwood Leshy; that link comes from alchemist's notes in the Ruined Hvergelmir.

The Eye of Graeae also notes that Pavlina was a primary researcher whose Prime Ice skill let her build facilities cold enough for research, and that she preserved many Hyperborean finds with Prime Ice at the Tsar's request. This places the Eitr among artifacts kept and studied in secrecy rather than a weapon used openly.

Known uses: Two uses are shown in canon. First, experimentation on living beings: the Snegovik Donskoy was turned into a snow giant by the Eitr (World Quest "A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains", 7.0), and the hidden objective "A Certain Noble's Relics" has the Traveler fight a Snegovik described as Eitr-altered and bound in ice. Second, Ronova's final act (see the 7.1 section below).

Wildlife-like creatures altered this way are described as gaining power surpassing their race's due, not as becoming a different kind of being.

Ronova fusion: In "Black Feathers Scattered at Parting" (Archon Quest, 7.1), after Pierro, Dainsleif and the Traveler defeated her, a mortally wounded Ronova, the Ruler of Death, felt death approach for the first time. She summoned an orb of light, which she described as hidden by Hyperborea in the depths of the Shadow Realm, and fused it to the Nail of Retribution hovering above the Cryo Dragon's remains over the ruins of Hyperborea, east of Snezhnograd. The Nail began to crumble as she disintegrated. She called it her parting gift and spoke of passing the sensation of death on to the world along with the hallowing of the soil.

After the cinematic, huge beams of light rose above the positions of the six Celestial Nails across Teyvat and the World Quest series "The Anomaly" became available in 7.1. The wiki ties the pillars to the fusion; canon does not yet say what they will cause.

Limits: Do not turn the Eitr into a generic power-up or an item anyone can carry. Canon shows it only in Hyperborean and Hvergelmir research and in Ronova's hands, and it is tied to forbidden knowledge and Light Realm power. Its mechanism is unexplained.

It is not a Gnosis, a Vision or an elemental energy source. Do not claim the Tsaritsa, the Fatui or any Harbinger uses it. Do not state what the light pillars will do.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Eitr as something spoken of in hushed, uneasy terms, if at all. Hvergelmir records, old researchers and the Eye of Graeae are natural sources. Ordinary Snezhnayans would not know the name.

Keep the tone clinical and sorrowful when it comes up in connection with Donskoy or other altered Snegovik. Do not let a character who was not present for the 7.1 Archon Quest know what Ronova did.

81.comment: Eitr: Ronova's fusion of the Eitr
81.content:
In "Black Feathers Scattered at Parting" (7.1), Ronova fused the Eitr to Snezhnaya's Celestial Nail as she died. She spoke of making Teyvat feel what dying is like as the Holy Soil spreads. Afterwards, pillars of light loomed over the six Nails.

The Nail hangs above the remains of the Cryo Dragon over Hyperborea's ruins. Ronova's own entry carries her story; this entry only covers the Eitr.

82.content:
Hvergelmir, the old research institute, held the Eitr after the Belyi Tsar found it. Koshchei and Pavlina used it in experiments on living beings. Pavlina, the Snegovik princess, modified Snegovik with it; Donskoy is the best-known subject.

The Eye of Graeae records an old verdict, 530 years old, charging a defendant named Koshchei with using living fae for alchemical experiments. It says no record of an execution exists and that this may be someone who merely shares the name.

83.content: Donskoy was a Snegovik transformed into a snow giant by the Eitr. In the 7.0 World Quest "A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains" a gentle voice says his spirit was damaged during the war and that Pavlina ordered that a human girl not be allowed to meet him; Pavlina's own voice says he needs long, peaceful sleep. His own entry carries the rest.

84.content:
Electro (also: Electro element, element of lightning): Electro is the element of lightning, one of Teyvat's seven elements. Its Archon is Beelzebul, publicly the Raiden Shogun, the God of Eternity who rules Inazuma, the land of thunder. Electro Vision holders conjure sparks, bolts and charged storms, and Electro reacts with every other element but itself. As of 7.1 the Electro Gnosis is no longer with the Archon: it passed through several hands and now belongs to the Tsaritsa.

The people of Inazuma associate Electro with their god, with storms and with the Shogunate. Vajrada Amethyst is the ascension gem of Electro characters, named after the vajra, a thunderbolt weapon of Indra.

In universe: Most people cannot use Electro. Those who can usually hold an Electro Vision. The current Electro Archon, Ei, draws on the Electro Authority of her divine throne in Celestia; she no longer holds the Electro Gnosis.

Electro appears in nature as lightning during a thunderstorm. Lightning can strike a person or the body of water they stand in.

Electro also has everyday uses: Keqing uses hers to stun fish for a meal (her "Survival Hairpin" character story). Ei's Musou Isshin story ties the sword to lightning: it says "the aesthetic of lightning is precisely to capture that which is precious amidst fleeting transience."

Electro and storms are bound together across Inazuma's history. Raiden Makoto and Ei came to power in the Archon War and ruled jointly; after Makoto died in the cataclysm 500 years ago, Ei succeeded her. Seirai Island, where the Thunderbird Kapatcir once raged, still has storms that the Adventurers' Guild finds dangerous to cross (Seirai Stormchasers, 2.1). Thundering Fury's artifact text describes ancient peoples who feared the Thunderbird's power and thanked it for blessings, while the monster itself paid them no heed.

Canon uses the vajra as the element's emblem in item text: the Vajrada Amethyst's full description is a paraphrase of what Ei says in the Chapter II finale, that her body is the noblest in the world and had promised her people an unchanging "eternity". The wiki traces the name to the vajra of Indra, a god of rain and thunder; it is the only gem group named after a weapon rather than a deity.

Origins: Origins, as canon tells them. The elemental Authorities first belonged to the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons of the old world. The Heavenly Principles stole part of that power and tied it to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (revealed in the Fontaine Archon Quest, 4.1); Visions also derive from these Authorities. In the Natlan Archon Quest (5.1), the Lord of the Night reveals that the Heavenly Principles created elemental energy by dividing the raw elemental currents of the Light Realm into seven, using Phlogiston, Teyvat's primordial energy, as a base; the result was easier to control and meant to better counter the Abyss. How an Archon relates to their element, and why a nation takes on its element's character, is still unexplained.

Canon never names an Electro Dragon Sovereign. The wiki's table of known Sovereigns lists Anemo, Geo, Hydro, Pyro and Cryo, and Apep is the Dendro Sovereign, but there is nothing for Electro; treat the old Electro Authority as unattributed. Bathysmal Vishaps are the one dragon-kin tie to Electro that canon describes: The book The Byakuyakoku Collection records that they strayed from "pure" Hydro forms into "impure" Cryo and Electro variants, which is why the next Hydro Sovereign was not born from them.

Archon and nation: Archon: Ei, whose divine name is Beelzebul, the God of Eternity, publicly known as the Raiden Shogun. "Baal", the divine name of her late twin Makoto, and the title Raiden Shogun were long understood to refer to both twins. Nation: Inazuma, ruled by the Inazuma Shogunate.

Ei is the second holder of the title; the first was her twin Makoto, who died in the cataclysm 500 years ago. About 400 years ago Ei built the Shogun, a puppet in her image that governs Inazuma, and placed her own mind in the Plane of Euthymia, sealed inside the sword Musou Isshin. Most Inazumans do not know the Shogun is a puppet or that Makoto existed.

Ei had served as Makoto's kagemusha, or body double, after Makoto ascended through Ei's sacrifice, so most people never learned there were two. Ei and Makoto were identical twins who lived at the start of the Archon War, about 6,000 years ago by the wiki's reckoning. About 2,000 years ago Ei defeated the last gods of the archipelago and, with Makoto, united the islands under the Inazuma Shogunate. Ei met Morax and Barbatos at one of the Seven's reunions in Liyue after the war ended. She keeps the title despite having passed the Electro Gnosis to Yae Miko, which shows that an Archon's seat in Celestia is independent of the Gnosis. Neuvillette's voice-over about the Electro Archon says that by taking the Authority of Electro "the Narukami placed herself on the list of the usurpers", and that he will visit her in a few centuries since she rarely appears.

Chapter II (Inazuma Archon Quest, 2.1) ends with the Traveler and Ei facing the Vision Hunt Decree. Fed by the Fatui-compromised Tri-Commission, the Shogun puppet had enforced the Sakoku Decree and Vision Hunt Decree with Ei's tacit approval. On the steps of Tenshukaku, the Traveler, helped by Yae Miko and drawing on the light of the seized Visions, convinced Ei to rescind the Vision Hunt Decree. In her later story quests she dueled the puppet over a new idea of Eternity, the Sakoku Decree was lifted and she began to take a more active part in ruling Inazuma. See the Raiden Shogun's own entry for the person; this entry covers only her role as the element's Archon.

Gnosis and authority: Ei gave the Electro Gnosis to Yae Miko about 400 years ago, before retreating into the Plane of Euthymia. She remains the Electro Archon without it.

A Gnosis is an Archon's focus resonating directly with Celestia. Ei had no use for hers, and none of her techniques could modify it. The Gnosis's later route: Yae Miko traded it to Scaramouche (the Wanderer) in exchange for the Traveler's safety; Nahida took it from him in Sumeru (Archon Quest Chapter III, 3.x) and later gave it to Dottore in exchange for his agreeing to erase his segments. By the time of Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana it was one of six Gnoses in the Fatui's hands. Scaramouche could manipulate lightning and weather while connected to it, but only after heavy modification with Sumeru Akademiya's help; Ei's own attempts to link him to it had failed. Nahida, by contrast, could not use it in battle against Dottore, though she did use it to open Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's realm of consciousness. According to Dottore, a Gnosis's use by anyone but its Archon may normally be restricted.

Besides her own Cryo Gnosis, the Tsaritsa gained the Anemo and Geo Gnoses first, then the Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses; the Pyro Gnosis never reached her. In the teaser "A Winter Night's Lazzo", after Capitano asks about Scaramouche and the Electro Gnosis, Dottore replies that "Divine Knowledge cannot be rationally comprehended."

Gnosis status: In the 7.1 Archon Quest "A Rekviem for the Underworld", Anastasya (the Tsaritsa) used her Cryo mastery together with the six Gnoses, the Electro Gnosis among them, to slow time within a room of her palace and stall Rhinedottir. As of 7.1 the Electro Gnosis remains in her possession; Ei does not have it.

Vision hunt note: For about a year before the Traveler reached Inazuma, no new Electro Visions appeared. Ei was surprised to hear of it, so the cause remains unknown.

Sumeru Akademiya scholars concluded that the Archons' wills govern Vision distribution, and Kazuha guessed it reflected the Shogun's doubts. Electro Visions were also among those confiscated. The Vision of Kazuha's friend, an Electro holder killed during the Vision Hunt Decree, became Masterless, and Kazuha briefly awakened it. A Masterless Vision loses its element and power when its holder dies, though one may resonate with a new person. Tartaglia, a Harbinger, has an Electro Delusion that Pierro pinned on him when he became one; as a playable character he uses only Hydro. During the Vision Hunt Decree the Shogunate laid the confiscated Visions into the Statue of the Omnipresent God.

Elemental beings: Electro elemental lifeforms such as Electro Slimes, Electro Specters and the Electro Hypostasis, and the Thunder Manifestation of Amakumo Peak.

Electro Slimes form from Electro coalescing in nature. Electro Specters are born of highly concentrated Electro and float. The Electro Hypostasis (code name Aleph) is a high-purity Electro entity at Cape Oath in Mondstadt. The Electro Regisvine of Sumeru's Lokapala Jungle is a giant plant that releases charge stored in the ley lines.

- Slimes: the Archive says their jumps reflect the electric potential difference in the ground, a behaviour that can be used to avoid danger in Electro-rich areas.
- Hypostases are the highest forms of elemental structures, formed at places bursting with elemental energy or at a clogged ley line.
- Thunder Manifestation (Amakumo Peak, Seirai Island, introduced 2.1): the Archive calls it an Electro life form that weaves thunder and lightning as a song to its resentment. It resembles an Oceanid but has none of her intelligence or memories, being driven by primal fury. Such beings are said to descend only where great lingering resentment remains, and as long as the grudges of the land do not fade, the thunder persists. Its origin is the remnant of the Thunderbird Kapatcir's power, kept in check at the Asase Shrine until Hibiki released it.
- Electro Specters are also found in Inazuma and Enkanomiya. One Archive entry jokes about a researcher who believed they must be Hypostases and was later investigated for academic corruption.
- The Regisvine entry says Electro awakens plants and boosts soil fertility, and that Kshahrewar researchers once proposed a circuit matrix around one to carry electricity to the city; Spantamad scholars opposed this and sacrificed ten Shroomboars to make their point.

Gods of lightning: Makoto and Ei are the gods of Electro in canon. Kapatcir was a monster rather than a god, though the Thunderbird's tribe worshipped it and read its actions as revelations.

Known uses: Lightning strikes, sparks that chain between foes, charged fields, and fast bursts of speed. Electro also sets off reactions with Pyro, Hydro, Cryo, Anemo, Geo and Dendro.

Electro also drives devices in Inazuma: Lightning Strike Probes respond to anyone affected by Electro.

- Electro Crystals and lanterns shock whoever touches them.
- Ei's sword stroke Musou no Hitotachi split Musoujin Gorge; the Follow the Wind cutscene says it is seen only during "divine punishment."
- The Musou Isshin story recalls the blade's first battle amid "wild winds and blazing thunder".
- The Traveler resonates with Electro at an Inazuma Statue of The Seven, and fights with lightning in the cinematics of Amidst Stormy Judgment and The Omnipresent God.
- Razor's Vision story notes that, though he had obtained a Vision, he was still unable to manipulate Electro energy with finesse: a Vision grants power but not instant skill.

- Visions are personal: Fischl, Keqing and Beidou also hold Electro Visions, and Kazuha briefly used a Masterless Electro Vision from his late friend.
- Kapatcir's lightning razed Tsurumi Island's mountain in her grief over a murdered boy; a curse she left on the land would only lift if she heard his song again (Thundering Fury artifact lore).

Limits: Electro does not react with itself. It has no effect of its own beyond enabling reactions.

Electro on its own does not change the target; it only enables reactions. A Vision fixes its holder to one element: Kazuha's brief Electro use came from a second Vision.

Gameplay: Electro Slimes and Specters are immune to Electro; Hypostases are too. Masterless Visions lose their element and power when their holder dies.

Interactions: Overloaded (with Pyro) explodes. Superconduct (with Cryo) damages and weakens Physical resistance. Electro-Charged (with Hydro) damages over time. Swirl spreads Electro. Crystallize with Geo forms a shield-granting shard. Quicken with Dendro enables Aggravate and Spread.

- Overloaded causes an explosion that deals AoE Pyro damage with high knockback.
- Electro-Charged deals Electro damage and high Poise damage over time to nearby targets that are Wet.
- Superconduct deals AoE Cryo damage and reduces nearby enemies' Physical RES by 40%.
- Swirl (Anemo) deals AoE Electro damage and spreads the Electro status to nearby enemies.
- Crystallize (Geo) creates an Electro shard; picking it up grants an Electro shield.
- Quicken (Dendro) applies a Quicken aura; Electro on it triggers Aggravate and Dendro triggers Spread.
- Hyperbloom (Electro, Hydro, Dendro) turns a Dendro Core from Bloom into a homing Sprawling Shot.

Lunar-Charged (wiki lists 5.8): in a party with a Moonsign character, Electro-Charged becomes a thundercloud that bursts with lightning on enemies affected by both Electro and Hydro. Stellar-Conduct (6.7, Luna VIII): pairing Cryo with Electro creates a Starlight Prism that raises Cryo and Electro DMG Bonus and cuts Physical RES nearby. Both have their own entries.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Electro is a damage type and the element of characters such as Fischl, Keqing, Raiden Shogun, Yae Miko, Cyno, Flins and Ineffa. Its ascension gems are Vajrada Amethyst.

Other Electro characters include Lisa, Beidou, Razor, Kujou Sara, Kuki Shinobu, Dori, Clorinde, Sethos, Varesa, Iansan, Ororon and Alyosha. Elemental Resonance "High Voltage" (two or more Electro characters): affected by Hydro for 40% less time; Superconduct, Overloaded, Electro-Charged, Lunar-Charged, Quicken, Aggravate or Hyperbloom have a 100% chance to generate an Electro Elemental Particle (5s cooldown). Electroculi (181 can be found in the overworld) raise the Statues of The Seven in Inazuma, and Electro Sigils, which come from chests, one-time domains and the Statues, raise the Sacred Sakura's Favor and upgrade Electrograna. The 4-piece Thundering Fury artifact set boosts Electro reaction damage; Thundersoother resists Electro damage. Exploration includes Electro Crystals, Electro Current Puzzles, Electro Rock Piles and Electro lanterns that apply Electro to the active character. The Traveler can resonate with Electro only if they unlock an Inazuma Statue of The Seven, and the game never forces this.

Gameplay recent: Gameplay, recent additions: Lunar-Charged (wiki lists 5.8), tied to Moonsign and the Nod-Krai Electro characters Ineffa (5.8) and Flins (6.0), is the Electro entry in the Lunar reactions; Stellar-Conduct (6.7, Luna VIII) is an Electro-Cryo Stellar Glimmer reaction. Alyosha (7.0) is a 4-star Electro Polearm character. The Version 7.0 and 7.1 notes give Mitya's elemental type icon as the Electro Stellar Linchpin.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Electro as light, sound and sudden force: a bright flash, a crack and rumble, hair lifting from static, the metallic smell of a storm. Violet is the usual colour cue, matching the Vajrada Amethyst and the Thunderbird's purple thunder; the wiki notes Electro can occasionally be seen as yellow. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can arc sparks, not summon a storm.

Narratively, Electro is the element of sudden change and of reactions: it sets things off. It also carries the Inazuma themes of eternity versus fleeting moments: her Musou Isshin story says the aesthetic of lightning is to capture something precious amid fleeting transience. Scenes in Inazuma can plausibly include storms, lightning-struck trees and thunder rolling in over the sea. Most Inazumans do not know that the Shogun is a puppet, that Makoto existed, or that Ei is a second Archon; the Raiden Shogun is the face of the god.

Avoid portraying Electro as an unlimited battery: canon shows Scaramouche needed heavy modification to channel the Electro Gnosis, and Nahida could not use it in battle. Do not give the Electro Gnosis back to Ei or leave it with Dottore; as of 7.1 it is with the Tsaritsa. Do not describe any named Electro Dragon Sovereign.

85.content:
The Electro Archon is the God of Eternity among the Seven and ruler of Inazuma. There have been two holders: Raiden Makoto, who died in the cataclysm 500 years ago, and her twin sister Ei, who succeeded her and has held the Electro Authority since. The Shogun puppet, built in the twins' image, is now the public face of the Archon. Titles such as "Raiden Shogun", "Narukami" and "Electro Archon" in older texts may refer to any of the three or to the general idea of Inazuma's god.

Makoto's own ideal was also eternity, but understood as time extended into infinity with dreams lighting each moment within it; Ei later remarked that her sister's understanding was far deeper than hers. Ei's own version was a stillness that never changes; after the story quest Radiant Sakura she no longer pursues eternity as stasis. See the Raiden Shogun's entry for her story.

86.content: The Electro Gnosis was Ei's, entrusted to Yae Miko about 400 years ago, then traded to Scaramouche for the Traveler's safety, taken by Nahida in Sumeru, handed to Dottore, and now belongs to the Tsaritsa along with five other Gnoses (as of 7.1). No one outside the Archon can easily use it: Scaramouche could, but only with heavy modification, and Nahida could not use it in battle.

87.content:
Kapatcir ("Great Eagle of the Storm") was a monster, a huge violet bird of prey in storm and thunder, worshipped as a guardian by the tribe of Tsurumi Island. The boy Ruu named her; when the tribe sacrificed him, she destroyed the mountain in grief and rage, killing the tribe, and left a curse on the land. Years later Ei hunted her down as "an obstacle to progress" and sealed the remnants of her power at the Asase Shrine on Seirai Island. A thousand years on, Hibiki's release of that seal let the Thunder Manifestation loose.

The Seirai Stormchasers world quest series and the Thundering Fury artifact lore (including the Thunder Summoner's Crown) tell her story. Her relationship to the Thunder Manifestation is a "remnant of power", not a rebirth: the Archive describes the Manifestation as a being of regret with no memories of its own.

88.content: Electro Visions are the external apparatuses by which people wield lightning. No new Electro Visions appeared for about a year before the Traveler reached Inazuma, and the reason is unknown. Many were taken by the Vision Hunt Decree and returned once it was rescinded. Known Electro Vision holders include Keqing, Fischl, Beidou, Razor, Kazuha's late friend and, 500 years ago, Fukami.

89.content: Electro Slimes form from Electro coalescing in nature and carry stored charge. Electro Specters, born of dense Electro, float, and grow larger and gain stronger attacks after taking heavy blows. The Electro Hypostasis (Aleph) is a boss of shell pieces and a core; the Electro Regisvine is a giant plant that releases ley line charge. The Thunder Manifestation on Amakumo Peak is a being of lingering regret. In gameplay, all these are immune to Electro damage.

90.content: Electroculi are consolidated Electro energy scattered across Inazuma. Item text describes them as a substance that "has accumulated intense Electro energy", offered at a Statue of The Seven to help it regain lost power. The wiki counts 181 in the overworld.

91.content:
Electro-Charged (also: Electro-Charged reaction, Electrocharged, Electro Charged): Electro-Charged is what happens when Electro and Hydro meet on a target, in either order. The target keeps both Hydro and Electro on it and takes Electro damage once a second, and the shock jumps to another wet enemy nearby. It continues until one of the two elements is used up.

The wiki lists it as a Transformative reaction. A third element can still react with the target, which makes Electro-Charged a good opener for follow-up reactions.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. Electro-Charged appears in tutorials and combat, not in character dialogue in the sources read. Treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from.

The in-game tutorial puts it plainly: Electro meeting Hydro causes Electro-Charged, which keeps dealing Electro damage until it wears off and electrifies nearby Wet opponents.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Electro-Charged leaves the target with a Hydro aura and an Electro aura at the same time. It deals Electro damage once per second; each tick reduces both auras by 0.4 gauge units, and it ends when either aura is gone. Normal aura decay still applies.

- It cannot damage off-field characters. Switching away pauses the ticks; if the character returns while still affected by Electro and Hydro, the ticks resume.
- Each time it deals damage it also hits one other nearby Wet opponent, about 5 m away (the wiki marks that range as unverified), accounting for that opponent's Electro RES. The Wet aura is not consumed by the arc, and an Electro aura is not applied to the arc target.
- If Electro-Charged ends because an aura expires, one more tick can occur if more than 0.5 seconds have passed since the last.

- Third element: because both auras exist together, other reactions can follow, such as Overloaded and Vaporize, Superconduct and Frozen, or an Electro and a Hydro Swirl. The Electro reaction is resolved first, and the Hydro reaction happens only if some of the triggering element is left after the Electro aura is used up.
- The coexisting elements also allow effects such as Thundersoother to be applied without giving up reactions.
- Environment: if an Electro attack hits a body of water, the water becomes Electro-Charged for a short time and any target walking into it takes Electro damage. Pyro or Cryo applied to that water can cause Overloaded or Superconduct.
- Damage is Transformative: it comes from the triggering character's level and Elemental Mastery and is resisted by the target's Electro RES.

Some talents grant immunity to Electro-Charged, and others, constellations and artifact sets raise its damage; the wiki holds those in category tables, which this entry does not copy. The Lunar-Charged page adds that Lunar-Charged shares all other properties of Electro-Charged, including damaging the ward of the Fatui Skirmisher - Hydrogunner Legionnaire at an increased rate.

Lunar charged: Lunar-Charged (own entry) is the Moonsign form of Electro meeting Hydro. It needs a party member with a qualifying Moonsign Benediction passive. According to the wiki, it summons a thundercloud that strikes every Wet, Electro-affected opponent in range every 2 seconds, and a target not struck in the last 2 seconds is hit at once when the second aura lands. Each strike consumes 0.4 gauge units of both auras. The cloud lasts 6 seconds, is reset by another trigger, and only one can exist at a time.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Electro-Charged as lightning crawling over wet surfaces: blue-white arcs skittering across a soaked body, a crackle in the air, hair and cloth standing up. The shock should leap between soaked enemies and puddles.

Water is the setting that matters. A stream, puddle or rain-soaked courtyard turns every Electro spark into a hazard, and an Electro user fighting there should take care of nearby allies. Do not have characters state tick rates or gauge units.

Examples: A Hydro slime drenches a group of enemies, then a bolt of lightning strikes one of them. The charge crackles along its wet body and jumps to another soaked enemy a few steps away, repeating until the water or the lightning fades.

An Electro user wading through a stream is plausibly dangerous for anyone else in the water, matching the wiki's note about Electro-Charged water.

Limits: It needs Electro and Hydro together: Anemo, Geo, Pyro, Cryo and Dendro do not cause it. Do not describe it as an instant burst; its identity is the sustained shock. Do not have it hit off-field targets, or spread to dry ones, as the wiki shows it arcs only to Wet opponents.

Do not move Lunar-Charged earlier than Version 5.8. Do not claim all characters or enemies take it; some talents grant immunity to it.

92.content: When an Electro attack hits a body of water, the water becomes Electro-Charged briefly, and anyone who walks into it takes Electro damage. Applying Pyro or Cryo to such water can cause Overloaded or Superconduct.

93.content: A thundercloud is the effect created by Lunar-Charged. It tries to position itself between active targets and the triggering party, lasts 6 seconds, and strikes Wet, Electro-affected opponents within range every 2 seconds. Only one can exist at a time.

94.content:
Elemental Burst (also: Ultimate, character ultimate): The Elemental Burst, or Burst, is a Talent that needs Energy and is usually stronger than the Elemental Skill. Fans call it the ultimate, or "Q" after its default PC key. Every character has one unlocked from the start. This is a gameplay mechanic; the narrative equivalent is a character unleashing their strongest technique.

Casting grants a character a few seconds of invincibility frames (the exact time varies per character), during which the HP bar is locked and no damage from enemies or debuffs is taken.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): a Burst can be used when (1) it is off cooldown and (2) the character holds at least the Burst's Energy Cost. Energy beyond the cost is ignored. Using it spends all Energy and starts a short cooldown, though Energy can still be gathered during the cooldown.

- Readiness: the HUD icon glows with an audio cue; off-field characters show a ready icon beside their portrait, and co-op players show a marker beside their names.
- Typical costs and cooldowns: 40 Energy with a 12 s cooldown; 50 with 13.5 s; 60 with 15 s; 70 with 18 s; 80 with 20 s; 90 with 18 s or 22 s.
- Exceptions: Hour of Burning Skies and Havoc: Ruin do not use Energy. The first spends Fighting Spirit (100-200) gathered from the party's Normal Attacks and Nightsoul point use in combat. The second uses Skirk's Serpent's Subtlety points (50-100) and has a 15 s cooldown.

- Increasing Burst damage can come from certain Talents, constellations, weapons and artifacts, each listed on the wiki by category; constellations can also raise a Burst's talent level.
- Barbara is the only 4-star character with a Burst animation like those of 5-star characters, and hers neither buffs nor damages.
- The Traveler, Varesa, Skirk, Flins and the Wonderland Manekin are the 5-star playable characters whose Bursts lack the cut-in animation.
- Kinich is the only character whose Burst-linked voice-overs keep playing while he is off-field.

- Tartaglia, Varesa, Skirk and Flins have two distinct Bursts, with separate animations, voice-overs, Energy timing, cooldown timing and targeting. The special versions for Varesa, Skirk and Flins have separate costs and no cut-in; Varesa's and Flins's special versions also have their own cooldown (the wiki flags some of these timing details as needing verification).
- The Wanderer changes his Burst voice-overs depending on whether he is in the Windfavored State, though the Burst itself is unchanged.
- Other Bursts behave differently depending on conditions (for example Albedo, Hu Tao and Yae Miko), but these do not count as two separate Bursts.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present a Burst as a character's signature, high-effort moment, a surge of power they can only call on after the fight has built momentum. Avoid quoting Energy costs or cooldowns in character. Match the character's element and weapon in the description.

Narratively, the brief invincibility frames can read as the character being untouchable in the instant they unleash it. Use the character's own technique names where canon provides them, and keep the Burst proportionate to the character's established power.

Limits: The Energy meter, key binding and cooldown are interface concepts, not things characters mention.

Figures are those listed on the wiki as of 7.1.

95.comment: Elemental Burst: Hour of Burning Skies
95.content: Hour of Burning Skies and Havoc: Ruin are the only Elemental Bursts that do not use Energy. Hour of Burning Skies uses Fighting Spirit gathered from the party's Normal Attacks and Nightsoul point consumption; Havoc: Ruin uses Skirk's Serpent's Subtlety points. Both have minimum and maximum costs rather than a fixed one.

96.content:
Elemental Mastery: Elemental Mastery is an attribute that enhances elemental reactions. The higher it is, the stronger the reactions a character triggers. It is a gameplay stat with no direct in-world number.

Most playable characters start at 0. The exceptions are Lauma and Nefer, who begin at 200 and 100 respectively. It has existed since version 1.0.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): on triggering a reaction, Elemental Mastery boosts it. Overloaded, Superconduct, Electro-Charged, Burning, Shattered, Swirl, Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon, Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom, Lunar-Crystallize and Stellar-Conduct deal more damage. Melt and Vaporize multiply the triggering attack. Aggravate and Spread add bonus base damage to the triggering attack. Crystallize shields absorb more damage.

Bonus is computed as a percentage that grows with diminishing returns: the formulas are 2.78 x EM / (EM + 1400) for Vaporize and Melt, 16 x EM / (EM + 2000) for the transformative reactions listed above, 5 x EM / (EM + 1200) for Aggravate and Spread, 6 x EM / (EM + 2000) for the Lunar reactions and Stellar-Conduct, and 4.44 x EM / (EM + 1400) for Crystallize shields. The bonus is added to the reaction bonus in a multiplier of 1 + EM bonus + reaction bonus. Every extra point of mastery gives less than the last.

- Enemies have 0 Elemental Mastery by default, and it is fixed and does not rise with level. Exceptions: Liam at 650 and Rilai (an Iktomisaurus Warrior: Cryocrystal Cannon) at 800.
- Increasing it: Talents, constellations, artifacts and weapons (as a secondary attribute or as part of a passive effect). Some effects raise the whole party's mastery. Certain characters' ascension stats are Elemental Mastery.
- The Dendro Elemental Resonance Sprawling Greenery gives 50 Elemental Mastery and temporary party bonuses after Dendro reactions.
- The Moonsign team bonus (Ascendant Gleam) lets non-Moonsign characters add Lunar reaction damage; for Anemo or Dendro characters this scales with Elemental Mastery at 2.25% per 100, up to the 36% cap, reached at 1,600 Elemental Mastery.

Percentages, thresholds and reaction lists are those on the wiki as of 7.1; Lunar and Stellar reactions are recent additions (6.x and 7.x). Several formulas were reverse-engineered by the community (the wiki cites player testing), so treat exact decimals as community-derived rather than officially published.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): a character with a lot of mastery is deft at combining elements and can make reactions blossom larger; show it through precision, timing and a feel for how elements push on each other rather than numbers. Characters tied to reactions in the story, such as Sucrose and Alhaitham, suit this portrayal, but their stat values are not canon facts.

Do not state EM values in dialogue. A lack of mastery should not imply a character is unskilled or foolish; many strong fighters rely on raw force.

Limits: No canon defines the stat outside the game's interface and tutorial text.

The attribute does not change Vision type or the elements a person can use.

97.content: Elemental Mastery bonus for reactions: 2.78 x EM/(EM+1400) for Vaporize and Melt; 16 x EM/(EM+2000) for transformative reactions; 5 x EM/(EM+1200) for Aggravate and Spread; 6 x EM/(EM+2000) for Lunar reactions and Stellar-Conduct; 4.44 x EM/(EM+1400) for Crystallize shields. These are community-derived formulas with diminishing returns.

98.content:
Elemental Reaction (also: Elemental Reactions, elemental aura, Transformative Reaction, Amplifying Reaction, Additive Reaction): An Elemental Reaction happens when an element is applied to a target that already carries a different element. Attacks, Visions and elemental creatures leave an "aura" of their element on a target, and a second element meeting it triggers an effect such as Vaporize, Melt, Overloaded, Swirl, Bloom or Crystallize. It is chiefly a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from, not as a named in-world law.

Reactions fall into groups by how they work: Transformative reactions deal their own damage, Amplifying reactions multiply the hit that triggered them, and Additive reactions add to it. Two newer families sit on top of these: Lunar reactions (from the Hydro-related reactions) and Stellar Glimmer reactions (from the Cryo-related ones).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): when an element is applied to an enemy, player or object it leaves an aura that fades over time. Applying a second, different element triggers a reaction, which consumes some or all of the first aura. Many attack sources have an internal cooldown, so they cannot reapply their element, or trigger a reaction, on every hit.

The base reactions by element pair, as listed on the wiki's overview table:
- Pyro with Hydro: Vaporize. Pyro with Electro: Overloaded. Pyro with Cryo: Melt. Pyro with Dendro: Burning.
- Hydro with Electro: Electro-Charged. Hydro with Cryo: Frozen (a frozen target hit by Geo or a blunt Physical attack Shatters). Hydro with Dendro: Bloom.
- Electro with Cryo: Superconduct. Electro with Dendro: Quicken.
- Anemo with Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo: Swirl. Geo with Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo: Crystallize.
- Bloom can follow with Pyro as Burgeon or with Electro as Hyperbloom; Quicken can follow with Dendro as Spread or with Electro as Aggravate.
- Dendro with Cryo, and Dendro with Anemo or Geo, do not react. Geo cannot be the first element on a target, so it only ever reacts as the second.

Transformative reactions are Overloaded, Shattered, Electro-Charged, Superconduct, Swirl, Burning, Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon. Each deals its own damage, based on the reaction type and the level of the character who triggered it, scaled by that character's Elemental Mastery; it cannot CRIT and ignores the target's DEF but is affected by Resistance.

Amplifying reactions are Vaporize and Melt. They deal no damage themselves; they multiply the triggering attack by 2x or 1.5x depending on which element came second, and Elemental Mastery boosts the multiplier further. The wiki's table: Hydro onto Pyro and Pyro onto Cryo give 2x; Pyro onto Hydro and Cryo onto Pyro give 1.5x. The 1.5x versions consume less of the first element and often leave the aura in place.

Additive reactions (Spread and Aggravate; an unofficial grouping name, which the game calls "Catalyze Reactions" in Miliastra Wonderland) add a flat bonus to the base damage of the triggering hit rather than multiplying it, and Spread's bonus is slightly higher than Aggravate's.

A reaction's strength is taken from the character who triggers it; the stats of whoever left the first aura do not count. Some Elemental Resonances react to reactions: High Voltage (two Electro characters) can generate Electro particles on several reactions, and Sprawling Greenery (two Dendro characters) grants Elemental Mastery after Dendro reactions.

Persistent auras are a special case. Players cannot apply a lasting Anemo or Geo status, so Swirl against an Anemo aura is practically limited to the Anemo Hypostasis, and certain enemies' lasting Geo status cannot be reacted with (the wiki's note adds that players cannot apply a persistent Geo status without Planet Befall).

The wiki cites the Behind the Scenes video "To Snezhnaya and the Future" for the statement that the reaction system was designed long before combat strategy and numerical planning, as modular, intuitive rules to support interaction. Further depth, such as gauge units and decay, belongs to the wiki's "Elemental Gauge Theory" page, which I identified but did not summarise here.

Lunar reactions: Lunar reactions are a subset of reactions. To trigger one, the party must include a character with a Moonsign Benediction passive talent that converts specific Hydro-related reactions. There are three: Lunar-Charged (Electro with Hydro), Lunar-Bloom (Dendro with Hydro) and Lunar-Crystallize (Geo with Hydro). Unlike their base versions, Lunar reactions can CRIT.

Lunar damage can be dealt directly by a character's talent, or (for all but Lunar-Bloom) as a separate instance that draws on the stats of every contributing character. It ignores DMG Bonus and the target's DEF but is affected by Resistance, and its base damage is boosted by Moonsign Benediction passives and by Elemental Mastery. The wiki records Lunar-Charged and the family itself as introduced in Version 5.8, Lunar-Bloom in Luna I and Lunar-Crystallize in Luna IV.

Each has its own signature effect on the wiki's description. Lunar-Charged summons a thundercloud that strikes wet and Electro-affected enemies every 2 seconds and lasts 6 seconds, only one existing at a time. Lunar-Bloom gives the player Verdant Dew, up to 3, which persists across teleports and sessions. Lunar-Crystallize creates three Moondrifts, which every third reaction resonate into a tracking Geo projectile (Moondrift Harmony). Moonsign itself has its own entry.

Stellar glimmer reactions: Stellar Glimmer reactions are a subset of reactions, triggered when a party includes a character with a passive talent that converts specific Cryo-related reactions. There are two: Stellar-Conduct (Cryo with Electro) and Stellar Swirl (Anemo with Cryo). They also interrupt a specific attack of Snowland Fae and Aberrant Chimeric Monsters.

Stellar Glimmer damage can be dealt directly by a talent or, for Stellar Swirl, as a separate instance using the stats of all contributing characters. It ignores DMG Bonus and DEF, is affected by Resistance, and is boosted by Stellar Jubilee passives and Elemental Mastery. Those passives belong to Snezhnaya characters with Stellar Linchpins and to the Cryo Traveler. The wiki records the family and Stellar-Conduct as introduced in Version Luna VIII (6.7, with Sandrone) and Stellar Swirl in 7.0.

Stellar-Conduct leaves a Starlight Prism for 7 seconds that sustains a Polestar Field boosting Cryo and Electro damage and lowering Physical RES, and which also affects the Kresnik Energy mechanic in the Snezhnayan open world. Stellar Swirl deals Anemo damage and creates a Stellar Vortex that bursts with Cryo area damage, grows stronger once Stellar Swirl has been triggered three times, and raises the player's next jump. The wiki's lore note says Saarelainen introduced Stellar Glimmer reactions to ancient Snezhnaya, citing the Version 7.0 Special Program.

In universe: Canon discussion of reactions is thin: most of the system is delivered as tutorial text and combat feedback. The pages read offer one clear in-world statement, that Stellar Glimmer reactions were brought to ancient Snezhnaya by Saarelainen. Stellar Linchpin users are described in quest material as having power that appears to come from beyond Teyvat, and the Snezhnayan reactions are enabled by their Stellar Jubilee passives.

The Stellar Linchpin page, citing the quests "Should We Meet Again" and "Mistilteinn", says the Fatui link Linchpins to the deceased Third Descender and plan to use their energy in Project Mistilteinn against the Heavenly Principles. I did not read those quests directly. The wiki identifies the Third Descender as Saarelainen, the same figure credited with bringing Stellar Glimmer reactions to ancient Snezhnaya; exactly how the reactions relate to the Linchpins' otherworldly power is not spelled out.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): describe reactions as visible, sensible results of two elements colliding. Fire on water becomes a burst of steam, fire on ice a fast melt, lightning in water a crackling spread, wind carrying flame, frost or sparks outward, stone crystallising around an element. Keep the effects local to the people involved.

Characters can notice that certain elements go well together without a formal "aura" theory; do not have ordinary characters speak in gauge units, internal cooldowns or multipliers. Treat Lunar and Stellar Glimmer effects as phenomena tied to Moonsign or Snezhnayan Linchpin users, not something a Vision holder does unaided. Hot-and-cold combinations, like Melt, are a natural fit for dramatic scenes.

Limits: Do not treat the tables above as cosmic law. Dendro does not react with Cryo, Anemo or Geo, and Physical damage reacts only as the Shatter follow-up to Frozen. Do not credit a reaction to the wrong trigger: a reaction counts for the character that triggers it, not the one who left the first aura.

Do not claim the in-world cause of reactions, who discovered them, or that a god designed them; canon does not say, apart from the Saarelainen note. Do not move Lunar or Stellar Glimmer reactions earlier than the versions that introduced them (5.8 for Lunar-Charged, 6.7 for Stellar-Conduct and 7.0 for Stellar Swirl, as the wiki records them).

99.content: Transformative reactions deal their own instance of damage, separate from the hit that caused them: Overloaded, Shattered, Electro-Charged, Superconduct, Swirl, Burning, Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon. Their damage depends on reaction type, the triggering character's level and Elemental Mastery; it cannot CRIT.

100.content: Vaporize and Melt multiply the damage of the attack that triggers them. The stronger "forward" case is 2x (Hydro onto Pyro, Pyro onto Cryo), the weaker "reverse" 1.5x (Pyro onto Hydro, Cryo onto Pyro), and the weaker case tends to leave more of the first element in place.

101.content: Spread and Aggravate, the follow-ups to Quicken, add a flat bonus to the base damage of the triggering hit. The name "Additive Reactions" is unofficial; the game's Miliastra Wonderland mode calls them "Catalyze Reactions".

102.content: An aura is the lasting mark of an element on a target. It decays over time, and triggering a reaction shortens or removes it by an amount that depends on the reaction and the strength of the second element.

103.content:
Elemental Resonance (also: Team Bonus, party resonance): Elemental Resonance is a game bonus granted when a full party contains certain element combinations. Two or more characters of the same element among the first four party slots trigger that element's resonance. Four different elements trigger Protective Canopy. It is a gameplay mechanic, not an in-world phenomenon.

Resonances depend only on the first four party members, work in Co-Op Mode, and do not need all members alive. A third or fourth character of the same element adds nothing more.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore), as of 7.1:
- Fervent Flames (two Pyro): 40% shorter Cryo effect, ATK +25%.
- Soothing Water (two Hydro): 40% shorter Pyro effect, Max HP +25%.
- High Voltage (two Electro): 40% shorter Hydro effect; certain Electro reactions have a 100% chance to produce an Electro particle (5 s cooldown).
- Shattering Ice (two Cryo): 40% shorter Electro effect, CRIT Rate +15% against Frozen or Cryo-affected enemies.
- Impetuous Winds (two Anemo): stamina use -15%, movement speed +10%, skill cooldowns -5%.
- Enduring Rock (two Geo): shield strength +15%, plus damage and Geo RES reduction effects when shields or Moondrifts are nearby.
- Sprawling Greenery (two Dendro): Elemental Mastery +50 and reaction-triggered boosts.
- Protective Canopy (four unique elements): all Elemental RES +15% and Physical RES +15%.

- Enduring Rock details: when a shielded character or Moondrifts from Lunar-Crystallize are nearby, damage dealt rises 15%, and dealing damage lowers enemy Geo RES by 20% for 15 s.
- Sprawling Greenery details: after Burning, Quicken, Bloom or Lunar-Bloom, nearby party members gain 30 Elemental Mastery for 6 s; after Aggravate, Spread, Hyperbloom or Burgeon, they gain 20 for 6 s. The durations count independently.
- High Voltage triggers: Superconduct, Stellar-Conduct, Overloaded, Electro-Charged, Lunar-Charged, Quicken, Aggravate or Hyperbloom.
- Co-op rule: if some of a co-op party is inside a Domain, only the characters in the Domain determine resonance and benefit from it.

Elemental Resonance is one of several team bonuses on the Team Bonus screen:
- Moonsign: Moonsign characters in the party give a Moonsign Level. One gives Nascent Gleam; two give Ascendant Gleam, which enhances Moonsign characters' talents and lets non-Moonsign characters raise Lunar reaction damage by up to 36% for 20 s after casting a Skill or Burst, scaling with an element-specific stat. The thresholds are 4,000 ATK (Pyro, Electro, Cryo), 60,000 Max HP (Hydro), 3,600 DEF (Geo), and 1,600 Elemental Mastery (Anemo, Dendro). Introduced with version 6.0.
- Hexerei: Secret Rite: two or more Hexerei characters in the party further enhance them, including activating their Witch's Eve Rite passive. Characters become Hexerei by completing Witch's Homework.
- Nightsoul Burst (region-based): with at least one Natlanese playable character, a Nightsoul Burst triggers at intervals of 18 s for one, 12 s for two, and 9 s for three or more Natlanese characters. Bennett and the Pyro Traveler do not count.

Region-based effects are not listed on the Party Setup menu, and several weapons and talents depend on party regions. Version notes: Elemental Resonance dates from 1.0; Moonsign 6.0; Hexerei 6.2 (per the archive's entries); Nightsoul Burst with Natlan 5.0. Values may shift in later patches.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): represent a resonance as companions who work especially well together, such as two Pyro users feeding each other's flames, with a visible shared glow of their element. Do not quote percentages in character. Protective Canopy can be shown as a diverse team covering one another's weaknesses.

Canon does not say characters feel or name a "resonance", so do not have anyone announce it. Anemo pairs may move more freely, Geo pairs hold firmer shields, and Dendro pairs sense reactions more keenly. Keep these as flavour, not canon facts.

Limits: Only a full party triggers resonance, except that Protective Canopy needs four unique elements. Extra same-element characters add nothing.

Unlisted: this entry does not cover individual talents or weapons that depend on the party's elements.

104.content: Protective Canopy is the resonance granted by a party of four unique elements: all Elemental RES +15% and Physical RES +15%.

105.content:
Elemental Sight (also: elemental trails, elemental traces): Elemental Sight is the ability to perceive the elements around you. Toggling it makes elemental traces visible, shows which nearby things are affected by an element and highlights what can be interacted with. In Teyvat it is bound up with owning a Vision, or at least having elemental sensitivity, which is rare but known.

The Traveler is among those canon confirms to have it, and the wiki also lists Amber, Lisa, Rosaria and Yanfei.

In universe: Elemental traces, also called elemental trails, are left behind by almost anything elemental, from slimes to gods to the wind itself, and can also be left by elemental magic or Vision holders. Everyone knows they exist, but those without elemental affinity find them hard to sense.

Sensitivity varies even between people who can wield the elements, and it can be trained. Lisa says she heard the Traveler's sensitivity is very strong, and later only calls a drawing clear once the Traveler has copied what they saw with Elemental Sight. Bennett is implied to have weak sensitivity: he wanted to swap his goggles for "Alchemist's Goggles", an item rumoured to let anyone see even the faintest elemental energy. Timaeus dismissed those goggles as impossible. An allogene who gives up their Vision may stay sensitive, as Jiangxue does.

Because a Vision helps field work and magical research, including this sight, scholars without one are seen as handicapped. The Fatui-run Northland Bank has some means of detecting elemental energy, which it uses to tell its certified bags of Mora apart. Dr. Edith has no Vision and so no Elemental Sight, yet says the Anemo-imbued leaves the Traveler brought back from the Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero really let one feel the wind, which hints that close proximity may let non-sensitive people notice the elements. Hurdle states that hilichurl bodies cannot withstand high elemental concentrations, so they normally avoid such areas, which suggests at least an instinctive sense for them.

Gameplay: Gameplay: Elemental Sight is toggled with a button beside the minimap (middle mouse button by default on PC). A white range indicator spreads from the active character; background objects turn dark and muted while interactable ones are highlighted.

It shows elemental trails for bounties, between Seelie and their gardens, between Monetoo and their resting places and in certain quests and hidden exploration objectives, and it shows possible routes between a Phase Gate and the gates it connects to. It also shows the element affecting enemies and most interactable objects, and reveals enemy name tags. Highlight colours follow the element: white for nothing, red for fire, torches and explosive barrels, blue for things made Wet, light blue for recently deactivated flamethrowers and Mist Flowers, purple for unbroken Electro crystals, yellow for Geo constructs and ore, turquoise for Anemo ambers and green for Dendro vines and flammable plant matter.

The sight switches itself off after the character moves a short distance, and its range depends on where the character stood when toggling, so far objects may not show. For bounties and some quests only the traces nearest the character appear. Enemies are highlighted even when inactive; shielded enemies take their shield's element while it holds. Not every elemental enemy is inherently affected by its element: Anemo Slimes never apply Anemo to themselves. Some things are not highlighted: most signs and tablets, bushes and small trees, trees yielding wood, and doors into areas of the same instance. It can be captured with the Kamera and is disabled during Third-Person Shooter gameplay.

A Special Elemental Sight exists for a character indwelling an Iktomisaurus, for Masters of the Night-Wind characters and for Mavuika. It widens the field of view and shows hidden details such as certain graffiti arrows and invisible barriers.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay (this project's interpretation, not canon): treat it as a sense, not a menu. A Vision holder can say they feel or see lingering elemental traces, noticing a trail, an enchanted thing or a hidden mechanism, but should not talk about toggles, cooldowns or colour codes. Characters without a Vision or elemental affinity should not perceive traces.

Limits: Canon gives no rule for how far elemental senses reach, and does not say that every Vision holder perceives the same things. Do not assume that all allogenes see equally well, or that people without a Vision cannot sense strong elements at all.

106.content:
Elemental Skill (also: Skill): The Elemental Skill, or just Skill, is a Talent every playable character has from the start. It costs no Energy; instead it goes on cooldown after use. It deals Elemental DMG, never Physical, and usually produces elemental particles that recharge the party's Energy.

It is the everyday counterpart of the Elemental Burst, which needs full Energy.

In universe: This is a gameplay category. In the world, the skill is simply what a character does with their element or training, such as a technique, a summoned construct or a stance. The game fixes one such signature move per character.

Gameplay: Gameplay: using the Skill starts a cooldown whose length differs per character and which cannot be used again until it ends. Cooldown can be shortened, reset or extended by Talents, Constellations and other effects.

Some skills accept more than one input before the cooldown begins, such as Diluc's and Fischl's, and they differ in whether the cooldown starts at once or after the effect expires. Single-input skills, including held ones, start cooldown straight away, with held skills starting it after the hold ends. Some skills have several Charges, shown as small squares on the icon. Many have different tap and hold versions; the hold is usually stronger but has a longer cooldown. Most Skills generate Energy particles when they damage an enemy.

Tartaglia is a special case. His Skill switches him between ranged and melee stances; in melee stance the Skill's stats apply to his Normal Attack, so all of its Skill DMG comes through Normal Attacks, and the cooldown depends on how long he stays in that stance. Talents, Constellations, weapons and artifact sets can raise Skill level, increase Skill DMG or react to its use.

The Skill's cooldown stat, number of charges and particle output differ for each character and are listed in the game's Talents menu and on each character's own entry rather than here. A small number of characters generate no particles from their Skill at all, and particle generation can have its own cooldown separate from the Skill's.

Limits: The Skill is not the same as the Elemental Burst or as a Normal Attack. It is a game category, so characters do not name it in dialogue.

107.content:
Element (also: the Elements, the seven Elements, seven elements, elemental power, elemental Authority, elemental Authorities): The Elements are Teyvat's seven forms of elemental power: Anemo (wind), Geo (earth), Electro (lightning), Dendro (plants), Hydro (water), Pyro (fire) and Cryo (ice). Each is bound to one Archon and that Archon's nation. Ordinary people wield an element through a Vision, a jewel-like focus granted to those with strong desires.

Behind the modern order lie the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons of the old world, whose Authorities were taken by the Heavenly Principles and tied to the Archons' divine thrones. Archons can use their element without a Gnosis, while mortals normally need a Vision.

As of 7.1, one divine throne has been destroyed (Hydro) and its Authority returned to the Hydro Sovereign, six Gnoses are known to have been gathered by the Fatui and the Tsaritsa, and the Pyro Gnosis has vanished. Two newer Vision-like objects exist alongside Visions: Moon Wheels, associated with Nod-Krai and the moon, and Stellar Linchpins from Snezhnaya.

In universe: Each element pairs with one Archon and one nation. Canon does not explain why.

Canon does not say how an Archon relates to their element, nor how a region is shaped by its element.

Some modern nations sit on the former land of the matching Dragon Sovereign. Sumeru was once the domain of the Dendro dragon Apep, the Primordial Sea beneath Fontaine was once governed by the Hydro Dragon, and Natlan was dominated by the Pyro dragon Xiuhcoatl and his draconic kin. Canon does not turn this pattern into an explanation. Most Archons already had some mastery of their element before they ascended: Barbatos began as a wind spirit, Morax was already called a god of Geo long before he became the Geo Archon, and Ei is described as an incarnation of lightning. Pyro is the exception in kind, since Pyro Archons are mortals rather than gods.

An Archon's power is attributed to three sources: ruling their region, their people's faith, and the Authority taken from the Sovereigns. Focalors is a rare case, having given up her innate Hydro ability as an Oceanid when she became a Fontainian human. Because no source explains the deeper relationship, treat claims that "the nation causes the element" or the reverse as open.

The seven elements: Anemo: Mondstadt, Barbatos (Venti). Geo: Liyue, Morax (Zhongli). Electro: Inazuma, the Raiden Shogun (Ei). Dendro: Sumeru, Nahida. Hydro: Fontaine, Focalors. Pyro: Natlan, Mavuika. Cryo: Snezhnaya, the Tsaritsa (Anastasya).

Barbatos and Morax are the only two original Archons still living; the rest of the original Seven have died and been replaced. After the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Ei replaced Makoto, Nahida replaced Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, Focalors replaced Egeria, and Anastasya replaced the Belyi Tsar as Cryo Archon. Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame so that she could return after 500 years.

Hydro is now unusual. In the Fontaine Archon Quest (Masquerade of the Guilty) Focalors destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne and returned its Authority to the Hydro Sovereign, so only six thrones remain. The Hydro Dragon Sovereign is now Neuvillette, born in human form. The Element page lists Neuvillette's source of power as an Ancient Dragon's Authority rather than a Vision.

Origins: The seven elemental Authorities were originally wielded by the Seven Sovereigns, the most powerful dragons of the old world, who ruled alongside the Dragon King Nibelung. When the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat they took part of those Authorities and later tied them to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (Calamitous Tread, 4.1). Visions are also derived from these Authorities.

Elemental energy as the modern world knows it was made later, as the Natlan Archon Quest (5.1, Beneath the Secret Source) reveals. The Heavenly Principles divided the raw elemental currents of the Light Realm into seven, using Phlogiston, Teyvat's primordial energy, as a base. The result was easier to control and more compatible with the Human Realm, and was meant to counter the Abyss (the Void Realm) better. Elemental energy is therefore regarded as the modern counterpart of Phlogiston.

After the war of the Funerary Flame, the Heavenly Principles were badly wounded and could no longer suppress the old order by their own absolute authority. With an unidentified entity ("the one who came after") they carved seven Gnoses from the remains of the Third Descender and stole part of the Sovereigns' Authorities, then set the gods against one another in the Archon War to choose seven victors. Details of this episode come from several late quests and the Gnosis and Seven Sovereigns pages; it is among the most spoiler-heavy material in the archive.

Gnosis origin: The 7.1 Archon Quest (Black Feathers Scattered at Parting) reveals that the Third Descender was Saarelainen, Anastasya's lover and the ancestor of the Khaenri'ahns. He consented to having his remains split into the seven Gnoses in exchange for Anastasya's resurrection and a promise that the Heavenly Principles would never harm his descendants. In the same quest, Anastasya used her Cryo mastery together with the six Gnoses she holds to slow time within a confined space.

Sovereigns: Each element has a Dragon Sovereign. The Sovereigns lost their status and most of their power when their Authorities were taken, and the living ones cannot use their full abilities, or recall the old world, unless their Archon dies or the throne is destroyed and the Authority returned. A new generation is being born as the original Sovereigns fade.

- Anemo: Dvalin, the new Anemo Sovereign, born from a convergence of elemental energy in the high heavens, friend of Barbatos.
- Geo: Azhdaha, once befriended by Morax and later sealed by him under the Dragon-Queller after erosion made him forget his love of humanity.
- Dendro: Apep, who held Sumeru's lush land and nurtured the ancient Dendro lifeforms.
- Hydro: the Hydro Dragon presided over the Primordial Sea; the current Sovereign is Neuvillette, whose Authority was fully restored with the end of Masquerade of the Guilty.
- Pyro: Xiuhcoatl, who held Pyro and presided over light, heat and wisdom; his power is said to show up in saurians directly descended from him.
- Cryo: a Cryo Sovereign whose corpse was used by Hyperborea in a failed Primordial Human project and which afflicted Snezhnaya with primordial ice.
- Electro: the sources read for this entry do not name the Electro Sovereign.
Sovereigns can only be born from elementally pure dragons. The Hydro Sovereign was not born from the Bathysmal Vishaps, who had strayed into impure Cryo and Electro variants, and so took human form. Canon also records that, in the Funerary Year, Nibelung returned bringing Abyssal power, which woke the slumbering Sovereigns for a great war against the Heavenly Principles; the Heavenly Principles dropped Celestial Nails and were left severely weakened.

Gnoses: A Gnosis is a chess-piece-like focus that, according to Venti in Ending Note (Prologue, 1.0), resonates directly with Celestia and is far more advanced than a Vision. Seven were made, one per element, and each belongs to an Archon. Archons can use their element without a Gnosis, and an Archon's divine throne exists independently of whether they hold it.

The Fatui, under the Tsaritsa, collect the Gnoses. Their known holders as of Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana were the Cryo Gnosis (the Tsaritsa), the Anemo Gnosis (taken from Venti by Signora), the Geo Gnosis (obtained from Zhongli under his contract), the Electro and Dendro Gnoses (held by Dottore after dealings with Nahida) and the Hydro Gnosis (given to Arlecchino by Neuvillette). The Pyro Gnosis was never retrieved by the Fatui and vanished after Nahida used it to burn the Irminsul. As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, every one except Pyro.

Skirk, who learned the macabre history of the Gnoses from her master Surtalogi, regards them as objects of misfortune. Like Visions, Gnoses can hold their owner's ambitions, and losing one can take strong obsessions with it. The Gnoses are the subject of their own entries, which carry the per-element detail.

Visions: A Vision is a jewel-like amulet that lets its wearer channel one element directly. Visions are given to "allogenes", people with strong desires and the potential to become gods, and take the shape of a gem with the element's symbol, often in a regional setting. A Vision does not grant instant mastery: using the element takes practice, so skill varies widely. Visions can be channeled through mundane objects and put to everyday tasks. Those who hold one have some sensitivity to elemental energy (Elemental Sight). When a holder dies, their Vision becomes a Masterless Vision, losing its power and element indicator, though some later resonate with a new person.

The Archons do not choose the holders: they have no control over who receives a Vision and know nothing about the recipient, and are only obliged to contribute a portion of their Authority when notified. Evidence suggests that a person deprived of their Vision loses the ambition as well, and the gods may collect a "gift" when a holder's goal is achieved. Details remain deliberately ambiguous.

Non vision sources: Not every character draws on a Vision. The Element page notes: the Traveler and the Wonderland Manekin have none; Venti, Zhongli, the Raiden Shogun, Nahida and Mavuika draw on a Gnosis or Archon power; Neuvillette on an Ancient Dragon's Authority; Skirk on the Seven-Shifting Serpent; Columbina on the Tri-Lunar Convergence.

- Moon Wheels (associated with Nod-Krai): objects formed in a pact between the Heavenly Principles and the Moon Sisters, using kuuvahki, an older, purer form of elemental power. Their users enable Lunar Reactions. Known users include Ineffa, Lauma, Flins, Nefer, Linnea and Zibai.
- Stellar Linchpins (Snezhnaya): Vision-like objects tied by Fatui research to the deceased Third Descender, whose users enable Stellar Glimmer Reactions. Known users are Sandrone, Odette and Vesna, among others.
- The Seven-Shifting Serpent (Chaos Permeation) is a Khaenri'ahn spell that disguises Abyssal power as an element; Skirk uses it to pass as Cryo.

Moon Wheels were distributed to the Moon Sisters' followers as a means of communication, and the wiki suggests Visions were formed on the same principle with modern elemental energy. The Fatui seek to use Stellar Linchpin energy in Project Mistilteinn, aimed at the Heavenly Principles, who would find Light Realm energy futile to fight.

Reactions: When a second element is applied to a target already carrying one, the two can react, for example Vaporize (Pyro with Hydro), Melt (Pyro with Cryo), Overloaded (Pyro with Electro) or Swirl (Anemo spreading another element).

Further examples: Hydro and Electro trigger Electro-Charged; Electro and Cryo, Superconduct; Hydro and Cryo freeze the target; Dendro with Hydro, Bloom; Geo produces Crystallize.

Reactions fall into groups. Transformative reactions (Overloaded, Shattered, Electro-Charged, Superconduct, Swirl, Burning, Bloom, Hyperbloom, Burgeon) deal their own damage. Amplifying reactions (Vaporize, Melt) multiply the triggering hit. Additive reactions (Spread, Aggravate) add to it. Elemental Mastery strengthens them.

Newer families extend the table. Lunar Reactions (Lunar-Bloom, Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Crystallize) need a character with a Moonsign Benediction passive, are tied to Hydro and use kuuvahki, the power associated with Nod-Krai (added from 5.8). Stellar Glimmer Reactions (Stellar-Conduct, Stellar Swirl), tied to Cryo, arrived with Stellar-Conduct in 6.7 and Stellar Swirl in 7.0, and need a character with the matching passive; the wiki notes Saarelainen introduced them to ancient Snezhnaya.

Elemental resonance: Gameplay: when a full party includes two or more characters of the same element, an Elemental Resonance applies. Examples: Fervent Flames (Pyro) raises ATK, Soothing Water (Hydro) raises Max HP, Impetuous Winds (Anemo) lowers stamina use and shortens cooldowns, and Protective Canopy (four distinct elements) raises Elemental and Physical RES by 15%. Every other element has its own named resonance.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not literal lore: the Elements are seven of the eight damage types, the eighth being Physical. Each character has one element, shown by a Vision-style icon.

Enemies can carry elemental auras, Elemental Nodes imbue enemies in some domains, and characters have Elemental DMG Bonus and Elemental RES stats.
Only the Traveler and Wonderland Manekin can change element, by resonating with a Statue of The Seven in a given nation. Characters who use more than one element in the story, such as Tartaglia (Hydro Vision, Electro Delusion) or Kazuha (briefly reawakening a Masterless Electro Vision), use only one in play. Dendro had no playable character until Version 3.0.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the element as the colour and texture of a power, not a switch that controls the world. Show it through sensory cues: pressure and sound for Anemo, tremors and stone for Geo, crackle and static for Electro, growth and spores for Dendro, flow and chill for Hydro, heat and light for Pyro, frost and silence for Cryo.

Keep scale proportionate. A Vision holder channels a modest slice; reshaping a climate or a mountain is Archon-level work. Distinguish who is using what: Vision, Gnosis, Moon Wheel, Stellar Linchpin and Dragon Authority are different sources and ordinary people mostly know only Visions.

Do not have a common NPC understand the Sovereigns, Gnoses or the Heavenly Principles. Most Mondstadters, for example, would not know a bard is their god. Do not let Visions be "given by the Archons", since canon says the Archons do not choose recipients; if characters believe this, record it as their belief.

Limits: A Vision fixes its holder to one element and cannot ordinarily be destroyed or tampered with by human methods. Elemental energy can run out: a Vision holder can burn through too much at once and need rest. Masterless Visions go dull when their holder dies. Gnoses held by non-owners may be restricted in what they can do.

Spoiler boundary: the origin of the Gnoses, the Sovereigns' history and the Heavenly Principles are late-game revelations (4.1, 5.1 and later). A character should not know them unless they were present.

108.content:
The Seven Sovereigns are the seven most powerful elemental lifeforms of the Light Realm and ruled the old world alongside Nibelung. The Heavenly Principles took their Authorities and gave them to the Archons' thrones. Living Sovereigns cannot use their full power until their Authority is returned. The Sovereign dragons are Dvalin (Anemo), Azhdaha (Geo), Apep (Dendro), Neuvillette (Hydro) and Xiuhcoatl (Pyro).

Each Sovereign's land was attuned to its element. The Sovereigns were defeated by the Heavenly Principles and the Four Shades; some fled into the ocean depths. Nibelung's later return with Abyssal power woke them for a failed war of vengeance. The Cryo Sovereign is dead; the Electro Sovereign is not named in the sources read here.

109.content: "Allogenes" is the gods' secret term for Vision holders: people with strong desires who could one day ascend to Celestia and become gods. Venti told the Traveler this in Ending Note (Prologue). Most holders and ordinary Teyvatians do not know the word.

110.content: When a Vision's holder dies, it loses its power and element and becomes a Masterless Vision. Sometimes one resonates with a new person. The very rich seek them as commodities, according to Ningguang's account. Kaedehara Kazuha once briefly used a late friend's Masterless Electro Vision.

111.content: Moon Wheels are Vision-like objects associated with Nod-Krai and the moon, formed from the stuff of the soul in a pact between the Heavenly Principles and the Moon Sisters. They use kuuvahki, an older, purer elemental power, and enable Lunar Reactions in combat. Nod-Krai Moon Wheels look identical to Nod-Krai Visions; Zibai, the only Moon Wheel user from outside Nod-Krai, has a differently shaped frame.

112.content: Stellar Linchpins are Vision-like objects from Snezhnaya, whose users have a power that seems to come from beyond Teyvat. Fatui research links them to the dead Third Descender, Saarelainen: impurities from its remains fix in place when a Linchpin manifests. Known users include Sandrone, Odette and Vesna; they enable Stellar Glimmer Reactions.

113.content: The Lord of the Night's account in the Natlan Archon Quest (5.1) is that the Heavenly Principles divided the Light Realm's raw elemental currents into seven, built on Phlogiston, producing the elemental energy that people now use. This made the energy easier to control and better suited to the Human Realm, to counter the Abyss.

114.content:
Energy (also: Elemental Energy, Energy Recharge, elemental particles, elemental orbs): Energy is the resource a character spends on their Elemental Burst. It builds up from elemental particles and orbs, which drop when Elemental Skills hit enemies or when enemies lose HP, and which recharge the whole party. Using the Burst empties it.

Characters with special energy, such as Mavuika and Skirk, work differently and are mostly outside the rules below.

In universe: Characters do not speak of Energy as a number. The nearest in-world idea is elemental energy: pulses of an element a fighter gathers and then releases in a signature technique. Canon lore elsewhere says elemental energy was made by the Heavenly Principles, who divided raw currents of the Light Realm into seven using Phlogiston as a base (revealed 5.1).

Treat the particles as flecks of an element shed in a fight and drawn to the character, which fits how they glow and fly toward a fighter.

Gameplay: Gameplay: each Burst has its own Energy cost, and a character cannot hold more than their base Burst needs. Being knocked out removes all of a character's Energy; if the active character falls out of bounds or drowns, the whole team loses all Energy.

Particles and orbs recharge the entire party, but only when they reach a character. Energy gained depends on element match, Energy Recharge, whether the character is active and party size. Per particle at 100 percent Energy Recharge, an active character gets 3 from a particle of their own element, 1 of a different element and 2 if non-elemental; orbs give three times as much. Inactive characters get 60 percent of the active rate with four in the party, 70 percent with three and 80 percent with two.

Elemental Skills can drop up to 6 particles at once or fewer at intervals. They may be generated even if the target is immune or shielded, but some coordinated-attack skills will not trigger against targets that cannot take damage. Some skills have a guaranteed count plus a chance of one more, and some have a separate particle cooldown that starts after any attempt. Hitting objects or non-hostile wildlife drops none, with exceptions for Razor's press Skill and Wriothesley's enhanced attacks. Enemies drop particles or orbs at HP thresholds, up to four, and slimes drop their own element while automatons drop non-elemental ones.
Normal and Charged Attacks can sometimes give 1 Energy, with a chance that rises on every failure and resets on success: swords begin at 10 percent and rise 5 per miss; bows 0 and 5; claymores 0 and 10; polearms 0 and 4; catalysts 0 and 10. This and other direct generation, from artifacts, weapons, talents and Constellations, ignores Energy Recharge.

Particles disappear if not collected within roughly 30 seconds and orbs within roughly 9. Weapons can also produce particles; the Electro Elemental Resonance, High Voltage, makes an Electro particle with a 5-second cooldown after an Electro-related reaction, and lightning strikes sometimes yield one. In Co-Op Mode, party size for inactive-character rates counts the characters one player controls, so in a two-player game the host counts as having 2. Energy can be drained by certain enemies, by Ley Line Disorders like High Voltage, and by weapons or artifacts such as Katsuragikiri Nagamasa and Shimenawa's Reminiscence. Special energy is unaffected unless explicitly stated. Event domains and events may also grant Energy.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay (this project's interpretation, not canon): describe a character building toward a signature technique as they fight, gathering momentum from elemental flecks, and releasing it all at once. Do not quote numbers or conversion rates in character.

Limits: Gameplay figures in this entry are mechanics, not world facts. Canon has no in-world rule that a hit produces a set amount of energy, nor a "party" that pools it.

115.content:
Exorcism (also: exorcist arts, Liyue thaumaturgy, thaumaturgy, thaumaturge, thaumaturges): Exorcists, also called thaumaturges, are Liyue people who have sworn an oath to cleanse the land of ghosts, spirits and demons. They are skilled in combat, magic and martial arts, and most come from families that keep exorcism as the family trade.

Canon names few groups: the Tianheng Thaumaturges (Chongyun's clan), the family of Yelan and the Lan Clan. This entry covers the tradition; the Exorcists culture entry covers the people.

In universe: Chongyun's clan motto, as recorded in his and Shenhe's voice-overs, is to keep the heart pure and evil erased. The Tianheng clan keeps handed-down books recording the spirits it has defeated.

Little is known of origins.
