The wiki says Liyue thaumaturgy took its modern form around 500 years ago after the Cataclysm, when a revolution in weapon and catalyst making shifted favour toward supernatural arts over traditional martial arts, though thaumaturges still practise both. Exorcist arts seem close to adeptal arts: Chongyun counts Shenhe, who trained under the adepti, as a master exorcist.

- Tianheng Thaumaturges: Chongyun's clan, with Shenhe from a branch family. Chongyun carries a spirit blade of ice; his abundance of yang energy means he has never actually met a spirit. Shenhe's mother used a dagger in exorcism.
- Yelan's clan: her ancestors held the Fantastic Compass, a device that seals away evil creatures, originally owned by the adeptus Sea Gazer and given to a thaumaturge friend. The clan's catalysts, usable only by its members, are said to be built on it. Boyang and Rongzhao, ancestors of Yelan, were exorcists at the battle at the Chasm 500 years ago with the Yaksha Bosacius.
- Lan Clan: descendants of the brothers of Lan Junming, the Wind Reader of the Eight Adepts, notable for Qimen Arts that may serve duty or craft.

Fetor is a different matter. In Springtime Charms (5.3, limited event) Chongyun reads a dying elder's chill as fetor, not an evil spirit, and the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, not exorcists, burns it with the Art of Homa. Lan Junming also taught a Soul-Binding Art, later outlawed for violating the natural order.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): exorcists favour talismans, wards, mantras and dedicated discipline over spectacle. A clan trade means family loyalty and inherited books and relics. They are not equal to adepti or Archons.

Do not make every Liyue spirit a "demon," and do not confuse exorcism with the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's rites. Do not state how Vision-less exorcists perform magic.

116.content: A device that can seal away evil creatures, said to have been invented by the adeptus Sea Gazer and gifted to a thaumaturge friend. It later reached Yelan's ancestors, who used it at the Chasm to seal in Abyssal monsters; her clan built catalysts on it.

117.content:
Fetor (also: fetor of death, Fetor Node, death energy): Fetor is the energy that leaks into the living world when the border between life and death is disturbed. It is a sign of death pressing in on the living and harms those it touches. It was revealed in the limited-time Liyue event "Springtime Charms" (Lantern Rite, 5.3).

Canon says it is not Abyssal and not divine in origin, and Chongyun distinguishes it from the "evil spirits" exorcists hunt.

In universe: Small leaks happen whenever the border is disturbed. The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is responsible for burning them away with its secret technique, the Art of Homa. In the event, Chongyun senses a strange chill around a dying elder and names it the "fetor of death."

The body absorbs fetor easily and, like Abyssal energy, it seems to linger. In humans it sharply speeds up ageing, leading to fatigue, weakness, coma and eventually death. In monsters such as hilichurls it drives a frenzy. Adepti such as Xiao can perceive it directly; ordinary people mostly cannot, though they may feel unnaturally cold near it. Xiao can share his perception by marking a person with a Witness Sigil.

Baizhu's account is that Changsheng's secret art does not affect fetor. Hu Tao explains that minor leaks are easy work for the Parlor, but a major one cannot be solved by burning, because the problem is the border itself, and the only remedy may be to purify the whole border. In the event this is done with the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, in which Homa altars at the gates burn the fetor away across Liyue. Qiqi absorbed a dangerous amount at the border yet survived, and Lan Yan remarks that she herself would probably not have; the wiki reads Qiqi as somewhat resistant, which may hold for other zombies.

Hu Tao says that about a dozen years before, a border incident at Wuwang Hill killed her father when he tried to burn off the fetor with the Art of Homa and was fatally exposed. In the climax the Traveler draws fetor out of Hu Tao and into themselves to save her; it fades from them afterwards. The event's setting is limited-time content: it is canon, but not every Liyue resident knows the details.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): during the event, fetor appears as balls of dark energy and as Fetor Nodes that can be temporarily dispelled with physical attacks.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show fetor through cold, a heavy hush, tired limbs and people who look suddenly older. Only adepti and those marked by one see it clearly. Keep it Liyue-specific and distinct from Abyssal taint, curses and ghosts.

Do not treat fetor as a curse that an exorcist can simply banish; Chongyun says it is not an evil spirit. Do not extend it to other nations without canon, and do not use Homa as a casual spell. Hu Tao treats it as serious professional work.

118.content: Fetor can accumulate into Fetor Nodes. In the Springtime Charms event they are dispelled for a time by physical attacks, which opens the way past them.

119.comment: Fetor: Border between life and death
119.content: Liyue's border between life and death is a cold, dark place reached through a rift at Wuwang Hill during the event. When it is disturbed, fetor leaks out. Hu Tao, Qiqi and Lan Yan were trapped in it, and Xiao and the Traveler went in to bring them out. The border seems peculiar to Liyue.

120.content:
Frozen (also: Frozen reaction, Freeze Aura, Hydro-Cryo reaction): Frozen is the elemental reaction that happens when Hydro and Cryo meet on a target, in either order. It deals no damage by itself. It encases the target in ice and holds it immobile for a short time. A heavy blunt blow or a Geo attack can then break the ice open, which is the Shatter follow-up. It is a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from.

Frozen has been part of the game since Version 1.0. The in-game tutorial says to wet opponents with Hydro, then switch to a Cryo character to trigger Frozen and control them. Shatter has its own id, system.shattered, and is also described briefly here.

In universe: Canon does not give a story explanation for Frozen. The in-game text is a plain tutorial: when Cryo meets Hydro the Frozen reaction is triggered, and frozen beings cannot move.

Nothing in the sources read ties the reaction to a named character, god or event. Do not invent an origin, for example a Cryo Archon's spell or a Fatui technique.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Frozen needs Hydro applied to a target already carrying Cryo, or Cryo applied to a target carrying Hydro. It deals no damage of its own. It gives the target a Freeze Aura that immobilises it for a while.

- The Freeze Aura's duration depends on the smaller of the two elemental amounts involved (the wiki's gauge units), and a target with Freeze Resistance stays frozen for less time.
- Shatter is triggered when a Frozen target is hit by a blunt attack or by Geo. It deals Physical damage and removes the Freeze Aura.
- Applying Pyro to a Freeze Aura consumes it and triggers Melt, Electro triggers Superconduct, and Anemo triggers Swirl.
- A blunt hit first uses up part of the Freeze Aura according to its Poise damage, and Shatter occurs only if some Freeze Aura is left afterwards.

- Immunity: during an Elemental Burst's invincibility frames no character can be frozen, and the wiki lists a few character abilities with the same protection (Fischl's Midnight Phantasmagoria, Mona's Mirror Reflection of Doom hold, the Wanderer's Hanega: Song of the Wind, and Chasca's Nightsoul's Blessing state). On a target immune to freezing, the reaction still triggers but the Freeze Aura does not apply and the target is not immobilised.
- Enemy immunity and resistance: most bosses are always immune, and the wiki lists many individual enemies as immune in certain states, such as Cryo Slimes, Large Cryo Slimes, Cryo Abyss Mages and the Tainted Hydro Phantasm when enraged. Freeze Resistance values are given for a few enemies; most land Local Legends have 90 percent.
- Shatter's damage follows the transformative-reaction model: it depends on the triggering character's level and Elemental Mastery, not on ATK.
- The Elemental Resonance Shattering Ice (two or more Cryo characters) raises CRIT Rate against targets that are Frozen or affected by Cryo; see the Cryo entry.

- The wiki's gauge model: the Freeze Aura holds twice the smaller of the two input amounts, and its duration grows more slowly than that amount does (a square-root relationship). This describes the gameplay framework, which the wiki calls Elemental Gauge Theory, not a character's explanation.
- Shatter happens before any elemental damage in the same hit, so it can prevent some reactions, but an element can persist or be reapplied under a Freeze Aura and react afterwards; the wiki's example is Hydro under a Freeze Aura being Crystallized after Shatter.
- Since Version 5.8, Lunar reactions replace Electro-Charged, Bloom and Crystallize in parties with a matching Moonsign passive, and since 7.0 Stellar Glimmer reactions replace Superconduct and Cryo Swirl in parties with a matching Stellar Jubilee passive. Frozen is not replaced by either family; the wiki's table lists it unchanged as of 7.1.

Environment: Gameplay: in the open world, parts of most bodies of water can be frozen by Cryo attacks, and characters and enemies can stand on the ice. Pyro melts the ice instantly, and Electro on it can cause Superconduct, which the wiki notes also happens near Electro-Charged water.

The frozen-water duration depends on how strong the Cryo application is, from about 2.5 seconds for a basic application to 8 seconds for the strongest one the wiki lists (Kaeya's Frostgnaw). Cryo Slimes and Cryo Abyss Mages freeze nearby water for about 8 seconds. Some objects can also be frozen, such as the Baron Bunny and Ushi gadgets from Masatsu Zetsugi: Akaushi Burst!, though explosive objects such as Exploding Barrels can only be frozen without being set off by damageless applications of Hydro and Cryo.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Frozen as a visible shell of ice that forms fast around the target, with a sharp crack and a spray of fragments when it breaks. A frozen person or creature is held in place, not killed; keep it a short, temporary combat effect. Frost is the Cryo cue; a blow that cracks the ice should feel heavy, like a hammer or a stone-hard Geo strike.

Narratively, Hydro first and Cryo second reads as wet things freezing, which is easy to depict. Do not mix up Frozen with the cold of Dragonspine or with Snezhnaya's winter; a frozen target in a warm room is still frozen by the reaction. Pyro frees a frozen ally by melting the ice, since Pyro consumes the Freeze Aura (Melt).

Avoid having ordinary Hydro and Cryo users freeze large crowds permanently, kill by freezing, or freeze a god or boss; the wiki lists most bosses as immune. Keep any Shatter damage proportionate.

Limits: Frozen does not hurt by itself, and it does not last long. It does not work on every enemy.

The Freeze Aura does not react with Hydro. Elemental shields and some innate enemy auras carry a different frozen state of Cryo that is not the same as a reaction-made Freeze Aura.

Examples: Gameplay example, from the in-game tutorial: soak an opponent with Hydro, then switch to a Cryo character and attack, and the opponent is frozen. A hammer strike or a Geo blow then Shatters it.

121.content: Shatter is the follow-up to Frozen. When a Frozen target is hit by a blunt attack or a Geo attack, the ice breaks and the target takes Physical damage; the Freeze Aura is removed. It uses the transformative-reaction damage model. Its own entry is system.shattered. The wiki's main page for it redirects to the Frozen page.

122.content: Some targets resist or ignore freezing. Freeze Resistance shortens the Freeze Aura on a target; the wiki lists the Abyss Herald Wicked Torrents while shielded, the Consecrated Beast, the Canine Bunshin and most land Local Legends among those with it. A target immune to freezing still triggers the reaction, but is not immobilised.

123.content:
Geo (also: Geo element, element of earth, element of rock, element of stone): Geo is the element of earth and stone, one of Teyvat's seven elements, seen in stone constructs, crystal shields and shaking ground. Its Archon is Morax (Rex Lapis), God of Contracts, patron of Liyue. He staged his own "death", gave up his Gnosis and now lives as Zhongli in Liyue Harbor.

Neuvillette addresses the Geo Archon as Deus Auri. Geo ascension gems are Prithiva Topaz.

In universe: Few people can use Geo, usually through a Geo Vision. Morax draws on the Geo Authority of his divine throne in Celestia instead; the Geo "Vision" at Zhongli's back is not a real one.

Geo's gifts to people are practical. A Liyue legend credits the Lord of Rock with the first settlers' stone stoves and struck-stone fires, which is why taverns once worshipped him as "God of the Stove"; the Moonlight Merriment event later shows that legend is false, as the true God of the Stove was Marchosius (now Guoba), whose tales merged into Morax's over time. Legend credits Rex Lapis with raising Mt. Tianheng and imprisoning the sea god Osial under the stone lances now called the Guyun Stone Forest. The Geo Archon's power was also what minted Mora, the currency of all Teyvat, at the Golden House.

Geo energy is said to saturate the crust of the earth, and it condenses into creatures: the Archive describes Geo Slimes as small monsters built from Geo gathered in the earth, and Geo Specters as monsters born from a high concentration of Geo that float in the air and resemble fruit when their wings close. Because Morax slew or sealed many ancient gods, legend holds that their bodies sank into the earth while their grudges seeped out as miasma, plague and monster attacks, which is why the Yakshas were called to keep subduing them.

Rex Lapis is the God of Contracts and Liyue's economy rests on his Mora. The Prithiva Topaz item text, a first-person line the wiki considers likely spoken by Morax, says that the currencies flowing through the land are "my flesh and blood", presenting Mora as part of himself. Canon does not explain how the Geo Authority and his contract role are connected.

Origins: Origins, as canon tells them. The elemental Authorities first belonged to the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons of the old world; the Geo Dragon Sovereign was Azhdaha, who ruled a vast territory that included what is now Liyue. The Heavenly Principles stole part of that power and tied it to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (revealed in the Fontaine Archon Quest, 4.1); Visions also derive from these Authorities. How an Archon relates to their element and why a nation takes on its element's character is still unexplained.

Archon and nation: Archon: Morax (Rex Lapis, Zhongli), oldest of The Seven. Nation: Liyue, now governed by humans.

Morax was born more than six thousand years ago and became Archon by winning the Archon War in the region. After faking his death in the Rite of Descension, he arranged a test of whether Liyue could manage without him, with the help of the Tsaritsa and her Fatui, and retired. He now works as a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor under Hu Tao. Few know he is the Archon. Along with Barbatos he is one of the two original members of The Seven who remain.

Liyue is governed by the Liyue Qixing, who run the city from the Jade Chamber; the Golden House has been shut since Morax's retirement, and Mora circulation depends on the Geo Gnosis he gave away. Morax told the Qixing, through Ningguang, that he was alive but had stepped down, and left the official explanation of his "death" to them. He forged contracts with the adepti, including a long-standing one with Ganyu, to protect Liyue Harbor, and called the Yakshas to subdue the ancient gods; one of them, Xiao, still serves him.

Earlier, he and Guizhong, the God of Dust, led the Guili Assembly at Guili Plains; Guizhong died in a battle that destroyed Guili Plains and Dihua Marsh, after which Morax moved their people south to found Liyue Harbor. Near the end of the Archon War he also defeated the mistress of Chenyu Vale, whose adepti servants sealed her away. Before he became Rex Lapis, in the era of the unified civilization, he met Zibai, then ruler of Lang-Gan, and taught her the art of Tri-Factor Excision.

Gnosis and authority: After the Rite of Parting in Archon Quest Chapter I, Act III (1.0), Signora, as the Tsaritsa's envoy, collected the Geo Gnosis from Zhongli peacefully under the contract he called the "contract to end all contracts". The Tsaritsa's end of the bargain is still unexplained.

Zhongli later told Azhdaha that he was no longer the Geo Archon, and Azhdaha, who said he could sense it, accepted that. Even so, the Archons' Divine Thrones and Authorities exist independently of their Gnoses, and Neuvillette, speaking of the Geo Archon as Deus Auri, expects that Morax will one day have to answer for the Authority he won. Ever since the Gnosis left Liyue, the Golden House stopped minting Mora.

The Gnosis page lists the Geo Gnosis as one of the six in the Fatui's possession as of Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, along with the Cryo, Anemo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses. Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, later used the six Gnoses together with her Cryo mastery to slow time within a large room in the 7.1 Archon Quest (Black Feathers Scattered at Parting).

Gnosis status: As of 7.1 the Geo Gnosis is not with Zhongli. The wiki records it as one of the six Gnoses in the Fatui's and the Tsaritsa's hands. Do not give the Gnosis back to Zhongli.

Elemental beings: Azhdaha, the Geo Dragon Sovereign, sealed beneath the Dragon-Queller; Geo elemental lifeforms such as Geo Slimes, Geo Specters and the Geo Hypostasis; and the Geovishap line of dragons.

Azhdaha was a friend of Morax whom Morax once gave sight, and who suffered from erosion until he lashed out at people. He was sealed in the Chasm and beneath the Dragon-Queller at Nantianmen. Geo Slimes are small and drifting, Geo Specters float and burst into earthquake-like attacks, and the Geo Hypostasis (code name Gimel) is a boss in the Guyun Stone Forest with a high-density solid shell around a reactive core. It raises pillars and drops them as stone seals.

- The Geo Hypostasis is the third of the Hebrew-letter-named hypostases (Gimel); only its exposed core reacts to elements.
- Geo Specters haunt Seirai Island and Watatsumi Island in Inazuma.
- Azhdaha holds command over the Ley Lines; he has sent a vessel in the form of a girl, Jiu, to free him, and his benevolent fragment possessed the human Kun Jun to warn Morax.
- Geoculi: crystallised Geo energy scattered across Liyue; the item text says offering one to a Statue of The Seven restores power the statue lost over the years.

In the quest Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved (1.5), the Traveler, Zhongli and Kun Jun fight Azhdaha, who is resealed; his body is held under the Dragon-Queller and the Mountain Shaper and the Moon Carver helped build the domain that first sealed him. Azhdaha's benevolent side, speaking through Kun Jun, bids Morax farewell.

Known uses: Barriers and shields, summoned stone constructs, pillars of rock, shaking the ground, and petrifying or fixing a target in place.

Geo shapes land as well as fights. Morax is said to have raised mountains, lowered tides and bound a sea god with stone lances. Geo Vision holders in play raise constructs and crystalline shields.

- Zhongli's burst (Planet Befall) petrifies enemies and places a persistent Geo status on them for the duration.
- Geo characters in play, such as Ningguang, Albedo, Chiori and Gorou, summon constructs or shields; the wiki lists Geo Constructs as a category of talents.
- Zibai (6.3) and Illuga are Moonsign-era Geo characters.
- The Traveler: resonating with a Statue of The Seven in Liyue changes the Traveler's element to Geo, and in the Heart of Glaze chapter a cutscene shows them using both Anemo and Geo.

- Visions remain personal. Zhongli's hair-tips glow amber when he uses his skill or burst, and the Geo "Vision" at his back is not a real Vision.
- Kachina (Natlan) and Linnea are among the more recent Geo characters, as are Illuga and Zibai.

Limits: Geo does not react with Anemo or Dendro; it crystallises Pyro, Hydro, Electro and Cryo.

Crystallize turns Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo into a shard of that element that grants a shield when picked up; it does not create an element.

Gameplay: a Geo aura cannot normally be applied by elemental attacks. Exceptions are the Geo Hypostasis, Stonehide Lawachurls and Large Geo Slimes while their shields are up (which cannot react), and Zhongli's burst, which applies a persistent Geo status of 0.04 gauge units that does not decay until the petrification ends and does not react. Geo elemental lifeforms are immune to Geo damage.

Interactions: Crystallize: Geo meeting Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo makes an elemental shard whose pickup gives a shield (own entry). Geo also gives Shatter, in which hitting a frozen target deals Physical damage and ends the freeze.

Lunar-Crystallize (Geo plus Hydro, 6.3): creates three Moondrifts near the target, Geo constructs that resonate after enough Lunar-Crystallize reactions, firing Moondrift Harmony for Geo damage.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Geo is a damage type and the element of characters such as Zhongli, Ningguang, Albedo, Noelle, Gorou, Yun Jin, Arataki Itto, Navia, Chiori, Xilonen, Kachina, Zibai, Illuga and Linnea, plus the Geo Traveler. Geoculi are scattered across Liyue.

The Elemental Resonance "Enduring Rock" (two or more Geo characters) increases shield strength by 15%. Characters protected by a shield, or near Moondrifts from Lunar-Crystallize, gain a 15% damage bonus and reduce enemies' Geo RES by 20% for 15 seconds. Crystallize shield strength rises with the user's level and Elemental Mastery; shards last 15 seconds, only one Crystallize shield can be active and each shield absorbs more against its own element. There are 131 Geoculi in the overworld, which allow the Liyue Statues of The Seven to be fully levelled with one to spare, and the Geoculus Resonance Stone marks nearby Geoculi. Geo ascension gems are Prithiva Topaz.

Gameplay recent: Gameplay, recent additions: Lunar-Crystallize joined Crystallize and Shatter as a Geo-based reaction in 6.3 and is part of the Moonsign system. Recent Geo characters include Zibai (6.3, a 5-star sword user tied to Lang-Gan, Zhongli and the Lantern Rite plot), Illuga (4-star polearm) and Linnea (5-star bow).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Geo as weight, stillness and pattern: amber-gold light, hexagonal or crystal facets, dust settling, a faint hum in stone. It protects more often than it strikes; a Geo defender plants themselves, and a shield that appears should read as solid, not glowing energy. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can raise a pillar or a crystalline barrier, but reshaping mountains and binding a god is an Archon's work.

Geo suits ideas of endurance and promises kept through time (an interpretation, not canon). Liyue's people associate stone with the Geo Archon, so a sudden rumble or a stone that does not give way can be read as an omen. Do not have an ordinary Liyue resident recognise Zhongli as Morax.

Avoid portraying Geo as earthquake or lava control for ordinary users; large-scale earth-shaping is shown only for the Geo Archon and the Geo Dragon Sovereign. Do not describe Zhongli as having regained his Gnosis, and do not describe the Geo Archon as still ruling Liyue.

124.content:
The Geo Archon is Morax, called Rex Lapis in Liyue and by many other titles. He faked his death during the Rite of Descension and gave his Gnosis to the Tsaritsa, leaving Liyue to humans. He lives as Zhongli, a funeral-parlor consultant in Liyue Harbor. His own character entry carries his biography, so this entry only points at the element.

Neuvillette says he intends to bring each of the Seven to trial and speaks of Deus Auri as the Archon who won the Authority of Geo. The Geo Archon is also the subject of a Liyue folk image, a stage hero in opera, and wrongly credited in folk legend as the God of the Stove (a title that belonged to Marchosius); the person Zhongli and the legend do not always agree.

125.content:
Azhdaha is the Geo Dragon Sovereign, an ancient Geovishap ancestor who once ruled a territory including what is now Liyue. Morax stopped the earthquakes that his movements caused, gave him sight, and made a contract with him. Erosion and human mining in the Chasm eventually drove him to attack the people he had loved, and he was sealed under the Dragon-Queller at Nantianmen. He is incapacitated, not dead, as of Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved.

The English "Geo Dragon" title comes from the Chinese "dragon king" wording, while his design notes and the Chinese text of the quest call him an Earth Dragon instead. His character page holds his full account.

126.content: Geoculi are found scattered across Liyue. The item text calls a Geoculus a substance that has accumulated intense Geo energy, to be offered at a Statue of The Seven to reinstate power it has lost over the years. In gameplay there are 131 in the overworld.

127.content: When Geo meets Pyro, Hydro, Electro or Cryo, Crystallize leaves a shard of that element on the ground. Picking it up gives the character a shield of that element. Shards last 15 seconds and only the three newest remain. Lunar-Crystallize is the Hydro version introduced in 6.3. Crystallize is a gameplay mechanic with only metaphorical support in lore.

128.content: Geo Slimes are small monsters formed by the build-up of Geo within the earth; the Archive notes their "down-to-earth" feel. Geo Specters float, burst into earthquakes when enraged and haunt Seirai and Watatsumi in Inazuma; some tales treat them as the fruit of a giant sky tree with medicinal value. The Geo Hypostasis, code name Gimel, is a boss in Guyun Stone Forest: a solid shell of concentrated Geo around a reactive core. In gameplay these lifeforms are immune to Geo.

129.content:
Hexerei (also: Hexerei: Secret Rite, Hexerei character, Hexerei characters, Witch's Eve Rite): Hexerei (German for witchcraft) is a party Team Bonus introduced in Version 6.2. Certain characters become "Hexerei characters" by completing their Witch's Homework quests. Bring two or more into the party and the bonus Hexerei: Secret Rite activates, strengthening them.

The system is built around the Hexenzirkel's "homework" for the Traveler. The Hexerei characters at launch were Sucrose, Mona, Durin, Klee, Albedo, Venti, Fischl and Razor; Varka, Nicole, Lohen and Prune were added later.

In universe: In the fiction, the Witch's Homework is set by witches. In the quest Unexpected Commission, Lisa of the Knights of Favonius library and the mage Alice have the Traveler sort a huge anonymous donation of books, among them banned ones, and the Traveler receives The Little Witch's Dictionary. Its description says it was made by the witches and "claims to explain" the storybook The Little Witch and the Undying Fire, while really containing homework tailored by the Hexenzirkel for each reader.

The Hexenzirkel was founded by Alice and is described as a mysterious group of powerful witches pursuing mostly personal goals. Not every Hexerei character is shown as a member: Nicole lists the Hexenzirkel as an affiliation, and Mona is a student of its astrologer Barbeloth, but canon does not make the whole roster members.

Gameplay: Gameplay: finishing a character's Witch's Homework makes them a Hexerei character. With at least two Hexerei characters in the party, Hexerei: Secret Rite is active.

Requirements: complete the Prologue Archon Quest Act III, finish Witch's Homework: Solution (the quest begins in Mondstadt City) to receive The Little Witch's Dictionary, own the character and have them at level 70 or higher. Each character then has their own homework quest.
In Witch's Homework: Solution, the Traveler may also invite one of Fischl, Sucrose or Razor to the party; only one can be chosen.
The Secret Rite gives each Hexerei character their Witch's Eve Rite Passive, an additional talent, and enhances some of their other talents and Constellations. Most of those effects work only while two or more Hexerei characters are in the party. Two weapons, Athame Artis and The Daybreak Chronicles, show their own effects when the party has the bonus.

The roster in the wiki's Witch's Homework table (character: quest "act" then follow-up quest, passive):
- Albedo: Of Questions Beyond Questions / Old Friends and New Knowledge; passive Book of Blinding Light.
- Klee: Of Leaves That Spark / The Great Mage's Journey of Trials; Sparkborne Magic.
- Mona: Of Untested Insight / A Dry Well Doth Not Reflect the Stars; Genesis of Starsigns.
- Venti: Of the Waking of Wind / Tales of Time and Wind; Temporal Wind's Eulogy.
- Durin: Of This World / A Child Wandering the World; Ode to Ascension.
- Varka: The Untitled Question / Stories to Sate the Glass and Scroll; Dawn's Return.
- Nicole: The Role of a Guide...? / Witch's Homework: The Role of a Guide...?; Light in the Darkness.
- Lohen: Of Various Foes / Proof of Strength; Unhealing Thorn.
- Fischl: Of the Unexpected / Alan Smithee, Author of Fischl; Phantasmal Nocturne.
- Razor: Of the Little Wolf Pack / With Lupical...; Surge of Lightning.
- Sucrose: Of Wonderland Flowers / The Law of Boundaries; Sevenfold Transmutation.
- Prune: Of What Is Contested / A Proposition Beyond Refutation; Witchseeker's Vow.
Hexerei sits beside Elemental Resonance and Moonsign as a Team Bonus type, and all three have their own tab on the Party Setup screen.

Version history: Version 6.2 "Luna III" (2025-12-03) added Witch's Homework as a permanent event and launched Hexerei: Secret Rite with Sucrose, Mona, Durin, Klee, Albedo, Venti, Fischl and Razor. Version 6.6 "Luna VII" (2026-05-20) added the homework quests for Prune, Lohen and Nicole alongside those characters, and a Hexerei-themed album for Repertoire of Myriad Melodies. Later patch notes (6.3, 6.6) mention fixes to the weapons' Hexerei visual effects.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat "Hexerei" as a loose bond of witch-adjacent people drawn together by the Traveler's homework, not a formal guild. A scene with two or more Hexerei characters can feel charged or unusually in tune, but avoid giving them powers beyond their own.

Do not assume any Hexerei character is a Hexenzirkel member unless canon says so, and do not claim the Witch's Homework reveals Hexenzirkel plans.

130.content: The Witch's Eve Rite Passive is an additional talent unlocked for a character once they finish their Witch's Homework. It is part of Hexerei: Secret Rite and enhances other talents and Constellations of that character.

131.content: A gadget received from Alice in the quest Unexpected Commission. It lists and starts the Witch's Homework quests. Its description says the witches made it and that it is "actually filled with homework tailored by the Hexenzirkel."

132.content:
Hydro (also: Hydro element, element of water): Hydro is the element of water, one of Teyvat's seven elements. Its homeland is Fontaine, the nation of justice. Two gods held the title of Hydro Archon, Egeria and then Focalors. Focalors executed herself in 4.2 and destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne, so Fontaine has had no Hydro Archon since. The Hydro Authority now belongs to Neuvillette, the reborn Hydro Dragon Sovereign.

Hydro ascension gems are Varunada Lazurite. Hydro users appear well beyond Fontaine; the Fatui Harbinger Tartaglia and Columbina of Nod-Krai both wield Hydro.

In universe: Most people use Hydro through a Vision. Neuvillette needs none, because the Hydro Authority is his own. In how it interacts with other elements, rain, rivers, the sea and the Primordial Sea beneath Fontaine all count as Hydro.

Fontaine was where the old Hydro Dragon ruled the Primordial Sea; Hydro vishap legend calls the Dragon its "beating heart". After the Dragon fell, Egeria became the god of Fontaine and gave it its laws. Hydro in Fontaine is entwined with justice, trials and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale.

The Fontainians descend from Oceanids that Egeria made human with water from the Primordial Sea, an act the Heavenly Principles branded as an original sin. The Prophecy of Fontaine foretold that the people would dissolve into water and leave the Hydro Archon weeping alone on her throne.

Origins: Origins, as canon tells them. The elemental Authorities first belonged to the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons of the old world. The Heavenly Principles stole part of that power and tied it to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (revealed in the 4.1 Archon Quest); Visions also derive from these Authorities. In the Natlan Archon Quest (5.1), the Lord of the Night reveals that elemental energy was made by dividing the raw currents of the Light Realm into seven, using Phlogiston as a base. Neuvillette's Vision character story adds that the Heavenly Principles, gravely wounded in a great war, made the Gnoses together with another entity as a substitute for their authority, and that the Seven had to grant a shard of their mastery to anyone whose wish reached the heavens. He says he obeys no edict from the heavens but acknowledges human will, so he too set parts of himself aside, like a dragon's hoard, for worthy humans to claim.

Archon and nation: Hydro Archon: none as of 7.1. The divine throne was destroyed in 4.2. The two former Archons were Egeria and Focalors, both Gods of Justice among The Seven. Nation: Fontaine.

Egeria presided over Fontaine from about 2,000 to 500 years ago, after the fall of Remuria, uniting the surviving tribes and establishing its laws. She died in battle at Tunigi Hollow during the Cataclysm and her body became the waters of the Amrita. Focalors, originally an Oceanid familiar of Egeria, succeeded her and governed for 499 years.

Focalors separated her divinity from her humanity. The body and spirit she left behind became Furina, who played the Hydro Archon in public for about five centuries to hide the real god's plan from the Heavenly Principles. In the 4.2 Archon Quest Focalors had the Oratrice sentence her to death, which destroyed the throne and returned its Authority to Neuvillette. The Fontainians were then absolved of the original sin and made true humans. Furina gave up the political post of Hydro Archon and now lives as an ordinary Fontainian. Neuvillette now handles the affairs of the title from the Palais Mermonia, with the duties of Hydro Sovereign and Iudex coexisting in him. The wiki infers there will be no further Hydro Archons, since the throne no longer exists.

The hydro dragon: The Hydro Dragon Sovereign, the Dragon of Water, was one of the Seven Sovereigns and ruler of the vishaps with sovereignty over water. It fought the Heavenly Principles, was defeated and withered away. Cassiodor says no new Hydro Dragon could be born while Egeria hibernated in the deep sea. An Enkanomiya prophecy held that a new Hydro Dragon would come in human form, because the Bathysmal Vishaps, originally Hydro, had become impure by learning Electro and Cryo. That came true in Neuvillette, the Iudex of Fontaine. Before 4.2 he had lost many memories and much of his hold on the Primordial Sea; with the Authority restored he regained both and used it to make the Fontainians fully human.

A Fontainian saying, told by Freminet, claims the Hydro Dragon weeps when it rains and that children should shout for it to stop. In canon the sky does rain when Neuvillette grieves, and Focalors repeated the saying to him at their last meeting. Neuvillette has chosen to keep giving out Visions, in recognition of human will.

Gnosis and authority: The Hydro Gnosis powered the Oratrice, which was secretly merged with Focalors; only a little of the Indemnitium gathered from trials at the Opera Epiclese ran the Court, and the rest was stored so she could execute herself. When Focalors died the Oratrice stopped working, but the Hydro Gnosis was unaffected. Archons keep their divine thrones and elemental power whether or not they hold their Gnosis.

Neuvillette obtained the Hydro Gnosis after Focalors's death. On Skirk's advice he wanted it out of Fontaine, and it went to the Fatui through Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift" for their help against the Prophecy; Before that, Arlecchino had the Tsaritsa's permission to try using the Hydro Gnosis against the Prophecy herself, a plan Lyney and Lynette knew of; the chance never came, and she later handed the Gnosis to the Tsaritsa.

Besides her own Cryo Gnosis, the Tsaritsa gained the Anemo and Geo Gnoses first, then the Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses; the Pyro Gnosis never reached her.

Gnosis status: In the 7.1 Archon Quest "A Rekviem for the Underworld", Anastasya (the Tsaritsa) used her Cryo mastery together with the six Gnoses, the Hydro Gnosis among them, to slow time within a room of her palace and stall Rhinedottir. As of 7.1 the Hydro Gnosis remains in her possession.

Elemental beings: Hydro Slimes, Hydro Samachurls, Hydro Specters, Hydro Mimics (summoned by Oceanids) and the Hydro Hypostasis. The Hydro Dragon Sovereign is Neuvillette.

Oceanids, occasionally called the Lochfolk, are beings of pure Hydro energy from Fontaine who float through the air, command water and make Hydro Mimics, water creatures that copy animals. Hydro Slimes form from Hydro dispersed through nature; legend says travellers once packed them as emergency water, though the dense Hydro makes drinking one harmful. Hydro Samachurls are aged hilichurl shamans who chant to the power of Hydro and call rain that heals allies.

- Hydro Hypostasis: Code Name: He, a high-purity Hydro entity that violently expels those who test it. It is found on Watatsumi Island in Inazuma.
- Bathysmal Vishaps: originally Hydro dragon-kin of the Primordial Sea, they later evolved to use Electro and Cryo.
- Since Egeria's death most of Fontaine's waters can no longer naturally create Oceanids.
- Powerful, wise Oceanids can make copies of people, as Idyia did with her past companions in the Veluriyam Mirage.

Known uses: Currents, jets, bubbles, rain and tides, healing water, and soaking things so that they react to Electro and Cryo.

Neuvillette commands the Primordial Sea's waters and can draw out the memories stored in water. Hydro Samachurls heal allies with rain.

- Furina's Vision appeared in her character story during a scene of the musical "The Little Oceanid" at the Opera Epiclese, when her heroine vanishes; she then studied it all night and flooded her building.
- Columbina, a Hydro character from Nod-Krai, is listed with a Tri-Lunar Convergence instead of a Vision and enables Lunar reactions (Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom, Lunar-Crystallize).
- Under Elemental Sight, Oceanids in human form show as Hydro.

- Tartaglia holds a Hydro Vision and also an Electro Delusion; as a playable character he only wields Hydro.

Limits: Hydro alone only soaks; it needs another element to do something special.

Wet itself has no special effect; it only allows Hydro reactions. A Vision fixes its holder to one element, while Archons and Sovereigns hold an Authority rather than a Vision.

The Hydro Hypostasis is immune to Hydro damage. In lore, the Hydro Archon's throne cannot be restored after 4.2, and Neuvillette's mastery of the sea is the full Authority only because Focalors returned it.

Interactions: Hydro reacts with Pyro (Vaporize), Cryo (Frozen), Electro (Electro-Charged), Anemo (Swirl), Geo (Crystallize) and Dendro (Bloom).

Bloom extends to Hyperbloom (Electro on a Dendro Core) and Burgeon (Pyro on a Dendro Core). Lunar reactions add Lunar-Charged (Hydro with Electro), Lunar-Bloom (Hydro with Dendro) and Lunar-Crystallize (Hydro with Geo).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Hydro is a damage type and the element of characters such as Neuvillette, Furina, Sigewinne, Tartaglia, Columbina, Vodyanitsa (added in 7.1) and the Hydro Traveler.

The Elemental Resonance "Soothing Water" (two or more Hydro characters) cuts Pyro duration by 40% and raises Max HP by 25%. Any Hydro damage, rain or contact with water applies Wet. Hydroculi, 271 of them in Fontaine (225 in the overworld and 46 in the Sea of Bygone Eras), are offered at Statues of The Seven. Neuvillette is Pneuma-aligned.

Lunar-Charged is the Moon Wheel variant of Electro-Charged: it makes a thundercloud that keeps damaging enemies affected by both Hydro and Electro. The Traveler becomes Hydro by resonating with a Statue of The Seven in Fontaine.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Hydro as flow, weight and sound: drips, condensation on glass, spray, a hush before rain. Blue and pale teal are safe visual cues. Keep scale proportionate: a Vision holder can raise a jet, bubble or wave; moving the sea is a Sovereign's work.

In Fontaine, rain can mirror mood, especially around Neuvillette. Wet clothing and pooling water are natural prompts for Electro or Cryo reactions.

Do not claim there is a current Hydro Archon, or that Furina is a god; since 4.2 she is an ordinary human. Do not place the Hydro Gnosis anywhere except with the Tsaritsa as of 7.1.

133.content:
Two gods held the Hydro Archon title: Egeria, the Mistress of Many Waters, and Focalors, the Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws. Focalors's death in 4.2 destroyed the divine throne, so as of 7.1 no Hydro Archon exists.

Furina played the public Hydro Archon for about 500 years, as Focalors planned, then abdicated. The Authority now rests with Neuvillette as the Hydro Sovereign.

134.content:
The Hydro Dragon Sovereign was the old ruler of water and the vishaps, one of the Seven Sovereigns. It died in the war against the Heavenly Principles and was reborn in human form as Neuvillette, who regained its Authority in 4.2.

A children's saying in Fontaine claims the Hydro Dragon weeps when it rains.

135.content: Hydroculi are collectible substances of intense Hydro energy found across Fontaine and the Sea of Bygone Eras. Offered at a Statue of The Seven, they help restore power the statue has lost over the years. There are 271 in total.

136.content: Varunada Lazurites are the ascension gems for Hydro characters. The gemstone's description quotes an unnamed speaker on ideals without stain and on laws and the Tribunal being able to judge even the speaker; the wiki reads the lines as fitting the 4.2 Archon Quest and the Oratrice's sentence on Focalors.

137.content:
Oceanids are beings of pure Hydro from Fontaine who followed Egeria. Legend says her first tear created the first Oceanid. She gave some of them human forms with water from the Primordial Sea, which the Heavenly Principles counted as a sin, and many Oceanids left Fontaine after her death.

Focalors was an Oceanid who became Hydro Archon. After the Prophecy was broken, the descendants of the transformed Oceanids, the Fontainians, were made true humans.

138.content:
Hyperbloom (also: Hyperbloom reaction, Electro Bloom reaction, Sprawling Shot): Hyperbloom is a Dendro elemental reaction. When Electro touches a Dendro Core (the orb a Bloom leaves behind), the core becomes a homing projectile, a Sprawling Shot, which flies to the closest enemy and bursts in a small area for strong Dendro damage. It is the Electro counterpart of Burgeon.

It debuted in Version 3.0 with Bloom, Burgeon, Quicken, Spread and Aggravate, the reactions introduced for Dendro. A Bloom, from Dendro and Hydro, has to make the core first.

In universe: Canon gives no in-world explanation for Hyperbloom. The pages read treat it only as a combat rule, so it is best understood as a charged seed of plant energy flung at a foe.

Gameplay: Gameplay: when Electro is applied to a Dendro Core, Hyperbloom triggers. The core turns into a Sprawling Shot that homes in on the nearest enemy and deals Dendro area damage on impact.

- The shot hits in a small radius of 1 m, compared with the 5 m burst of Burgeon, and the wiki lists it with increased damage over an ordinary Bloom core.
- If an enemy or the environment triggers it, the shot homes in on the closest ally instead. The wiki adds that the Lea Lotus Lamp made by the Dendro Traveler's Elemental Burst counts as a target for Hyperbloom in that case.
- The damage hits enemies and players alike; damage to players from Bloom-related reactions is 2% of the damage to enemies.
- It can be triggered by a party other than the one that made the Bloom, including the environment, and its damage scales with the party that applied the Electro.
- Hyperbloom is a transformative reaction: it does its own damage, based on the triggering character's level and Elemental Mastery, and ignores ATK and cannot critically strike unless a talent or constellation allows it.

- A target can take only two instances of damage from each Bloom-related reaction per source every 0.5 seconds, separately for each triggering character.
- Hyperbloom cannot be triggered on Bountiful Cores, the quick-bursting cores some abilities and event buffs make in place of ordinary Dendro Cores. They share the limit of five cores with normal ones.
- Electro is also the other half of the Quicken family: Electro on a Dendro-affected target starts Quicken, and Spread and Aggravate follow (own entries).

- Version 3.0 added the Dendro Elemental Resonance Sprawling Greenery, which gives nearby party members 20 Elemental Mastery for 6 seconds after Hyperbloom (or Spread, Aggravate, Burgeon), against 30 for Burning, Quicken or Bloom. The same patch adjusted the Electro Resonance High Voltage so that Hyperbloom has a guaranteed chance to generate an Electro Elemental Particle, with a 5-second cooldown.
- The wiki lists talents, constellations and artifacts that raise Hyperbloom damage, let it critically strike or add flat damage; these are character-specific and not detailed here.
- Lunar-Bloom (the Moonsign version of the Dendro-Hydro reaction, which the wiki says replaces Bloom) also spawns a core. Treat Lunar-Bloom as a separate reaction.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show a green, lumpy seed of energy hanging in the air, a crackle of lightning touching it, and the seed lunging away in a streak of sparking vines to strike a target. Keep it quick and precise rather than a huge blast.

It reads best as a team move: one person coaxes the seed out with water and plants, another sends a bolt into it. The seed seeks its target by itself, so it suits enemies that are spread out or hard to reach. Scale it to a skirmish.

Avoid having Hyperbloom work with no core present, avoid claiming a Dendro-only or Electro-only user can do it alone, and avoid giving it an origin story. Do not have the shot chase a target indefinitely or across a battlefield; it is a short-range homing burst.

Limits: Hyperbloom needs a Dendro Core, so it needs Bloom first. It does nothing to a Bountiful Core.

The shot can hurt the party too, though far less than it hurts enemies. The core vanishes after its duration if its creator has left the party.

Examples: Gameplay example: Hydro and Dendro together leave a Dendro Core. An Electro attack on it triggers Hyperbloom at once and a Sprawling Shot homes in on the nearest enemy.

139.content: The Sprawling Shot is the homing projectile that a Dendro Core becomes when Electro triggers Hyperbloom. It deals Dendro area damage in a small radius on impact and seeks the nearest enemy, or ally if an enemy or the environment set it off.

140.content: A Dendro Core is what the Bloom reaction (Dendro with Hydro) leaves behind. If left alone it bursts after about six seconds. Pyro on it triggers Burgeon, Electro triggers Hyperbloom. No more than five can exist at a time.

141.content:
Immortality and Resurrection (also: curse of immortality, Curse of Immortality, immortality in Teyvat, resurrection in Teyvat, Curse of Death, Elixir of Immortality): Teyvat has no single rule for avoiding death. Canon shows separate, bounded cases: the Curse of Immortality that Ronova, Ruler of Death, laid on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns 500 years ago; long-lived adepti, gods and dragons, who still die or erode; zombies such as Qiqi; and Natlan's conditional Ode of Resurrection.

Each case has a cost: the curse stops dying and ageing but not mental and spiritual decay; zombies lose memory or feeling; the Ode needs a victory and heals only fatal wounds. The Authorities of Life and Death, held by two of the Four Shades, are what Celestia polices.

As of 7.1, Ronova's Authority of Death has been reclaimed by Celestia and she is defeated, with her fate unconfirmed. Her Snezhnayan Curse of Death also showed that death in Teyvat is a process involving souls and the Ley Lines (see the Souls entry), not only the end of a body.

In universe: - Cursed immortality: pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns, by Ronova.
- Longevity: adepti, gods and dragons live for millennia but can die or be worn away.
- Zombification: adeptal energy (Qiqi) or an Elixir of Immortality (Jialiang).
- Resurrection: Natlan's Ode, for fallen Ancient Name bearers.

Ordinary people age and die; no source gives a human lifespan.

Ronova could define the form of death for any being, or deny it. Rhinedottir, who merged with Naberius, holds the Authority of Life among the Four Shades. Gods are not exempt from wearing down: erosion, which the Heavenly Principles built into the natural order and which tracks the flow of the Ley Lines, affects bodies, memory, will and spirit. Zhongli says the more powerful a being is, the more dangerous it becomes under erosion. Azhdaha, Ei (who built the Shogun to withstand it) and the Khaenri'ahns are the standard examples.

Curse of immortality: During the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Ronova cursed Khaenri'ah's pure-blooded people with immortality as a punishment. They cannot die or age, but they still erode. Khaenri'ahns of mixed or foreign descent were instead turned into monsters, per the wiki's reading of the story.

- Canon describes the curse as falling on the whole population, including those who knew nothing of the Five Sinners' use of Abyssal power.
- Many survivors, notably most of the Abyss Order, eventually became Abyss mages, heralds or lectors.
- The royal guards, the Black Serpents, became Shadowy Husks or stayed Black Serpents in a different form, still eroding. Halfdan kept his captain's face and orders for centuries and passed on only after Dainsleif acknowledged him in the Chasm.
- Rates of erosion vary. Some hilichurls knew of a fountain in the Chasm where they could "die" peacefully.
- Chlothar was driven fully insane by the curse and, the wiki says, is presumed dead in Avidya Forest after finding a way to break it. How is not given.

Pierro (the Jester) says that in the cataclysm he saw neither pity nor pleasure in Ronova's eyes while people begged for mercy, and that the curse created a feud "destined never to die." Dainsleif calls Ronova the architect of his torment over the last five hundred years.

Erosion and the curse: Dainsleif says the curse denies death but does not promise that those under it will never die: body and soul keep eroding until they are nearly nonexistent, even if death is not the form that erosion takes. His ring, a gift from his brother Vedrfolnir, continually resets his body's condition and lets him keep his memories better than other Khaenri'ahns, though his mind still erodes.

Erosion has four canon forms: mental (progressive loss of memory, clearest in Azhdaha), physical (deterioration, which led Ei to replace her body with a puppet), of the will, and of the spirit (loss of the sense of self, leading to feral behaviour or madness). It is imposed by the Heavenly Principles and may be connected to Istaroth, the Ruler of Time. Two attempts to stall it are recorded: Zhongli sharing power with Azhdaha, which failed, and Ei's Shogun.

In 7.1 Dainsleif says the battle with Ronova took an exceptionally heavy toll on the Jester's mind and soul, and that wielding such power always costs something irrecoverable. He also suggests that a fellow Khaenri'ahn's forgiving manner might be an attempt to resist erosion.

Capitano case: In Natlan's Archon Quest Ronova demanded Mavuika's life as the price for using her power against the Abyssal invasion. Capitano, a cursed Khaenri'ahn and the First Harbinger, offered his death instead, aiming to exploit the paradox: a being made unable to die by Ronova's own curse could not pay her price without forcing her to break one of her rules. Ronova chose to keep the Curse of Immortality, and Capitano's life force went into the Lord of the Night, who became essentially immortal. His body stayed on the Throne of the Primal Fire. As a result, souls from outside Natlan can now enter the Night Kingdom.

The wiki records that Capitano also aimed to save the souls of the dead by this substitution. How his own curse now stands is unstated. Do not extend the outcome to other Harbingers.

Ronova and authority: Ronova was the Ruler of Death among the Four Shades and Arbiter of the Heavenly Principles, a god whose existence predated any Archon. She let Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, borrow her power to set the rules of Natlan, on the understanding that she would deny involvement if the Heavenly Principles found out. Anyone who uses her power must eventually die. After Natlan's victory over the Abyss she honoured a bet by letting Xbalanque see present-day Natlan.

She also created the Maranasati Caskets that guard the Apathic Interval. The wiki further reads the Staff of Homa, which purified miasma in Liyue's Archon War era, as her gift; that is an inference from item text.

Curse of death: In Snezhnaya, Ronova spread a Curse of Death to stop technology that might threaten the Heavenly Principles, especially Project Mistilteinn. Whenever someone conceived such an idea, the curse killed them and everyone nearby for a short time. They revived with short-term memory loss, so researchers at the Armory Palace reported lost time, and Odette once found Mitya's body only to see him alive days later. Such killings broke the Heavenly Principles' rules, so Ronova and Rhinedottir used a loophole: kill, then resurrect within a window before Celestia's monitoring cycle noticed.

In the Wraith's Nocturne quest (7.0) the Curse of Death killed everyone in the Korolevskiy Theater. Its Ley Lines had been modified by angels so that they could take only two souls a day, which left the dead stranded in an afterlife that felt like a blizzard outside the theater. Ronova, disguised as the dead Alyosha, killed two people a night. When the Traveler and Mitya exposed her and destroyed the disguise, everyone in the theater woke up alive. In 7.1 Rhinedottir's resurrection could not be carried out in time because the Tsaritsa had used her six Gnoses to tamper with space and time around Rhinedottir. Celestia detected the aberration, reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death and undid the unauthorised curse. Rhinedottir noted she would rather not lose her Authority of Life too.

Ronova status: As of 7.1 Ronova has been defeated. Pierro (the Jester), the Traveler and Dainsleif fought her after Celestia took back her Authority. The Jester spent his own soul and life force on the final strike, a summoned elemental nail. A portal was closing in the crater afterwards. Even without her Authority she still had power befitting a Shade. The Fatui count it as their victory, and the Snezhnayan blockade on technology ended with it.

Zombies: A zombie is a person brought back from death, usually cold and stiff, with talismans to hold the state. Qiqi was never awakened by anyone and gives herself orders. She has poor memory, little expression, no sense of smell, prefers cold, and her flesh decays in heat. Jialiang, revived by Baizhu's Elixir of Immortality, is the only other known zombie.

Qiqi's story: an ordinary herb-picker caught in a clash between adepti and demons in Liyue, near death, who received a Vision in her last moments. The adepti each gave her a portion of strength to keep her alive. It was too much for a mortal, so she went berserk and Mountain Shaper sealed her in amber. Hundreds of years later humans found the amber and carried it toward the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor; the seal weakened on the road and she woke, escaped and met Baizhu, who took her in.
- She does calisthenics daily so that rigor mortis does not make her hop.
- In combat she drops her restraint and her undead strength and speed come out.
- She forgets a person within about three days unless she reinforces the memory; she writes things in a notebook and sometimes forgets to read it. Her self-given orders can be cancelled by an honest hug.
- Her appearance is fixed at the moment of her death, so her age cannot be estimated reliably.

During Baizhu's Story Quest "The Heart of Healing" (3.6), after Jiangli's god-remains treatment for Jialiang's rare heart condition was ended, Baizhu used the elixir on him. He woke at Bubu Pharmacy under talismans and, unlike Qiqi, kept his memory and speech. Baizhu did not know how long it would hold; the family left for Natlan hoping its hot springs would help. Baizhu's long pursuit of eternal life is said to be so that he can protect himself and Changsheng; Qiqi's Character Story ties his taking her in to his own pursuits.

Adepti and longevity: The adepti are very long-lived but not immortal. Liyue still holds the Rite of Parting, a memorial service run by Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, for each adeptus who passes, though it has been needed only a handful of times in three thousand years.

Legend says some adepti, tired of waiting for a natural end, asked Morax to turn them into stone statues. Adeptal energy endangers mortals because their souls are less robust, which is also what overwhelmed Qiqi. Adepti arts include Dream Trawler, which separates the soul from the body, and Pervases's Mortal Lingering, which lets a spirit regain a physical vessel for a short time.

Ode of resurrection: In Natlan the Ode of Resurrection, a ceremony at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, raises Ancient Name bearers who died fighting the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars, provided their group achieved victory. The Pyro Archon enters the Sacred Flame to seek the deceased and their name in the Night Kingdom while the crowd sings. It heals fatal injuries only, and its power comes from Ronova.

Kachina's Ode failed: Mavuika came out alone and said neither Kachina nor her Ancient Name could be found in the Night Kingdom. Abyssal unrest was blocking it, so she suspended the Pilgrimage. A bearer who dies in defeat and is not resurrected loses the name; one who dies otherwise is eventually reborn in Natlan in a different form. After the six Heroes of Natlan gathered, Mavuika briefly called on the Lord of the Night's power to extend the Ode to every Natlanese warrior, nameless or not, and casualties effectively dropped to zero. When the Sacred Flame faltered during the assault on the Abyss, Kachina began the Ode spontaneously to send the nation's support, re-empowering the Flame. The ceremony was discontinued after the Night Wars.

The melody and lyrics are an excerpt of the Natlan soundtrack and are sung in Swahili. After he defeated Xiuhcoatl, Xbalanque was said to have been "revived from the flames" (legend). Pyro Archons begin as ordinary humans who win the position by combat, so they remain mortal.

Other returns: In the Liyue Story Quest "A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon" (Version Luna IV, 6.3), once the shadowmoon vanished, the Traveler and Zhongli reunited the three fragments of Zibai's divided soul and restored her. This is a unique, quest-specific act, not a general method.

In 7.1 the Traveler is sent to the afterlife by Ronova's curse and escapes with a Seal of Life formed from their memories, used by Vesna through the Authority of Life. This is a bounded act within one story scene, not a general rule.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): fallen party members can be revived at a Statue of The Seven or with a dish. No story source treats these as literal in-world resurrection.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat any return from death as costly and conditional. A Khaenri'ahn survivor should feel tired, not triumphant; a zombie should show cold, stiffness or forgetfulness; an adeptus's death is a rare, formal event.

Do not offer the Ode as a service outside Natlan. Do not let an ordinary character cast the Curse of Immortality or Death, which are Authority-level acts.

Avoid portraying the curse as invulnerability: the cursed can be hurt, exhausted and defeated; canon says only that they do not die. Do not claim that Dainsleif or any named Khaenri'ahn has a way to end the curse unless the scene's canon says so.

Limits: No source describes a way to undo the Curse of Immortality, and no resurrection is unconditional.

Ronova could not simply break her own rules (Capitano's paradox), and when she exceeded the limits Celestia permitted, it reclaimed her Authority. The Ode needs victory, a name, a fatal wound and a Pyro Archon willing to enter the flame.

Zombies need orders to act (Qiqi's self-given ones can lock her into a task), and adeptal energy that revives a mortal can overwhelm her. Canon records no proven remedy for erosion, so every long-lived being, god or mortal, faces a limit.

142.comment: Immortality and Resurrection: Curse of Immortality
142.content: Ronova, the Ruler of Death, cursed the pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. They cannot die or age but are not shielded from erosion, which gradually dissolves memory, will and spirit. Dainsleif and Capitano are among the cursed. As of 7.1, Ronova's Authority is reclaimed, but the characters who live with the curse still treat it as active.

143.comment: Immortality and Resurrection: Curse of Death
143.content: Ronova's Snezhnaya curse that killed anyone developing dangerous technology and their surroundings, then returned them to life with memory loss. It worked with Rhinedottir's Authority of Life and a resurrection window before Celestia's monitoring cycle. In 7.1 the window passed, Celestia reclaimed the Authority of Death and the curse was undone.

144.comment: Immortality and Resurrection: Elixir of Immortality
144.content: Baizhu's elixir turned the dying Jialiang into a zombie in the 3.6 Story Quest "The Heart of Healing". Unlike Qiqi, Jialiang kept his speech and memory; the wiki guesses this is because the elixir does not use adeptus arts. Its duration is unknown.

145.comment: Immortality and Resurrection: Rite of Parting
145.content: A Liyue memorial service for the passing of an adeptus, run by Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. It has been simplified over time and has been needed only a few times in three thousand years, so adepti are best described as long-lived rather than immortal.

146.comment: Immortality and Resurrection: Authority of Life
146.content: Rhinedottir merged with Naberius and holds the Authority of Life among the Four Shades. The wiki says her creations draw on it and gain a degree of immortality. In 7.1 she says she would rather not have the Authority reclaimed too, and complies with Celestia's directive to rectify Ronova's mistake by resurrecting the people Ronova killed.

147.content:
Karma (also: karmic debt, divine karma, bad karma, karma of the yakshas): Karma, or karmic debt, is the corruptive residue left by the wills and powers of ancient gods slain in the Archon War. It seeps into land, monsters and people, and can drive humans mad. The yakshas were called by Rex Lapis to destroy it, and absorbed so much of it that most died or went insane. As of 7.1 the sole surviving yaksha, Xiao, still bears it.

The term is used mainly in Liyue. Adepti can make a medicine that temporarily eases karma, but like most adeptal medicines it is lethal to mortals.

In universe: During the Archon War, Morax subdued many gods. Their hatred and powers lingered in the world as half-awake remnants that corrupted land, spawned monsters and caused pestilence, miasma and mutations. Contact with karma can make humans insane and makes monsters stronger.

Morax summoned the yakshas, especially fierce illuminated beasts, to fight these remnants. As Zhongli narrates in the cinematic of Glimmers of the Vigilant Yaksha, they swore to restore order through slaughter, but each kill left a mark: the debt wore into their souls, and they went mad with fear, turned on each other or were lost to the darkness. Of the five foremost yakshas, three died and Bosacius vanished, leaving Xiao as the only one.

Xiao's profile gives the most personal account. When he cut down the manifestations of slain gods' revenge, he fractured their hatred, and the fragments eventually tainted his own soul. The only way to remove such hatred is to accept the karmic debt it brings, and the debt he has accumulated is enough to consume flesh, bone and soul. His story says he feels no hatred himself: after more than two thousand years no single debt is more than a fleeting memory. Because his surroundings are tainted too, he avoids people, since human souls are less robust than adepti ones.

The gods' hatred does not stay quiet. It sometimes erupts with abnormal force in its half-dreaming state, and the worst eruption of all is at the Lantern Rite, so Xiao fights day and night then, performing the Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering, and has come to dislike the festival. Many human festivals recall days when adepti defeated man-eating monsters, and later generations turned the exorcism rites into celebrations. A chapter called "Ode to Windborne Wraith" in a Sumeru scholar's folklore book records that the yakshas were bound by their own karma to suffer horrors, and lists comforts such as food offerings and holy chants.

Effects and resistance: Karma corrupts monsters and strengthens them, and can send humans insane. Yelan's clan story adds that her ancestor found temporary relief from his insanity only near the Wangshu Inn. Vision holders have heightened resistance, as do the Traveler and illuminated beasts; in the adepti's view, a Vision is a valid form of illumination.

The hazard persists in places: the Karma-Heavy Cavern is a quest domain in The Purging of Evil, named for the heavy karma it holds. Karma also wore at the yakshas' minds; Bosacius saw several comrades kill each other and went mad himself, forgetting his own name and fighting beside the Millelith at the Chasm in the cataclysm as the "Nameless Yaksha."

Relief and remedies: Remedies are partial. Adepti alchemy yields Remedium Tertiorum, which Zhongli once asked a traveler to pass to Xiao, but it can be lethal to mortals. Venti once relieved Xiao's pain by playing the flute through the night, which Xiao's profile describes as quieting his wild senses; the Liyue legend of the sound of a flute among the reeds near Dihua Marsh is tied to this. The Qixing built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh to give Xiao a place to rest, and he eats Almond Tofu there.

A fragment of Yelan's family tradition says Xiao's presence near the inn eased her ancestor's madness, and her voice-over says she would fight beside him with her focus on the mission, not on his status. The Nuo Dance, which purges demons and divine karma, costs its user great suffering in return for the strength to subdue a god's might, according to the wiki.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Xiao remains the last yaksha and still carries the karmic debt. No release up to the cutoff resolves or removes karma, and no canon source says it has been cured.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): karma appears in Xiao's character materials and quests such as The Purging of Evil, the Karma-Heavy Cavern domain, and the idle quotes of Xiao as a companion, one of which is simply "Karma..." There is no general karma mechanic in the open world.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat karma as a heavy, quiet burden rather than a spell. Xiao keeps people away, speaks little of it and does not ask for pity; the yaksha's own line in the profile says yakshas need no sympathy or tears. Show it through weariness, sudden pain, cold sweat or a distant, haunted look, not melodrama.

Do not make everyone in Liyue aware of karma or the yakshas; the story says few know Xiao's role. Do not have ordinary Visions "cure" it. The only canon relief is Remedium Tertiorum and a flute song.

Avoid suggesting Xiao hates humans; canon says he is gentle and curious about people but avoids them for their sake. Keep his guilt tied to the yakshas' oath and his own deeds. Do not extend karma into Natlan, Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya scenes unless a scene is explicitly Liyue-related.

148.content: The yakshas were fierce illuminated beasts summoned by Morax to destroy the lingering hatred of defeated gods. Five stood foremost: Bosacius the eldest and leader, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus (Xiao). Accumulated karma destroyed them. Bonanus, Indarias and Menogias died, Bosacius went mad and vanished, and Alatus alone remains.

149.content: An adeptal medicine that Zhongli gave to the Traveler to pass to Xiao. It can temporarily ease karma, but nothing in the world can withstand its power, and like other adeptal medicines it is lethal to mortals, so he warned that Paimon must not eat them.

150.content: An inn at Dihua Marsh built at least five hundred years ago by the Liyue Qixing to give Xiao somewhere to stay and rest while he does his duty. It is run by Qixing agents Verr Goldet and Huai'an.

151.content:
Khvarena (also: Spirit Light, Khvarena of flowers, the Khvarena, Great Khvarena): Khvarena is a pure, divine energy of Sumeru. Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, made it for one purpose: to oppose the cataclysm she foresaw. Its divine nature lets it purify Abyssal energy and Forbidden Knowledge. She called the first Khvarena her innocent, pure daughter and gave it to Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who shaped it into the divine bird Simurgh. When the Abyss began to corrupt the Amrita, Simurgh shattered her form into countless motes of Khvarena. The only sentient ones became the Pari.

The name is a Zoroastrian term for divine glory or radiance, and game texts use the word loosely: for the original being (spoken of as feminine), for the countless entities she became when she divided, and for the abstract quality of light and favour ("do not let your Khvarena dim"). Related Sumeru items include the Vourukasha's Glow artifact set and the Great Songs of Khvarena.

In universe: Khvarena is not presented as an element and is not tied to a Vision. It is an energy of divine life and purity, opposed to the darkness of the Abyss. It exists in many forms: wild motes in the Girdle of the Sands, the Pari, Plumes of Purifying Light and orbs of coalesced light that can raise barriers.

The origin is told in two ways. A legend relayed by Sethos says Rukkhadevata received the Khvarena as a gift at the first Sabzeruz Festival. The artifact texts of Vourukasha's Glow instead show Nabu Malikata handing over a shard of her own being, after a dream of a faceless nightmare (the cataclysm), asking Rukkhadevata to keep it safe until the day the Abyss rises to drown life. Both agree on the purpose: to blunt a disaster that Nabu foresaw.

Khvarena has a built-in destiny of sacrifice. Nabu's words in the artifact text tell it that it will face "the trial of division and death", then become immortal, which she calls a harder road. Item text also treats withering and rebirth as the shape of Khvarena's meaning: things born from the Khvarena of flowers wither, and are then reborn, nourished by the Amrita, no longer troubled by death.

The texts carry some unusual wording. Khvarena is called a "point in the flower's heart, a single drop of light in a sea of sweet dew". Nabu says it comes from "the wisdom of the flowers and the veins of the skies" and holds the pure essence of life. A scholar's note found in the desert, partly redacted, argues that Khvarena resembles the Abyss in one structural way: it assimilates whatever energy and material it touches and has a kind of self-recognition, though it is opposed to the Abyss's energy. This is one writer's inference and canon does not confirm it.

Origins: Nabu Malikata, one of the three companion-gods of the old desert kingdom, foresaw the cataclysm. She separated a piece of her own being, called it her innocent and pure daughter, and gave it to her friend Greater Lord Rukkhadevata to protect and to use against the coming darkness. After Nabu and King Deshret died, Rukkhadevata, per the artifact texts, turned the Khvarena into a divine bird.

Rukkhadevata shaped the Khvarena into a beautiful form: the divine bird Simurgh. The texts say she charged her with the protection of two worlds and the guardianship of "the border between new birth and death". Simurgh lived among pines, cypresses and snow-lotuses and slept until disaster came. The artifact texts present Rukkhadevata's act as the keeping of a pact with her fallen friends.

Each piece of Vourukasha's Glow tells part of this story in verse from a different side, and the details sometimes differ, so it is best treated as in-world legend. The Flower of Life piece is Nabu speaking to the Khvarena; the Sands piece has Nabu asking Rukkhadevata to guard the Khvarena; the Goblet piece has the Khvarena speaking of itself as the remnant of its mistress. The core events agree.

Simurgh and the pari: When the cataclysm came, the Amrita (made from the remains of Egeria, the earlier Hydro Archon, slain in the upheaval) began to be corrupted by the Abyss. To save it, Simurgh flew into the pool and shattered her form, becoming countless motes of Khvarena. These formed the Vourukasha Oasis, a sea of flowers. The only motes with intelligence became the Pari, who consider their god to be Egeria, whose consciousness lies in the Harvisptokhm.

Pari live in the Vourukasha Oasis. Each is said to have a fated responsibility to carry out alone. At the end of its life a Pari turns into a Plume of Purifying Light, which should be returned to the Amrita Pool. A Pari stained by Abyssal corruption is rejected by the Oasis and turns into a Fravashi Tree, so the humans who bond with Pari (called Yasnapati) are charged with bringing them home. Wiki listings also name Sunyata Flowers and Farrwicks as descendants of Simurgh.

In The Hymn of Tir Yazad, the Pari are said to have fought the cataclysm alongside Khaenri'ahn warriors (a masked swordsman and a one-armed sage) and Akademiya scholars who later became the Order of Skeptics. In the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests, Zurvan, an elder Pari, says that the Pari alone were given intelligence among all the motes, so they can speak with what remains of the mother-tree's consciousness and guide Khvarena's power.

Great songs: Zurvan says that, in the past, she used the Khvarena to repair the seal that held back the darkness and fused the strongest Khvarena into five Great Songs to purify the land. Item and tutorial text describe them as the physical form of Khvarena's might, which create barriers; only a Pari with the Twin-Horned Chaplet, the symbol of Khvarena's recognition, can touch them. Sorush, who is given the Chaplet, goes with the Traveler to collect them.

In As the Khvarena's Light Shows, the Great Songs lie in hard-to-reach places in the Girdle of the Sands, including a ruined Dahrian factory underground. Nasejuna, who joined the search, turns on the party and says the Songs could reverse the Rite of Chinvat and release the Abyss seal. He and Klingsor of the Abyss Order demand the Songs, and the party refuses and takes them back to Zurvan.

The party notes that the Songs have little effect near a petrified Setekh Wenut, which suggests to Nasejuna that Khvarena acts only on things connected to the Abyss. The Songs belong to the wider effort, in the Hymn of Tir Yazad quests, to deal with the Sign of Apaosha, which Sorush had sworn to destroy.

Known uses: Purifying: cleansing Abyssal energy and Forbidden Knowledge, and repairing seals against the Abyss. Raising barriers. Giving life to the Vourukasha Oasis.

In Sorush's hands, orbs of coalesced Khvarena in the desert can be woken to expand a barrier that deflects incoming attacks. Pari can use their link to Khvarena to guide its power. Plumes of Purifying Light can be offered to the Amrita Pool.

- Small Khvarena creatures, floating motes sometimes called mayflies, appear around tree stumps in the Girdle of the Sands as a catching challenge.
- Zurvan's account in the quests says Khvarena has been used to repair the seal over the darkness and to fuse the Great Songs.
- Item text for Plume of Purifying Light calls it a fragment left by Khvarena, a carrier of past memories.

An Ode to Khvarena is a text found in the House of Daena, said to be lore passed down within a lost religious group of the desert. It recalls the Khvarena as the glorious aid of the Lord of Wisdom scattered in endless forms, and invokes Nagarjuna with a vow to cleanse the sinless and let them be reborn in a pure land.

Limits: Khvarena is not unlimited. Its sentient form, the Pari, lives out a fated duty and ends as a plume; the great form, Simurgh, gave up her shape. It cannot cleanse every taint: a Pari that is corrupted is rejected by the Oasis and becomes a tree.

Only a Pari with the Chaplet can handle the Great Songs. Their effect, in the quest, did not extend to things not tied to the Abyss. Canon shows no ordinary person wielding Khvarena as a power.

Do not treat Khvarena as proof against all Abyssal threats; the cataclysm still devastated Sumeru and the Abyss Order remained active there.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Khvarena appears as exploration content in the Girdle of the Sands, including Khvarena Mayflies, Khvarena Barrier orbs, Plumes of Purifying Light and Great Songs, all tied to Sorush's gadget and the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests. The artifact set Vourukasha's Glow carries its lore in item texts.

Vourukasha's Glow gives HP +20% for two pieces; at four, Elemental Skill and Elemental Burst DMG rises 10%, with an additional 80% after the wearer takes damage, for up to five stacks. Plumes of Purifying Light are offered to the Amrita Pool for rewards; 36 can be found in the Girdle of the Sands.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray Khvarena as soft, clean light, the feel of petals, dew and clear water, not as a weapon. Pari speak of it as a sacred inheritance and a duty.

Keep it tied to sacrifice and renewal: a bright thing that gives itself up and is reborn. Do not let a Khvarena user become an unbeatable hero or simply overwrite the Abyss. Ordinary Sumeru residents are unlikely to know the full tale of Nabu Malikata and Simurgh.
