Avoid calling Khvarena an element, a Gnosis or an Archon power. Do not give Khvarena to people outside the Pari lineage beyond what the quests show (Sorush's Chaplet and gadget).

152.content: Simurgh was the divine bird made when Greater Lord Rukkhadevata gave a shape to the Khvarena that Nabu Malikata had entrusted to her. She slept until the cataclysm, then shattered her form in the Amrita Pool to purify it, becoming countless motes of Khvarena. The Pari descend from her. See her own entry for details.

153.content: The Pari are avian, flower-like descendants of Simurgh who live in the Vourukasha Oasis in the Girdle of the Sands. They are the only sentient form of Khvarena, each with a fated duty. When their life ends they become Plumes of Purifying Light, to be returned to the Amrita Pool. Tainted Pari turn into Fravashi Trees. Humans bonded with Pari are called Yasnapati.

154.content: Five concentrated forms of Khvarena, fused by Zurvan from the strongest Khvarena collected in the flower sea to purify the land. Only a Pari carrying the Twin-Horned Chaplet can touch them. In the Khvarena of Good and Evil quests, Sorush and the Traveler gather them; Nasejuna, with the Abyss Order, tries to seize them.

155.content: Vourukasha's Glow is an artifact set whose five pieces tell the legend of Khvarena in verse: Nabu Malikata's farewell to her daughter, Rukkhadevata's pact, Simurgh's birth, the corruption of the Amrita and the founding of the flower sea. The pieces are Stamen of Khvarena's Origin, Vibrant Pinion, Ancient Abscission, Feast of Boundless Joy and Heart of Khvarena's Brilliance. Treat the texts as poetic legend; they do not always agree on small details.

156.content:
Kresnik Kristall (also: Kristall, Kresnik's Torch, Kresnik Torch, Kresnik Energy): Kresnik Kristall is the crystalline ore that keeps Snezhnaya warm. Burned in furnaces called Kresnik's Torches, it gives off heat efficiently, and every Snezhnayan city is built around one such torch. The ore is mined chiefly in Novokitezhgrad and shipped across the nation by rail.

The Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya oversees both the torches and the Kristall's transport and use. In gameplay the Eye of Graeae turns Kresnik Energy from Kristall and torches into protection against the cold.

In universe: Most Snezhnayan settlements need Kresnik Kristall to survive. Before the torches existed, the Eye of Graeae says, the land was made only of Frigid and Subzero Zones and unfit for human life.

A torch holds a Normal Temperature Zone within a certain range and shields a city from snowstorms. Small civilian-model torches also stand across the countryside. Villages without a rail stop depend on deliveries; in "Gunfire in the Silent Lands" a character from the village of Alatyr fears that if Kristall deliveries have stopped there, the villagers will freeze.

Snezhnaya's most important torch is in Kresnik's Burning Heart, a chamber under the central plaza of Snezhnograd. The wiki, citing an NPC of the Energy Commission, says it was built almost immediately after the Belyi Tsar completed his experiments in the Pale Crown Palace, where prototype torches remain. Loading-screen text states the Belyi Tsar created Kresnik's Torch to help humans survive the cold.

Zones form a scale: Normal Temperature, Cold, Frigid and Subzero. Settlements and warm places such as Flamefeather Valley are Normal; the edges of the map are Subzero. Who tended the earliest torches, and how the Commission arose, is not covered in canon read here (the Commission's history is blank on the wiki).

Origin: The Kristall is said to come from power released when the Cryo Dragon Sovereign lost control in Snezhnaya. A potion formula found in a world quest calls the ore the ideal material, as power refined from the authority released by a colossal beast of ages past that lost control.

In "An Ark That Used to Be a Soul" (7.0), Aksinya explains that after the Cryo Dragon's corpse and unchecked authority turned Snezhnaya into Holy Soil of primordial ice, even the ley lines became veins of pure crystal, until the Heavenly Principles sent down a Celestial Nail. The wiki dates the event to about 6,000 years ago and infers that today's large deposits are remnants of that change.

Legend, as told by the Kristall Bug's archive entry, says early Snezhnayans found the rich ore beneath the frozen land by following the trails of Kristall Bugs, whose shells resemble the ore, and built a civilisation from it.

Known uses: Burned in a Kresnik's Torch, Kristall provides heat. Gameplay (not literal lore): each ore deposit and many torches release Kresnik Energy that the Eye of Graeae uses to keep the Traveler from Sheer Cold.

Gameplay: mini torches release energy orbs at intervals and need a small amount of Kresnik Energy to activate; medium torches only release pickup orbs, and some are decorative. Kristall ore is mined by attacks, yields a fixed amount of energy and respawns after a short time. Catching a Kristall Bug also gives energy.

Limits: Do not treat the ore as a source of elemental power for combat or as Cryo itself; canon describes its use as heat and energy for survival. Do not claim a character can make Kristall by Cryo or Pyro power.

Do not state that the Fatui, the Tsaritsa or the Harbingers command the supply directly; oversight belongs to the Royal Energy Commission and the rail bureau transports it.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): in Snezhnaya, warmth is a civic fact. Characters notice how far a torch reaches, speak of stove-fuel and coal-like shipments, and feel a rail delay as a danger rather than an inconvenience. Foreigners are surprised that a Snezhnayan town is built around a heat source.

Villages without a station worry about deliveries; city-dwellers take the torch for granted. Do not make the torches magical wonders to locals; they are everyday infrastructure.

157.content: A furnace that burns Kresnik Kristall for heat. Large torches anchor cities, small civilian ones stand across the land, and the most important sits in Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd. Prototype torches remain at the Pale Crown Palace. The Royal Energy Commission maintains them.

158.comment: Kresnik Kristall: Royal Energy Commission of Snezhnaya
158.content: The Commission, seated in Snezhnograd, maintains the torches and manages the transport and use of the Kristall. Its acting chair is Zarechnaya; members include Mitya, Yelagina and Zaretsky. Its history is not documented in canon read here.

159.content: A beetle found near Snezhnayan mines whose shell resembles the ore. Local lore says people first found the deposits by following these bugs' trails.

160.content:
Lunar-Bloom (also: Lunar Bloom, Lunar-Bloom reaction, Verdant Dew): Lunar-Bloom is the Lunar Reaction between Dendro and Hydro, in either order. When the party includes a character whose Moonsign Benediction passive enables it, ordinary Bloom is replaced by Lunar-Bloom. By itself it does no damage. Instead it gives the party Verdant Dew, a stored resource certain characters spend to deal Lunar-Bloom damage, which can crit. It arrived in Version 6.0 (Luna I) with Nod-Krai.

The Dendro Cores and Bountiful Cores that the reaction still creates are identical to those from Bloom. Damage from those cores is not counted as Lunar-Bloom damage.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. Verdant Dew and Lunar-Bloom are shown in tutorials and combat, not discussed by characters in the sources read. Treat them as a gameplay abstraction.

Related setting: the reaction came with the Nod-Krai region and the Moonsign party bonus. It replaces Bloom, the Dendro and Hydro reaction from Version 3.0.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Lunar-Bloom does no damage on its own. The only ways to deal Lunar-Bloom damage are certain character talents and constellations, which spend Verdant Dew.

- After Lunar-Bloom triggers, the party gains 1 Verdant Dew every 2.5 seconds for 2.5 seconds. The party can hold up to 3.
- Triggering Lunar-Bloom again while dew is being gained resets the duration.
- Verdant Dew lasts indefinitely. It persists through party changes, teleports between maps and domains, daily resets and game sessions.

- Lunar-Bloom damage uses the shared Lunar formula with a base reaction coefficient of 1. It applies only when a talent deals it directly, so the elemental mastery bonus is 6 x EM / (EM + 2000) on top of any reaction bonus.
- The wiki lists Lauma (Nature's Chorus, a burst that deals Lunar-Bloom in up to 36 instances, and Constellation 2), Nefer (Dusklit Eaves) and Columbina as Moonsign sources of Lunar-Bloom bonus, and Baizhu and Aino as providing reaction bonus.
- Increases come from artifacts and weapons such as Flower of Paradise Lost, Night of the Sky's Unveiling, Silken Moon's Serenade, Blackmarrow Lantern and Nightweaver's Looking Glass.

- Sprawling Greenery resonance (two Dendro characters) gives party members Elemental Mastery for a short time after Lunar-Bloom triggers.
- Event and mode boosts have applied to it: the 6.0 notes list 75% Lunar-Bloom boosts alongside 200% Bloom boosts in the same half of a limited-time mode.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present Lunar-Bloom as the same seed-like burst as Bloom with an added pale shine, and Verdant Dew as small drops that gather and are spent. Keep it tied to a team that includes a Moonsign Benediction user.

Because the dew is stored and carried between fights and sessions, a scene may show characters keeping a little of it after a battle. This is an interpretation of the gameplay rule, not something canon narrates.

Do not claim Verdant Dew is a real substance sold or gathered by Nod-Krai residents, or that Lauma invented the reaction. Neither is stated in the sources read.

Limits: Lunar-Bloom does not deal damage when it triggers; the dew must be spent by a character that can use it.

Dew caps at 3. Dendro Core and Bountiful Core damage is not Lunar-Bloom damage.

Without a Moonsign Benediction character, Dendro meeting Hydro is plain Bloom.

161.content: Verdant Dew is the resource Lunar-Bloom grants: 1 every 2.5 seconds for 2.5 seconds after the reaction, up to 3, never expiring. Certain characters consume it to deal Lunar-Bloom damage to enemies.

162.content:
Lunar-Charged (also: Lunar Charged, Lunar-Charged reaction, thundercloud reaction): Lunar-Charged is the Lunar Reaction between Electro and Hydro. When the two meet on a target and the party includes a character whose Moonsign Benediction passive enables it, the usual Electro-Charged is replaced by Lunar-Charged. The reaction forms a thundercloud that keeps firing lightning at nearby enemies carrying both Electro and Hydro. Its damage can crit. It was the first Lunar Reaction, arriving in Version 5.8 alongside Ineffa.

Unlike Electro-Charged, the damage is based on every character who applied an element during the reaction, so the whole party shares in it. The damage is Electro.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. The thundercloud is shown only in tutorial and combat material. Treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow as a storm gathering over a fight.

Related setting: Ineffa, the character who introduced the reaction, is a 5-star Electro polearm user, and the reaction came out in 5.8, before the Nod-Krai region opened in 6.0. The wiki also lists a Genius Invokation TCG summon called Thundercloud created by Lunar-Charged; that is a card game effect, not a story event.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): the thundercloud deals Electro damage to all Wet enemies who are also affected by Electro within roughly 5 m, every 2 seconds. A target that has not been hit in the last 2 seconds and is Wet or Electro-affected is struck at once when the other aura lands on it.

- Each strike uses up 0.4 gauge units of the Wet and Electro auras together.
- The cloud lasts 6 seconds, which resets if another Lunar-Charged triggers. Only one cloud exists at a time; triggering outside its range makes a new one and removes the old one.
- Thunderclouds try to position themselves between active targets and the triggering party.

- Lunar-Charged shares all other properties of Electro-Charged, including damaging the wards of Hydrogunner Legionnaires at a higher rate.
- Damage is dealt indirectly (by applying elements) or directly by a talent. The base reaction coefficient is 3 in both cases. The elemental mastery bonus is 6 x EM / (EM + 2000).
- A party member with a Moonsign Benediction turns the reaction on; the wiki lists Ineffa (Assemblage Hub), Flins (Old World Secrets) and Columbina as providing a Lunar-Charged base damage bonus, up to 14% for the first two and up to 7% for Columbina.
- Artifact sets and weapons such as Night of the Sky's Unveiling, Silken Moon's Serenade and Bloodsoaked Ruins increase Lunar-Charged damage.

- High Voltage resonance (two Electro characters) gives Lunar-Charged a 100% chance to generate an Electro particle, with a 5-second cooldown.
- Event and mode buffs have boosted it: the 5.8 notes show a 75% increase to Electro-Charged and Lunar-Charged damage in one half of a limited-time mode, and the 6.0 notes show similar 75% boosts in two halves of another.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show a small, low thundercloud that follows the fight, flickers when Electro and water are on the same enemy, and drops short bolts. Keep it a visible, compact storm rather than a weather event. Reserve it for scenes with an Electro user and a Hydro user.

Because everyone who applied an element contributes, narrate it as a team effort: one person soaks, another sparks, and the cloud answers both. No named character in the sources read calls the effect by its game name in dialogue.

Do not give the cloud a will or intelligence, and do not present it as Ineffa's personal invention; the wiki ties its availability to Moonsign Benediction talents, not to a story event.

Limits: The cloud only strikes enemies that carry both Electro and Hydro (Wet), and only one cloud can exist at a time.

Without a Moonsign Benediction character who enables it, Electro meeting Hydro simply makes the ordinary Electro-Charged.

The 5 m reach is flagged on the wiki as unconfirmed. Range and tick figures belong to the game mechanic and should not be quoted in story as exact distances.

163.content: A thundercloud is the object created by a Lunar-Charged reaction. It lasts 6 seconds, drifts between targets and the triggering party, and fires Electro damage at nearby enemies that are both Wet and affected by Electro. A Genius Invokation TCG summon shares the name.

164.content:
Lunar-Crystallize (also: Lunar Crystallize, Lunar-Crystallize reaction, Moondrift Harmony): Lunar-Crystallize is the Lunar Reaction between Geo and Hydro. When the party includes a character whose Moonsign Benediction passive enables it, Hydro Crystallize is replaced by Lunar-Crystallize, which creates three Moondrifts around the target. Every third Lunar-Crystallize while Moondrifts are present sets them resonating in Moondrift Harmony, a tracking projectile that deals Geo damage and can crit. It arrived in Version 6.3 (Luna IV).

As with the other Lunar Reactions, the damage is based on every character who applied an element during the reaction, and it can also be dealt directly by a talent. The wiki treats Moondrifts as Geo constructs.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. Moondrifts and Moondrift Harmony appear in tutorial and combat material only. Treat them as a gameplay abstraction.

Related setting: the reaction came to the Nod-Krai-themed Moonsign family later than Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Bloom. The wiki's announcement images for it describe it as Hydro and Geo meeting again under the moonlight; that wording is the announcement's, not a statement about the story world.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): triggering Lunar-Crystallize makes three Moondrifts near the target. While at least one is on the field, each third Lunar-Crystallize makes them resonate and fire a projectile that tracks the target for Geo damage.

- The wiki classes Moondrifts as Geo constructs.
- The tutorial says triggering the reaction three times starts Moondrift Harmony, which hits nearby opponents with Geo damage.
- Damage can crit and is shared across contributing characters who applied Geo or Hydro.

- Lunar-Crystallize uses the shared Lunar formula. Its base reaction coefficient is 1.6 in both indirect and direct damage, and the elemental mastery bonus is 6 x EM / (EM + 2000).
- The wiki lists Zibai (The Coursing Sun and Moon) and Linnea (Habitat Survey) for up to 14% Lunar-Crystallize base bonus, Columbina for up to 7%, and Aino's Constellation 6 for a reaction bonus.
- The wiki keeps category tables of artifacts, weapons, talents and constellations that raise Lunar-Crystallize damage; they are not copied here.

- Enduring Rock resonance (two Geo characters) gives extra benefits when Moondrifts are nearby: 15% more damage dealt and a 20% Geo RES reduction on enemies for 15 seconds after damaging them.
- Limited-time mode boosts in 6.3 reached Lunar-Crystallize: the notes list a 75% Lunar-Crystallize boost for one half of a mode and a True DMG shockwave when a character deals Lunar-Crystallize damage, once every 3 seconds. A fix in the same notes corrected an earlier case where the Floor 9 and 10 Lunar boost of 50% missed Lunar-Crystallize.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show three small floating stones circling a foe that glow pale and then fly together in a single strike. Keep them small; they are summoned by a reaction, not a landslide.

The three-then-strike rhythm suits a team pattern: two hits to set the stones turning, the third to release them. Narrate who contributed Geo and who contributed water, since both count.

Do not claim Moondrifts are fragments of a moon or related to the Three Moons. The sources read say neither, and the name is only a game term.

Limits: Without a Moonsign Benediction character who enables it, Geo meeting Hydro is ordinary Hydro Crystallize.

Moondrift Harmony needs Moondrifts on the field and fires only on every third Lunar-Crystallize.

Moondrifts are Geo constructs for the game's rules but have no stated in-world nature; do not give them one.

165.content: A Moondrift is one of three objects a Lunar-Crystallize creates near the target. While they are on the field, every third Lunar-Crystallize makes them resonate in Moondrift Harmony, firing a Geo projectile that tracks the target. They count as Geo constructs.

166.content:
Lunar Reaction (also: Lunar Reactions, Lunar reaction family, Moonlight Reaction): Lunar Reactions are a family of three elemental reactions that appear when a party contains a character whose Moonsign Benediction passive allows them. Each one takes a normal Hydro-related reaction (Electro-Charged, Bloom, Crystallize) and replaces it with a Moon-themed version: Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom and Lunar-Crystallize. Unlike their base versions, Lunar Reactions can land critical hits. They belong to the Nod-Krai era of the game.

They arrived in stages: Lunar-Charged in Version 5.8, Lunar-Bloom in Version 6.0 (Luna I) and Lunar-Crystallize in Version 6.3 (Luna IV). Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Crystallize can be set off by simply applying the right elements; Lunar-Bloom does no damage by itself and works through character talents and constellations.

In universe: Canon offers no in-world explanation. Lunar Reactions are presented as tutorial and combat material. Treat them as a gameplay abstraction: a scene may borrow the look (moonlit clouds, drifting stones, glowing dew) without naming an in-world law.

Related setting, from the wiki: the reactions are tied to Moonsign, a party bonus keyed to characters of Nod-Krai (plus Zibai), and their enabling passives are called Moonsign Benedictions. Columbina, the new Moon Goddess in the wiki's account, and users of the Moon Wheel are the ones whose passives turn the reactions on. Nod-Krai is also where kuuvahki, described as the power of the Three Moons, is found.

The wiki's Kuuvahki page describes that power as a primordial form of elemental energy tied to the Three Moons, found only in Nod-Krai. It does not say that Lunar Reactions are kuuvahki, so this entry does not either; see the uncertainties for the project brief's wording.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): while a character with a matching Moonsign Benediction is in the party, three Hydro-related reactions are replaced. Electro and Hydro give Lunar-Charged instead of Electro-Charged; Dendro and Hydro give Lunar-Bloom instead of Bloom; Geo and Hydro give Lunar-Crystallize instead of Hydro Crystallize.

- Lunar Reactions can land critical hits, which their base versions cannot.
- Lunar-Charged makes a thundercloud, Lunar-Bloom gives Verdant Dew, and Lunar-Crystallize makes Moondrifts (each has its own entry).
- Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Crystallize can deal damage through a separate instance when elements are applied, using the stats of every character that contributed an element. Lunar-Bloom damage comes only from talents and constellations.

- Damage uses a shared formula with the Stellar Glimmer reactions. Its elemental mastery bonus is 6 x EM / (EM + 2000), and the base reaction coefficient is 3 for Lunar-Charged, 1.6 for Lunar-Crystallize and 1 for Lunar-Bloom (the last only when a talent deals it directly).
- Only Moonsign Benediction passives of Moon Wheel users and Columbina give a Lunar Reaction Base DMG Bonus: up to 7% for Columbina and up to 14% for the others the wiki lists.
- Moonsign levels: one Moonsign character gives Nascent Gleam; two give Ascendant Gleam, which strengthens Moonsign characters and lets non-Moonsign characters raise Lunar Reaction damage for 20 seconds after a skill or burst, up to 36%, scaled by an element-specific stat.

- Elemental resonances also react to the family: High Voltage (two Electro) can generate Electro particles on Lunar-Charged; Enduring Rock (two Geo) buffs allies near Moondrifts; Sprawling Greenery (two Dendro) grants Elemental Mastery after Lunar-Bloom.
- The 6.0 and 6.3 patch notes show the reactions in limited modes: limited-time modes and a Spiral Abyss ley line disorder raised Lunar Reaction damage (50% or 75% in the cases noted), and a 6.3 fix corrected an issue where the 50% Lunar boost on Floors 9 and 10 did not apply to Lunar-Crystallize.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): give Lunar Reactions a cool, silvery cast. A thundercloud drifting between fighters, a ring of floating stones, dew beading on leaves under moonlight. Keep them tied to someone with a Moonsign Benediction, since that is what the game requires.

Characters in Nod-Krai may talk about moonlight and kuuvahki, but no named character in the sources read calls these "Lunar Reactions". Use the term in out-of-character or system-minded narration, not as an in-world discipline taught to ordinary people.

Do not claim Lunar Reactions are kuuvahki powered, caused by Columbina's will, or that ordinary Hydro reactions stop working in Nod-Krai. Canon says none of these.

Limits: Without a Moonsign Benediction character in the party, nothing changes and the ordinary reactions occur.

Lunar-Bloom does not make its own damage when it triggers; the Dendro Cores it creates are ordinary Bloom cores and do not count as Lunar-Bloom damage.

The family is Hydro-based only. Pyro, Cryo and Anemo have their own Stellar Glimmer family (Stellar-Conduct, Stellar Swirl), which is a separate set of reactions.

167.content: The three Lunar Reactions are Lunar-Charged (Electro with Hydro, replaces Electro-Charged, 5.8), Lunar-Bloom (Dendro with Hydro, replaces Bloom, 6.0) and Lunar-Crystallize (Geo with Hydro, replaces Hydro Crystallize, 6.3). Each has a matching entry for its details.

168.content:
Melt (also: Melt reaction, Melt DMG, Pyro-Cryo reaction): Melt is the elemental reaction between Pyro and Cryo. It deals no damage itself. Instead, the attack that triggers it hits harder. The bonus is larger when the trigger is Pyro landing on a target already affected by Cryo, and smaller when Cryo lands on a Pyro-affected target. It is a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction, not a named law of the world.

Melt has existed since Version 1.0. Its sibling amplifying reaction is Vaporize (Pyro with Hydro). Both give damage multipliers, and neither creates a new effect on the target.

In universe: Canon gives no story explanation for Melt. The in-game tutorial only says that when Pyro meets Cryo, Melt occurs, and the triggering source of damage receives a bonus.

Nothing read ties Melt to a character or event. Do not invent an origin. The everyday idea that heat melts ice is a safe image for a scene, but treat it as flavour.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Melt happens when Pyro hits a target that already carries Cryo, or when Cryo hits a target that already carries Pyro. The triggering attack's damage is multiplied. Pyro as the trigger gives a 2x multiplier; Cryo as the trigger gives 1.5x.

- Elemental Mastery of the triggering character raises the multiplier further, and certain artifact sets raise Melt damage.
- The 2x version consumes more of the first element, usually removing it quickly. The 1.5x version consumes less and often leaves the aura in place.
- Applying Pyro to a Freeze Aura left by Frozen consumes it and triggers Melt. Melt can also dissolve ice on water in the open world instantly.

- Melt is one of two amplifying reactions with Vaporize. Unlike transformative reactions such as Overloaded, amplifying reactions can CRIT, because they scale the triggering attack's own damage.
- The strength of the reaction comes from whoever triggers it; the stats of whoever left the first aura do not count.
- Because many attacks have an internal cooldown on applying their element, a source cannot reapply Pyro or Cryo on every hit, and so cannot Melt on every hit.

- Melt is unchanged by the newer reaction families. As of Version 7.1 the wiki's reaction table still lists Pyro with Cryo as Melt, with the same 2x and 1.5x multipliers.
- The wiki cites the Elemental Gauge Theory page for the amounts of aura consumed by the two directions. This entry does not reproduce its numbers.

Limits: Melt cannot happen without a first element in place, and it does nothing to a target with neither Pyro nor Cryo on it.

It adds no damage of its own, so a weak hit stays weak. Enemies immune or resistant to Pyro or Cryo reduce the benefit.

Examples: Gameplay example from the in-game tutorial: use Cryo attacks to coat opponents with Cryo, then switch to a Pyro character and attack; the Pyro attack triggers Melt and hits much harder, so opponents fall faster. The wiki's preview shows Melt being caused on a Cryo Slime.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Melt as a burst of steam and a hiss where flame meets frost, with the strike landing harder than it should. Pyro is the orange-red cue, Cryo the pale-blue cue; keep the effect to one blow, not a lasting area of fire or ice.

Narratively, Melt rewards teamwork: one person chills a foe and a partner finishes it with fire, or the reverse. It is a nice way to show two characters with opposing Visions working in sync. Do not have ordinary Vision holders melt walls of ice or glaciers with a single spell.

Avoid mixing Melt up with Frozen: Frozen locks a target in ice, while Melt boosts a hit. Pyro on a frozen target ends the freeze; do not have it do both at once for free.

169.content: Melt and Vaporize are the two amplifying reactions. They multiply the damage of the triggering attack by 2x or 1.5x depending on which element came second, instead of dealing their own damage. The multiplier is raised again by Elemental Mastery. The 1.5x reactions consume less of the first element than the 2x reactions do.

170.content:
Moon Wheel (also: Moon Wheels, Nod-Krai Vision): A Moon Wheel is a Vision-like gem associated with Nod-Krai and the Three Moons. It is "formed from the stuff of the soul" and lets its bearer manipulate the elements like a Vision does, but it draws on kuuvahki, an ancient and purer form of elemental power, instead of ordinary elemental energy. In Nod-Krai a Moon Wheel looks identical to a Vision.

All playable Moon Wheel users hold a Moonsign Benediction passive, the talent that links them to the Moonsign mechanic and to Lunar Reactions (own entries). The known users are Ineffa, Flins, Lauma, Linnea, Nefer and Zibai.

In universe: Moon Wheels work like Visions in practice: the bearer wears the gem and channels one element. The difference is the energy behind it. Kuuvahki is described as a primordial form of elemental power, the power of the Three Moons.

The wiki's lore summary is that the Heavenly Principles and the Three Moon Sisters originally created Moon Wheels, and that they were given to the Moon Goddesses' human followers so the Goddesses could talk with them during rituals. A Natlan-era note in Ineffa's story calls the Moon Wheel a plaything the "traitors" (the Three Moons) gave their human followers to communicate with, and says it relies on a purer power rather than on elemental energy "tainted" by the usurper, the Heavenly Principles.

The same note records an experiment on a Vision, concluding that, like the northern ritual items, it is "formed from the stuff of the soul", with its form fixed through wishes so that it can call forth elemental power. The writer asks whether this is why Visions have recently appeared alongside human wishes. The writer served the Sovereign Lords of Natlan and worked from a Vision taken at Ek' Pulinik, so this is one in-world researcher's hypothesis. Lauma's story adds a human-scale puzzle: she wonders whether Moon Wheels even existed when the three moons stood in the sky.

Appearance: A Nod-Krai Moon Wheel is an orb-shaped elemental gem set in the upper part of a circular frame, with a crescent-like small circle and four rhombuses on the lower half. It is visually identical to a Nod-Krai Vision.

Zibai, the only known user from outside Nod-Krai (she is from Liyue), has a slightly different frame: the crescent-like circle has an inverted colour scheme and the four rhombuses are missing. Her story says Istaroth, the shade of Time, gave her the Moon Wheel, which may explain the difference; the wiki lists that as one possible reason, not a stated one.

Origins: Item text from the Aubade of Morningstar and Moon artifact set tells of an age of three moons when people, frightened by questions the gods' envoys would not answer, turned to the Three Moons, who answered with madness and inspiration beneath the moon. An archpriestess then returned from a mountain summit with a small circular talisman, called the "Moon Wheel", the new pact between the three moons and the people.

Moon Envoys were servants of the Heavenly Principles who also worked with the Moon Goddesses. In Zibai's case, a Moon Wheel marked her new post: she then served both Celestia and the Moons, travelling between the Lunar Palace, Celestia and her home Lang-Gan. Her story says she sensed that the Moons' love for the world differed from that of the morning stars (the Heavenly Principles): moonlight settled gently on each scorched plant rather than only on the sacred ones.

Users: Playable Moon Wheel users: Ineffa (Electro), Flins (Electro), Lauma (Dendro), Linnea (Geo), Nefer (Dendro) and Zibai (Geo). Sigurd's Electro gem might also be a Moon Wheel; this is unknown.

- Ineffa: the only user the player sees receive a Moon Wheel on screen. Her character story says the Moon Wheel inside her core, when it began to glow, brought back her memories.
- Flins: his story says a Moon Wheel appeared suddenly in his showroom one night, a gift that matched his coat and served as cover for his power and flames. He first told Illuga he got it at an auction. As a Lantern Fae he does not need one for his power.
- Lauma: has had hers since birth; it reportedly fell from her swaddling clothes. It troubles her that she cannot remember how she got it, and she regards it as a symbol of vigilance, restraint and responsibility.
- Linnea: found a plain gray stone on a seabed-ruin expedition; the glutton Lumi swallowed it, and afterwards it turned out to be her Moon Wheel. She keeps it as an ornament.
- Nefer: it appeared at the bottom of a gift box from a Northern Intelligence Network emissary, in the quest "An Elegy for Faded Moonlight". She links it to Thoth, who told her tales of labouring across the three moons, although she believes none of his claims.
- Zibai: see origins; a Moon Envoy's mark.

Release notes for the wiki's infobox dates: Ineffa, the first user, released on 2025-07-30 (Version 5.8), Zibai on 2026-02-03 and Linnea on 2026-04-08. The wiki also notes that the Moon Wheel users the player actually watches receiving a gem on screen are limited to Ineffa; with Visions included, Rana, the Wanderer and Furina also receive theirs on screen. Nothing in canon as of 7.1 says a Moon Wheel has been taken from a user or destroyed, and Ineffa's story is the only one that places a Moon Wheel inside a machine rather than on a person.

Kuuvahki link: Kuuvahki is found only in Nod-Krai and is described as the power of the Light Realm in its purest form. Lunar Reactions use kuuvahki, and Moon Wheel users enable them through their Moonsign Benediction passives.

Per the wiki, kuuvahki exists in Nod-Krai either because Columbina poured her power out over the land, or because two of the Three Moons shattered above it. Kuuvahki of sufficient strength can counter or convert Abyssal power, but a stronger source of Abyssal energy will suppress the weaker kuuvahki instead (Flins's remark in "The Ashen-White Order Burns"). Moon Wheels and kuuvahki are separate things: the wheel is the gem, kuuvahki the energy.

Gameplay: Gameplay, not literal lore: Moon Wheel users are playable characters from Nod-Krai (plus Zibai) who carry a Moonsign Benediction passive. Each passive raises the party's Moonsign level by 1, and Moon Wheel users enable and strengthen Lunar Reactions.

Lunar Reactions are a subset of elemental reactions (Lunar-Bloom, Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Crystallize) which, unlike their base reactions, can CRIT. A character with a Moonsign Benediction passive that converts specific Hydro-related reactions must be in the party to trigger them.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat a Moon Wheel in a scene like a Vision, a gem at the hip or back that glows with its element. Pale, silvery light is a safe cue for kuuvahki.

Most Nod-Krai citizens would not tell a Vision from a Moon Wheel by sight; the difference matters to scholars and to people who know the Moons' history. A character who learns what a Moon Wheel is might be uneasy about its origin, as Lauma is. Do not claim a given character's wheel was a gift from a specific being unless their story says so.

Limits: Canon does not say who can receive a Moon Wheel, whether it needs a particular wish or desire (as Visions are said to), or whether a Moon Wheel and a Vision can be held together. It does not say an ordinary person can buy one.

Do not state that Columbina hands out Moon Wheels, or that the Moon Goddesses personally chose any current user. Only Zibai's story ties her wheel to a Moon-related figure (Istaroth).

171.comment: Moon Wheel: Moon Wheel and Vision
171.content: Moon Wheels look the same as Nod-Krai Visions, but are "formed from the stuff of the soul" and use kuuvahki rather than normal elemental energy. They were originally given to the Moon Goddesses' followers to let the Goddesses speak with them.

172.content: Zibai, the White Horse Adeptus, was an Angel who guided Lang-Gan before Liyue. Her wiki history says Istaroth gave her a Moon Wheel as a symbol of becoming a Moon Envoy of the Lunar Palace, assigned to Sonnet, goddess of the Iridescent Moon. Her own story tells it more ambiguously: the shade of Time placed before her a crest engraved with the moons' sigil, and she at first treated it as unnecessary to her mission. Her Moon Wheel has a different frame from Nod-Krai ones.

173.content: In Ineffa's story the Moon Wheel in her core glows and her memories return. A Natlan-era note describes a Moon Wheel acquired for study, and a scene in the same story has Lianca fit a gem that once belonged to her mother, a gem that suited the core's phlogiston power. Treat the exact chain of ownership as only partly told.

key: how I got my Moon Wheel
174.comment: Moon Wheel: Moon Wheel acquisition stories
174.content: Lauma's wheel fell out of her swaddling clothes; Linnea's was a gray stone Lumi swallowed; Nefer's turned up in a gift box from a Northern Intelligence Network emissary; Flins's appeared in his showroom one night. In each case the story gives the how and not the why.

175.content:
Moonsign (also: Moonsign Level, Nascent Gleam, Ascendant Gleam, Moonsign: Nascent Gleam, Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam, New Moon's Embrace): Moonsign is a Team Bonus that sits beside Elemental Resonance. Some characters, mostly from Nod-Krai, carry a Moonsign Benediction passive, and each one in the party raises the party's Moonsign Level by one. One Moonsign character gives Nascent Gleam; two or more give Ascendant Gleam, which strengthens those characters and rewards non-Moonsign teammates for their skills. It is a game system, not a thing characters talk about, and it is tied to the moon-themed power of Nod-Krai.

It first appeared in Version Luna I (6.0), the first Nod-Krai version. The Lunar Reactions it supports (Lunar-Charged from 5.8, Lunar-Bloom from 6.0, Lunar-Crystallize later) are separate systems.

In universe: Canon never explains Moonsign inside the story. The only in-world frame is the one the game gives: Nod-Krai is where "the new moon rises", and the tutorial says there are other ways to raise a party's Moonsign Level there.

The related lore is concrete, though. Moon Wheels are Vision-like gems that channel kuuvahki, the moon-linked primordial elemental power found in Nod-Krai, and every playable Moon Wheel user has a Moonsign Benediction passive. Kuuvahki is described as the power of the Three Moons, spread over Nod-Krai by the new Moon Goddess Columbina. Moonsign should be read as the game's way of showing a team gathering around that moonlight; canon does not describe it as an in-world ritual or ranking.

Not every Moonsign character uses a Moon Wheel. Per the wiki, the Moonsign roster is: Ineffa, Flins, Lauma, Aino, Nefer, Jahoda, Columbina, Illuga, Zibai and Linnea. Of these the wiki lists Flins, Ineffa, Lauma, Linnea, Nefer and Zibai as Moon Wheel users; Aino, Jahoda, Illuga and Columbina are not on that list. Zibai is from Liyue and is the only roster member whose region is not Nod-Krai.

Mechanics: Gameplay (not literal lore): the party gets a Moonsign Level equal to the number of Moonsign characters in it. One gives the Nascent Gleam effect. Two or more give Ascendant Gleam, which also includes Nascent Gleam's effects.

At Ascendant Gleam, certain Talents and Skills of the Moonsign characters themselves are enhanced. In addition, for 20 seconds after a non-Moonsign character uses an Elemental Skill or Elemental Burst, nearby characters deal more Lunar Reaction DMG, up to 36% and not stacking. How much depends on the caster's element: for Pyro, Electro and Cryo, 0.9% per 100 ATK; for Hydro, 0.6% per 1,000 Max HP; for Geo, 1% per 100 DEF; for Anemo and Dendro, 2.25% per 100 Elemental Mastery.

The stats needed to hit the 36% cap are 4,000 ATK (Pyro, Electro, Cryo), 60,000 Max HP (Hydro), 3,600 DEF (Geo) and 1,600 Elemental Mastery (Anemo, Dendro). The tutorial adds that a higher Moonsign Level also improves some Weapons and Artifacts. Gameplay behaviour in Co-Op Mode is not settled (see uncertainties).

Moonsign Benediction passives of the Lunar-Reaction users also change the reactions themselves (see the separate entry). The passives of Illuga, Jahoda and Aino are the plain form: their wiki text states only the +1 Moonsign Level effect and no reaction conversion.

Moonsign benediction: A Moonsign Benediction passive is the Talent that adds one Moonsign Level while its owner is in the party. Gameplay: the passives are Ineffa's Assemblage Hub, Flins's Old World Secrets, Lauma's Nature's Chorus, Aino's Force Limit Analysis, Nefer's Dusklit Eaves, Jahoda's Rooftop Dash, Columbina's Moonlight, Lent Unto You, Illuga's Unwithering in Winter, Zibai's The Coursing Sun and Moon and Linnea's Habitat Survey.

Per the wiki, Columbina's passive and the Moon Wheel users' passives also convert a base reaction into its Lunar form and add Base DMG scaling to a stat of the owner. Ineffa and Flins convert Electro-Charged into Lunar-Charged (0.7% Base DMG per 100 ATK, capped at 14%). Lauma and Nefer convert Bloom into Lunar-Bloom (0.0175% per point of Elemental Mastery, capped at 14%). Zibai and Linnea convert Hydro Crystallize into Lunar-Crystallize (0.7% per 100 DEF, capped at 14%). Columbina converts all three (0.2% per 1,000 Max HP, capped at 7%).

Lunar reactions: Lunar Reactions are a subset of Elemental Reactions that only happen when a character with a fitting Moonsign Benediction passive is in the party. Unlike their base versions they can land CRIT hits, and they use kuuvahki. Lunar-Charged (Electro + Hydro) is a thundercloud that strikes enemies affected by both Wet and Electro; it came with Ineffa in 5.8. Lunar-Bloom (Dendro + Hydro) does no damage by itself and grants Verdant Dew. Lunar-Crystallize (Geo + Hydro) creates Moondrifts that fire Moondrift Harmony strikes. Moonsign Level matters because several Lunar Reaction bonuses key off Ascendant Gleam.

Sources of ascendant gleam: Only inside Nod-Krai: completing a quest of Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles (Columbina's reputation system, unlocked by "The Dark Side of Memory") gives the New Moon's Embrace effect until the seventh daily reset after it. While it lasts, the party's Moonsign Level is always Ascendant Gleam when in Nod-Krai, and it cannot be switched off. The Selenic Chronicles quests become unavailable once "A Nocturne of the Far North" starts after Act IV of the Archon Quest and return after "True Moon". Treat this as gameplay-system context, not a character-visible event; its availability depends on quest progress.

Equipment: Gameplay, the equipment that reads Moonsign Level: the Silken Moon's Serenade artifact set (Luna I) gives party Elemental Mastery of 60 at Nascent Gleam and 120 at Ascendant Gleam for 8 seconds after the wearer deals Elemental DMG, plus extra Lunar Reaction DMG for each different Gleaming Moon effect in the party. The Aubade of Morningstar and Moon artifact set (Luna IV) gives Lunar Reaction DMG while the wearer is off-field, with a further large bonus at Ascendant Gleam or higher.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): Moonsign is a gameplay label and ordinary characters should not mention Moonsign Levels, "Nascent Gleam" or "Ascendant Gleam". If a scene wants the flavour, use soft silver or pale light, quiet confidence and a sense of people drawing strength from one another near Nod-Krai's moonlight, without claiming characters can feel a numbered level.

A party of Nod-Krai characters with Moon Wheels can be played as sharing a recognisable "moon-touched" connection, but canon does not say that their wheels link to each other. Do not give a non-Moonsign character a Moon Wheel or kuuvahki power because they stand near a Moonsign character.

Do not present Moonsign as a formal title or rank in Nod-Krai society, as something only Columbina grants, or as a power that exists outside the moon-linked themes the wiki ties to kuuvahki. Zibai's membership shows it is not limited to Nod-Krai natives.

176.content: Nascent Gleam is the Moonsign effect for a party with one Moonsign character; every party member gains it. It is the lower of the two named levels. Ascendant Gleam includes Nascent Gleam's effects.

177.content: Ascendant Gleam is the Moonsign effect for a party with two or more Moonsign characters. It enhances Moonsign characters' Talents and Skills and lets non-Moonsign characters boost nearby Lunar Reaction DMG for 20 seconds after using a skill or burst, up to a 36% cap. In Genius Invokation TCG, "Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam" is also an Elemental Resonance event card, with the in-card line "Come night or day, may the moonlight connect us."

178.content:
The Talent type that adds a Moonsign Level. Characters who have one: Ineffa, Flins, Lauma, Aino, Nefer, Jahoda, Columbina, Illuga, Zibai and Linnea. Passives of Columbina and the Moon Wheel users also enable Lunar Reactions.

The passive names, in the order above, are Assemblage Hub, Old World Secrets, Nature's Chorus, Force Limit Analysis, Dusklit Eaves, Rooftop Dash, Moonlight, Lent Unto You, Unwithering in Winter, The Coursing Sun and Moon and Habitat Survey.

179.content: New Moon's Embrace is the temporary effect gained from completing Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles quests. In Nod-Krai the party's Moonsign Level is always Ascendant Gleam while it lasts (up to the seventh daily reset after the quest), and it cannot be disabled. It is tied to the Selenic Chronicles quest line and is not a standing feature of the system.

180.content: The reputation system for Columbina (called "the Damselette") at Silvermoon Hall in Nod-Krai. Unlocked by "The Dark Side of Memory" in Version Luna I, it unlocks a quest every seven daily resets and gives rewards after set quest counts. Its link to Moonsign is the New Moon's Embrace effect.

181.content:
Moonsign Benediction Passive (also: Moonsign Benediction, Moonsign Benediction Passives, Benediction passive): A Moonsign Benediction passive is a Passive Talent carried by certain characters, mostly from Nod-Krai plus Zibai of Liyue. While its owner is in the party, the party's Moonsign Level rises by one. On Columbina and on Moon Wheel users, the passive also lets a base reaction turn into a Lunar Reaction. It is a game-mechanic label, not something characters discuss in the story.

Official wiki phrasing ties the passive to the Moonsign Team Bonus, which sits beside Elemental Resonance: one Moonsign character gives Nascent Gleam, two or more give Ascendant Gleam.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore. Every Benediction passive adds +1 Moonsign Level while its owner is in the party. Illuga, Jahoda and Aino have only this plain form.

The Lunar-enabling passives convert a base reaction triggered by any party member and add Base DMG that scales with a stat of the owner, per the wiki. Ineffa and Flins convert Electro-Charged into Lunar-Charged (0.7% Base DMG per 100 ATK, up to 14%). Lauma and Nefer convert Bloom into Lunar-Bloom (0.0175% per point of Elemental Mastery, up to 14%). Zibai and Linnea convert Hydro Crystallize into Lunar-Crystallize (0.7% per 100 DEF, up to 14%). Columbina converts all three (Electro-Charged, Bloom and Hydro Crystallize) into their Lunar forms, adding 0.2% Base DMG per 1,000 Max HP, up to 7%.

Moonsign levels: one Moonsign character in the party gives Nascent Gleam; two give Ascendant Gleam, which enhances certain Talents and Skills of Moonsign characters. Non-Moonsign teammates also help once Ascendant Gleam is reached: for 20 seconds after casting a Skill or Burst, they raise nearby characters' Lunar Reaction DMG according to a stat tied to their element, to a maximum of 36%. See the Moonsign entry for details.

Roster: Passive, owner and release as listed by the wiki:
- Assemblage Hub: Ineffa (5.8), Electro-Charged to Lunar-Charged.
- Old World Secrets: Flins (Luna I, 6.0), Electro-Charged to Lunar-Charged.
- Nature's Chorus: Lauma (Luna I, 6.0), Bloom to Lunar-Bloom.
- Force Limit Analysis: Aino (Luna I, 6.0), Moonsign level only.
- Dusklit Eaves: Nefer (Luna II, 6.1), Bloom to Lunar-Bloom.
- Rooftop Dash: Jahoda (Luna III, 6.2), Moonsign level only.
- Moonlight, Lent Unto You: Columbina (Luna IV, 6.3), all three conversions.
- The Coursing Sun and Moon: Zibai (Luna IV, 6.3), Hydro Crystallize to Lunar-Crystallize.
- Unwithering in Winter: Illuga (Luna IV, 6.3), Moonsign level only.
- Habitat Survey: Linnea (Luna VI, 6.5), Hydro Crystallize to Lunar-Crystallize.

Reading the roster: the three reaction families map to the three Lunar Reactions, each with two Moon Wheel-style converters, and Columbina covers every family. The wiki's description says that those belonging to Columbina and Moon Wheel users additionally enable and enhance Lunar Reactions. Aino, Jahoda and Illuga add a level but change no reaction.

In universe: Nothing found presents the Benediction as an in-world ritual. The surrounding themes come from Nod-Krai lore: kuuvahki, the moon-linked primordial energy, the Moon Wheels that channel it, and the Moon Goddess Columbina. Treat the passive as the game's way of showing a team gathering under that moonlight, not as a title or rank.

How {{char}} behaves: Project-recommended narrative interpretation, not canon. Characters should not say "my Moonsign Benediction passive" or quote numbers. If a scene needs the idea, show moonlight making a shared effort stronger: the owner steadies the party's reactions, and other teammates feed it through their own skills.

Limits: Do not state that Zibai or any non-Nod-Krai character is a Nod-Krai native because they carry the passive. Do not claim a Moonsign rank exists in society. Do not assume Illuga, Jahoda or Aino alter reactions. Co-Op behaviour of Moonsign is unverified.

Release order, per the wiki change histories: Ineffa's passive came first in 5.8 (the version that introduced Lunar-Charged), then Flins, Lauma and Aino in Luna I (6.0), Nefer in Luna II (6.1), Jahoda in Luna III (6.2), Columbina, Zibai and Illuga in Luna IV (6.3), and Linnea in Luna VI (6.5). The wiki dates the Moonsign Team Bonus itself to Luna I, so how Ineffa's passive counted a level before 6.0 is not documented here. The in-game passive names differ across languages (the Chinese title is Yuezhao Zhuci, roughly Moonsign Blessing), and the English name is the only one this archive uses as a key.

182.comment: Moonsign Benediction Passive: Moonsign Benediction passives
182.content: The Talent type that adds one Moonsign Level while its owner is in the party. Owners: Ineffa, Flins, Lauma, Aino, Nefer, Jahoda, Columbina, Illuga, Zibai and Linnea. The passives of Columbina and the Moon Wheel users also enable Lunar Reactions.

183.content:
Mystic Arts in Teyvat (also: Mystic Arts, mystic arts of Teyvat, magic in Teyvat): "Mystic arts" is the wiki's umbrella for the magical, ritual and supernatural traditions of Teyvat that are not just a Vision's elemental power. Mondstadt has openly practised alchemy and astrology; Liyue has the adepti's arts, exorcism, the Art of Homa and the Qimen arts; Inazuma has kitsune and bake-danuki magic, onmyoudou and tengu arts; Sumeru has the Akasha, Akademiya alchemy and the Aranara's Ararakalari. A parallel circle of powerful mages, the Hexenzirkel, practises witchcraft (its own entry).

The grouping is the wiki's, not the game's: each tradition keeps its own in-world name and rules. The mystic arts are mostly shown by what particular people can do, not by a rulebook; canon explains very little about how any of it works. Nation entries and the Alchemy, Art of Khemia, Adeptal Arts, Exorcism and Witchcraft entries carry the detail.

In universe: Magic is not limited to Vision-bearers: Yelan says her clan has practised it for generations, and kitsune, adepti, tengu and aranara work wonders without Visions. Arts include divination, talismans, transformation, dream-magic, pocket dimensions, purification, alchemy and spirit-summoning.

Many traditions inherit from each other. The adepti's arts were taught to them by Rex Lapis. Liyue's exorcist arts look like derivatives of adeptal arts. Inazuma's onmyoudou was built by Kamuna Harunosuke 500 years ago from adeptal techniques and the tengu art of transcension. The Fantastic Compass, invented by the adeptus Sea Gazer, was handed to a mortal exorcist friend and later reached Yelan's family, which developed its own catalysts.

The same expertise is often cumulative in one person: Alice is credited with alchemy, astrology, engineering, magic and medicine; Rhinedottir mixed Khemia with the Hexenzirkel's wider learning. Tools and devices (talismans, catalysts, compasses, nets, orbs) carry much of the work, often needing a specific trained user, such as an adeptus working with a mortal on the Fantastic Compass.

Mondstadt: Alchemy is openly practised (bio-alchemy and Albedo's Art of Khemia). Astrology, including hydromancy, is practised by Barbeloth and Mona.

Astrology rests on the belief that the stars record the destinies of all Teyvat's inhabitants, and Vision-bearers' destinies are thought to be tied to particular constellations. Those who come from outside Teyvat, such as the Traveler, cannot be read this way. Mona warns that reading your own fortune makes fate turn in on itself, and that giving advice to the subject risks entangling your fate with theirs. Hydromancy, a subclass practised by Barbeloth and Mona, reads the inverted reflection of the stars on water; Mona says the best water is the pure water of melted snow. Pyromancy, presumably a fire-based divination possibly connected with Phlogiston, is known only from a single diary.

Albedo's Khemia can also produce ordinary objects such as chairs. The Alchemy entry covers Mondstadt, Liyue, Sumeru and Snezhnayan alchemy in detail. Witchcraft (the Hexenzirkel) is also linked to Mondstadt, where several members have appeared, but it has its own entry.

Liyue: The adepti's Adeptus Arts, taught to them by Rex Lapis (adeptal alchemy, dream-magic, talismans, pocket dimensions), plus exorcism, the Art of Homa and the Qimen arts.

- Dream Trawler: also called the giving and receiving of dreams; Rex Lapis and Xiao are known users.
- Mortal Lingering: lets the user take a human form even after their original body has died. Pervases used it.
- Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering: known to be used by yakshas; the mask lets the wearer subdue a god's might, at the cost of great suffering.
- Sigils: Qiqi's body is full of adeptal power, and the talismans on her clothing keep it from making her berserk. Rex Lapis also made Sigils of Permission that let mortals channel adeptal power; Starsnatcher used one against evil spirits, and the Fatui later duplicated them.
- Sub-Space Creation is considered inferior to Rex Lapis's power to move mountains and seas. Adepti can also make Teapot Spirits as butlers for their abodes.

- Art of Homa: a secret technique to purify the border between life and death and burn away fetor leaking into the living world, using Homa altars and the Staff of Homa. Hu Tao says it demands great focus and no hesitation in the face of death; doing it wrongly can shorten or end one's life. The wiki says it was first used by the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame, one of the Eight Adepts, whose sacrifice in the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method purified Tao Dou; Wuwang Kid then handed her methods to the founders of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.
- Exorcism: Liyue's exorcists (thaumaturges) drive off ghosts, spirits and demons, and often learn the trade from their families. Known groups are the Tianheng Thaumaturges (Chongyun's clan), Yelan's clan and the Lan Clan (see the Exorcism entry).
- Fantastic Compass: a catalyst made by Sea Gazer to seal monsters; "one can move the heavens and shake the earth" when activated by an adeptus and a mortal together. Past users include Boyang and Bosacius, Yanfei (briefly), and Xiao with Yelan.
- Parametric Transformer: an elemental-powered device from the Dunyu Ruins that transmutes items into other items; its origin is unknown.
- Qimen arts: originated with the Wind Reader of the Eight Adepts, ancestor of Chenyu Vale's Twelve Tribes; fortune conveyance, fate transference, divination, illusion and warding. The Lan Clan of Chenyu Vale has practised them for generations; one art uses rattan figures and is Lan Yan's specialty.

Inazuma: - Bake-danuki magic: bake-danuki are tanuki with mystical knowledge, known for transforming into people or objects. Kichiboushi's trick "Eight tatami Kapow" made an air cushion he floated on in Dragonspine's cold winds.
- Kitsune magic: past kitsune were said to shapeshift. After the passing of the Kitsune Saiguu, Sky and Earth kitsune became stone statues and the race lost its power. Yae Miko, a Sky Kitsune of the Hakushin line, remains masterful. In "A Centuries-Long Dream" she performed a summoning ritual that made the Traveler a host for the spirit of another kitsune, Urakusai.
- Tengu arts: include the art of transcension, which was used in creating onmyoudou. Tengu warriors such as Kujou Sara use feather fans with magical effects.

- Onmyoudou: the Kamuna art Harunosuke created 500 years ago during the Cataclysm by combining Liyue's adeptal techniques with the art of transcension, which he learned under the Yougou Tengu. Most of it is lost. It centres on shikigami (paper cut-outs with magical power, such as Shiki Taishou) and shikifuda (paper seals focused on elemental power). The Kairagi, former samurai, still use shikifuda to put elements in their blades without a Vision.
- Mystic Onmyou Chamber: a shifting-room domain built with onmyoudou as a samurai training ground, now abandoned.
- Ubiquity Nets: made with Kamuna onmyoudou to capture small animals; the Omni-Ubiquity Net, Wakamurasaki's improvement, can hold the essence of a creature and recreate it, but neither net affects humans.

Sumeru: - The Akasha: a Gnosis-powered knowledge system made by the former Dendro Archon Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and developed by the Akademiya. Akasha Terminals give users knowledge; Lesser Lord Kusanali calls herself the first Akasha Terminal. Terminals can also run without the Akasha from knowledge stored as "Canned Knowledge" in Knowledge Capsules.
- Alchemy: studied in the Spantamad Darshan, with alchemical divination and the Remelting Effect (see the Alchemy entry).
- Ararakalari: special abilities of the Aranara, drawn from their memories and powered by forest plants. They come from the "Mahamaitri Kusa Stotra", an Aranara song in praise of Queen Aranyani, humans and themselves.

- Each Aranara has a unique Ararakalari. Strong ones can attack, teleport or shield against the Withering, but each use costs some of the Aranara's memories. They can gain new abilities from new memories, including borrowed ones: Arama obtained Aramuhukunda's teleportation by receiving his memories. A Kusava seed strengthens an Ararakalari and lets humans, including the Traveler, use one briefly.
- Eremite Spirits of Omen: Eremite Stone Enchanters and Galehunters can summon spirits sealed in their weapons (the Stone Drake and the Wind Glede).
- Wisdom Orb: a Fungus-capturing device invented by the Amurta researcher Kautilya for the Nilotpala Cup; the wiki says it was repurposed from earlier experimental devices and concealed a backdoor command. It resembles the Omni-Ubiquity Net, which the Akademiya investigators noted, tracing both to Liyue's adeptal arts.

Other regions: The wiki page covers only Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma and Sumeru. Other nations have their own non-Vision traditions that live in separate entries: Natlan's Nightsoul, Nod-Krai's Moonsign and Moonchanters, and Khaenri'ah's Khemia. Fontaine's mystic traditions are not covered by the wiki page.

Phlogiston, the Delusions, the Gnoses and Abyssal power are treated as cosmological powers and have their own entries, not as "mystic arts" in the wiki sense.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat each tradition as belonging to a place, a lineage and a way of thinking, not as a generic spell list. Liyue's arts are talismans, formulas and discipline; Inazuma's are paper charms and transformations; Sumeru's are knowledge, memory and lectures; Mondstadt's are lab benches and star charts. Magic should cost something: focus, memory, health, a rare tool or a partner.

Reserve godlike feats for Archons, adepti and the Hexenzirkel. A mortal exorcist can seal, ward and banish; they cannot reshape land. Magic does not need a Vision, and a Vision is not a spell: keep elemental power and mystic arts distinct in description.

Do not let the Traveler or any other character casually learn secret arts (Homa, Khemia, onmyoudou) without canon support. Do not give ordinary kitsune or tanuki Yae Miko's power. Do not treat the wiki grouping as a single magic system.

Limits: Canon never defines a unified magic system. Arts are tied to teachers and lineages and some are lost (most onmyoudou; kitsune power after the Saiguu). Some carry serious risks: adeptal elixirs kill non-adepti, the Nuo Dance inflicts great suffering, Homa can shorten a life, and astrologers risk entangling their own fate.

The question of how a non-Vision user performs magic is unanswered; every exorcist seen using exorcist arts in-game holds a Vision.

184.comment: Mystic Arts in Teyvat: Astrology and Hydromancy
184.content:
Astrology infers fate from the movements of stars. Barbeloth and her student Mona practise it; hydromancy is the subclass in which the starlight's inverted reflection on water is read. Mona says reading your own fate makes it turn in on itself and advising a subject can entangle your fates. The Traveler's fate cannot be read this way. Pyromancy is a presumed fire divination known only from a single note.

In the Witch's Revelation system, Barbeloth's case of oracles and the Lunar Arcana are tied to her readings (see the Witchcraft entry).

185.comment: Mystic Arts in Teyvat: Adeptus Arts
185.content:
The adepti's arts were taught to them by Rex Lapis. Besides controlling the elements, adepti can make elixirs, give or receive dreams, remain in human form after death, use yaksha masks, store power in talismans, and create pocket dimensions with teapot-spirit servants. See the Adeptal Arts entry.

The Fatui duplicated Sigils of Permission through research, and Tartaglia used many of them with his Harbinger power to reawaken Osial.

186.comment: Mystic Arts in Teyvat: Art of Homa
186.content: A secret technique of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor that purifies fetor, the leakage of death into the world of the living. Hu Tao says it needs great focus and no hesitation; mistakes can shorten the practitioner's life. Wuwang Kid passed it to the Parlor's founders after the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame's death.

187.comment: Mystic Arts in Teyvat: Qimen Arts
187.content: A set of Liyue techniques including fortune-telling, fate transference, illusion-making and warding off evil, originated by the Wind Reader of the Eight Adepts. The Lan Clan of Chenyu Vale uses them for both duty and craft; one form uses rattan figures. Lan Junming also taught a Soul-Binding Art that was later outlawed.

188.content: Liyue's exorcists (thaumaturges) swear to cleanse the land of ghosts, spirits and demons and are skilled in combat, magic and martial arts. Most come from families that hold the trade, among them the Tianheng Thaumaturges (Chongyun, and Shenhe's mother), Yelan's clan and the Lan Clan. Their arts seem derived from adeptal arts; every exorcist seen using them in-game has a Vision. See the Exorcism entry.

189.content: Inazuma's Kamuna art of paper-based charm magic, created by Kamuna Harunosuke 500 years ago from adeptal techniques and the tengu art of transcension. Shikigami are enchanted paper cut-outs; shikifuda are elemental seals. It is largely lost, though the Kairagi use shikifuda, and its techniques survive in devices like the Ubiquity Nets and the Mystic Onmyou Chamber.

190.content: The Aranara's memory-fuelled abilities. Each Aranara has a unique power that can attack, teleport or shield against the Withering, spends their memories when used, and can grow with new memories. A Kusava seed amplifies it and lets humans use it briefly.

191.comment: Mystic Arts in Teyvat: Akasha System
191.content: Sumeru's Gnosis-powered knowledge network, created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and developed by the Akademiya. A terminal gives its user any knowledge they seek; Lesser Lord Kusanali calls herself the first Akasha Terminal. Terminals can also work without the Akasha, from stored Canned Knowledge in Knowledge Capsules.

192.content:
Nightsoul's Blessing (also: Nightsouls, Nightsoul Burst, Nightsoul Transmission, Nightsoul Points, Nightsoul-aligned): Nightsoul's Blessing is the power state of Natlan's warriors. Natlan's dead enter the Night Kingdom, a realm of souls beneath the land; the souls there are called Nightsouls, and Natlanese fighters borrow their strength to run, climb, swim, leap and fight beyond what they could alone. The Wayob, spirits venerated by the six tribes, live in that realm, which the Lord of the Night made. It is a Natlan power tied to the land's own rules, not an element.

In play, the state is entered mostly through a character's Elemental Skill, runs on a pool of Nightsoul points, and is stronger inside Natlan. It is separate from the Vision system, though many Natlanese fighters use both.

In universe: In story terms, the Night Kingdom is "a liminal space between the body and mind, life and death," deep underground. Natlanese people go there when they die and slowly lose themselves into a sea of souls. Living warriors can draw on those Nightsouls to enhance their abilities, which is Nightsoul's Blessing.

The Night Kingdom effectively works as Natlan's Ley Lines. Natlan lacks stable, deep Ley Lines, and the original ones were badly damaged in the War of Funerary Flame. The Lord of the Night, guided by Ronova, rebuilt a similar network from the fragments; the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, strengthened it later. Memories gained in Natlan are recorded there. Experiences outside Natlan are not, which is why Xilonen needed the Lord of the Night's help to forge an Ancient Name for the Traveler.

Item text in the Obsidian Codex artifact set tells how the realm's contact with the living began: the human Chaac, the last of his companions, climbed a mountain on his final night, lit the first flame and called out; the god of the night realm answered, and the first Wayob was born in that moment. Natlan's tribes later each had their own Wayob, to whom they pray for protection and whose will they read in the dreams of their chiefs.

The Abyss's long effects can leave Natlanese people without the Wayob's protection prone to memory loss, stress and bad luck, which is why most stay inside Natlan; leaving needs the approval of the Wayob through the tribal chief. The Wayob cannot extend their protection abroad without spending power reserved for fighting the Abyss.

Wayob and night kingdom: The Wayob are described by the Dreamseeker Priest as non-corporeal "will without form or thought." They live in the Night Kingdom and can see the past and future. Each tribe has its own Wayob, and the Wayob choose who receives an Ancient Name. They are not physically in Natlan, but they can appear through obsidian totems and Nightsouls as Wayob Manifestations. Natlan's people do not know why these appear; the common belief is that they are sent to solve some problem.

The Night Kingdom was created by Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, who was once an angel. After the cataclysm 500 years ago, Abyssal forces overran it. For centuries the Wayob fought them without rest, and that war wore down their strength and their link to the people. By the time of Natlan's Archon Quests, Mavuika estimated the realm would be destroyed in under a year.

The Weaver of Secrets, a Dragonlord, merged her consciousness into the Night Kingdom, making a "dream labyrinth" where the souls of dead dragons and humans can rest, and keeps a pact of protection with the Masters of the Night-Wind (per weapon item text).

Ancient names and death: Ancient Names are obsidian-stone titles carried by chosen members of the tribes. Their deeds become part of the Name's legacy. Each is granted by a tribe's Wayob to someone who has lived out its spirit, or is forged on commission of the Pyro Archon by a Name Engraver at a cost to the smith's lifespan. A bearer who fell in the Night Warden Wars can be returned by the Ode of Resurrection if their group won against the Abyss. If no one returned victorious, the Name is lost for good. A bearer who dies in some other way is reborn in Natlan eventually, in another form.

Ronova, Ruler of Death, is the source of the Ode's power: she let Xbalanque borrow it. The Night Kingdom records Natlan's memories, which is why only Natlan's deeds could serve as the basis for a Name until the Lord of the Night made the Pilgrim's Chronicle for the Traveler.

Last changes: After the Abyss was repelled from Natlan, the Fatui Harbinger Capitano exchanged his own death for Mavuika's, merging his life force with the Lord of the Night to rewrite the Ley Lines' rules. Afterwards, people from outside Natlan are accepted into the Night Kingdom, and the Lord of the Night returned to maintain it. The Traveler's Sibling later met with her and obtained the Ley Lines for New Khaenri'ah, stored in an Atlas.

Known uses: Entering the state boosts mobility and fighting power; characters often move in ways ordinary people cannot. Kachina, for instance, rides Turbo Twirly while she has points left, and the state ends when they run out.

Nightsoul Transmission lets a Natlan character swiftly run, climb, swim or jump after a swap. Nightsoul Burst is a periodic surge triggered by elemental damage when a Natlanese character is in the party. Nightsoul points are gained or spent by each character in their own way; when they run out or when certain abilities are used, Phlogiston is drawn instead.

- Nightsoul-aligned damage is better at breaking Void Wards (three times as effective) and the shields summoned by Wayob Manifestations.
- Nightsoul Totems, obsidian totems around Natlan, send the player into the Night Kingdom to attempt combat trials.
- Characters tied to Natlan with the state include the Pyro Archon Mavuika and fighters such as Kinich, Mualani, Xilonen, Chasca, Ororon, Citlali, Kachina, Iansan, Varesa and Ifa. How each uses it differs by character.

Limits: It is a Natlan power: it works best in Natlan and relies on the Night Kingdom's support.

The state ends when a character's Nightsoul points are exhausted. The Night Kingdom has no record of deeds outside Natlan, and in canon the Wayob protect their people poorly abroad.

Nightsoul-aligned damage has no special effect in ordinary fights, only against Void Wards and Wayob Manifestation shields. Nightsoul Burst does nothing by itself; only certain talents and artifacts react to it.

Interactions: Phlogiston: Natlan's primordial energy, a form of Pyro, powers many Natlan devices and Saurian abilities, and is drawn on when Nightsoul points are gone.

Visions and the Elements: Nightsoul's Blessing is not an element, so it rides on whatever element a character wields. Burning is a fast way to wear down a Void Ward without the state.

The Abyss is the common enemy of the Wayob and the Night Kingdom. Per Beneath the Secret Source, the Heavenly Principles modified elemental energy on a Phlogiston basis to counter the Abyss.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): the state is entered mainly through Elemental Skills, enhances movement and combat, and is boosted in Natlan. Nightsoul Burst triggers on elemental damage with an interval of 18 seconds for one Natlanese character in the party, 12 for two and 9 for three or more, marked by a white screen outline. The mechanics arrived with Natlan in Version 5.0.

Night Realm's Gift passive talents give each Natlan character their Transmission movement. An achievement, Imperishable Night, asks the player to hold the state for 18 seconds.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show it as quiet weight: ember-lit patterns of soul-light, a sense of ancestors close by, a body suddenly lighter. Natlanese characters treat it as ordinary inheritance and take it with humour or pride. Keep respect for the dead.

Do not let an outsider simply use it, and do not give a non-Natlanese character a clear grasp of the mechanism. Let characters mention the Wayob as guardians who fight the Abyss. Do not turn the Night Kingdom into a generic afterlife of punishment.

Avoid claiming Nightsoul's Blessing appears in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya; as of 7.1 canon has not shown it there.

193.content:
The Night Kingdom is the realm of the Wayob and the souls of Natlan's dead, made by Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, from fragments of the old Ley Lines, and it serves as Natlan's Ley Lines. Natlanese souls lose themselves there into a sea of souls. Souls of warriors who die in Natlan's ritual wars can be recalled by the Ode of Resurrection if their group wins.

The Abyss invaded it after the cataclysm and was driven out in the Archon Quest; Gosoythoth fled to its deepest parts and was destroyed there by the Traveler and Mavuika.

194.content: The Wayob are the spirits of the six tribes, believed to embody the will of tribal ancestors. They guard their people and choose who bears an Ancient Name. They can appear in Natlan as obsidian-tied Wayob Manifestations, which are also elite enemies in play.

195.content: An Ancient Name is a title and a stone representing the deeds of all its past bearers, chosen by a Wayob or forged on the Pyro Archon's commission. If a bearer dies in the Night Warden Wars and nobody in the group returns victorious, the Name is lost.

196.content: A periodic surge that triggers when a party containing a Natlanese character deals elemental damage. On its own it does nothing; some talents and artifacts add effects.

197.content:
Overloaded (also: Overloaded reaction, Overloaded DMG, Pyro-Electro reaction): Overloaded is the elemental reaction between Pyro and Electro, in either order. It causes an explosion that deals area Pyro damage and throws nearby targets back. It is a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction that a scene may borrow from, not a named law of the world.

Overloaded has existed since Version 1.0. It is a transformative reaction, meaning it deals its own damage separate from the attack that triggered it. The in-game tutorial calls it a powerful explosion and tells players to alternate Pyro and Electro attacks to trigger it.

In universe: Canon gives no story explanation for Overloaded. The in-game tutorial only says that when Pyro meets Electro, or Electro meets Pyro, Overloaded occurs, causing powerful explosions that deal area Pyro damage.

Nothing read ties the reaction to a character, god or event. Do not invent an origin. Fire and lightning causing a blast is a natural image for a scene, but treat it as flavour.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Overloaded happens when Electro hits a target carrying Pyro, or Pyro hits a target carrying Electro. The explosion deals area Pyro damage in a roughly 5 metre radius and causes strong knockback.

- It does not apply Pyro to the targets it hits, so it cannot set off further reactions by itself.
- Overloaded damage counts as a blunt attack, so it can trigger Shatter on Frozen targets and is more effective against certain enemy shields.
- Like other transformative reactions, its damage depends on the level of the character who triggers it and is raised by that character's Elemental Mastery. It cannot CRIT.

- One target can take only one instance of Overloaded damage every 0.5 seconds from the same attacker, and several Overloaded reactions on the same target within 0.1 seconds produce damage only once, whatever their source.
- Certain artifact sets raise Overloaded damage.
- The explosion causes significant knockback; the wiki's preview also shows Overloaded damaging ore deposits.
- Elemental Resonance (two or more Electro characters, High Voltage) interacts with Overloaded; see the Electro entry.

- Overloaded is unchanged by the newer reaction families. As of Version 7.1 the wiki's reaction table lists Pyro with Electro as Overloaded, alongside Lunar and Stellar Glimmer reactions that replace other Electro reactions in matching parties.
- The Pyro element in the blast is a damage type only: Overloaded does not leave a Pyro aura, unlike Burning, which keeps applying Pyro.

Limits: Overloaded needs both elements on the same target and does nothing to a target with only one. The knockback can scatter enemies instead of keeping them together.

The explosion is fixed-size and tied to the triggering character's level, so a weak character does not produce a huge blast. Pyro-immune enemies reduce its damage.

Examples: Gameplay example from the in-game tutorial: switch characters in battle and use Pyro and Electro attacks in turn to trigger Overloaded and defeat opponents quickly. The wiki's preview shows an Overloaded blast on an enemy and one used to break open ore.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Overloaded as a sharp bang of purple lightning and orange flame, with a shockwave that shoves people and loose objects back. Keep it a single blast, loud and brief, not a lasting fire.

Narratively, Overloaded is chaos: great for a scene where two characters with opposing Visions clash by accident or on purpose. Characters can be knocked off their feet, but the blast should not be lethal for an ordinary person unless the scene calls for it. Cover, ringing ears and scorched cloth are proportionate.

Avoid describing Overloaded as a way to demolish buildings or to destroy gods. Do not have it light a lasting fire; that is Burning, a different reaction with Dendro.

198.content: Overloaded is a transformative reaction, along with Shattered, Electro-Charged, Superconduct, Swirl, Burning, Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon. Each deals its own damage based on its type and the triggering character's level, raised by Elemental Mastery. This damage cannot CRIT, ignores the target's DEF in practice, and is still affected by resistance.

199.content:
Party (also: Party Setup, party system, character switching, team composition): A party is a team of up to four playable characters. The player controls one at a time and can swap to another with a short delay. Team bonuses such as Elemental Resonance apply to the party as a whole.

The ability to set up parties unlocks after the quest "Unexpected Power".

In universe: Gameplay abstraction: in the story the Traveler travels with a handful of friends, but canon never states a four-person limit or an instant swap between them. Treat party swapping as the game's way of presenting who is fighting rather than a rule of the world.

Gameplay: Gameplay: switching characters has a 1-second cooldown. Up to four characters are deployed, added left to right, and a team with none cannot be deployed. Trial-character stages can add a fifth, the trial character, to a full party of four.

Party Setup is opened from the Paimon Menu or with L on PC. There are four default teams ("Party 1" to "Party 4"), which can be renamed but not disbanded, and a maximum of 15 teams.
