The deployed team cannot be disbanded. Characters can be reordered by dragging, and the Configure Team and Quick Setup menus help manage them. The Party Setup background can change by region, with variants for Nod-Krai (also depending on Moonsign characters) and Snezhnaya (depending on Stellar Linchpin characters), if the player enables that setting.

Some talents, Constellations, weapon passives and artifacts only work while the character stays on the field, so effects can end after a swap; others apply to the whole party. Co-Op Mode keeps the total at four: two players get 2 each; three players get 2, 1 and 1; four players get 1 each. Most food effects do not apply to characters owned by another player.

In Version 1.0 a bug let a player field five characters through revival, related to the fact that the party system supports five to fit a trial character. Many characters show an object, elemental effect or companion in their Party Setup animation; Venti, Zhongli, the Raiden Shogun and Nahida keep a persistent elemental effect after it finishes, and Charlotte and Tartaglia are the only ones whose outfits stay changed.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay (this project's interpretation, not canon): in fiction, the Traveler's friends take turns in a fight and cover for each other. Avoid telling characters they have been "swapped out"; treat it as people stepping in and out of a battle.

Limits: The four-character limit, cooldown and menu are mechanics. Canon does not limit how many friends the Traveler may have around them.

200.content:
Phlogiston (also: primal flame, Natlan Phlogiston, Liquid Phlogiston, Solid Phlogiston, Gaseous Phlogiston): Phlogiston is the primal energy of Natlan. People there can sense and use it: it powers machines, written signs and the Nightsoul's Blessing state of Natlan's warriors. It exists as liquid, solid and gaseous forms and flows along Spiritways. Canon calls it Teyvat's primordial energy and a form of "computronium", programmable matter that stores information. The dragon Kukulkan stole it and taught humans to use it.

The Heavenly Principles later reworked elemental energy using phlogiston as a base, so elemental energy is described as phlogiston's modern counterpart. Natlanese treat phlogiston as a symbol of an indomitable spirit.

Phlogiston is also the reason Natlan is a target: in earlier ages the Heavenly Principles treated Natlan's phlogiston-rich soil as a "Holy Soil" phenomenon and cast sky-nails down at it, according to Kukulkan.

In universe: In the world: Natlan's people use phlogiston for devices, signs, paints and warrior abilities. It carries heat and is dangerous to those who cannot handle it, but the Natlanese, nearly all of whom can use it, read it and work with it directly.

Phlogiston can appear as a gas that leaks from the ground and flows in currents, as a flowing liquid, and as solid crystals or blocks. Natlanese craft solid phlogiston into barrels, targets and nails. Item text describes it as a high-temperature thermal energy found throughout Natlan "in all shapes and sizes", and warriors switch to drawing on it to keep their Nightsoul's Blessing going once their Nightsoul runs out.

Those who can use phlogiston can read words recorded in Phlogiston Engravings by sensing the phlogiston inside them, so formal study of the writing is partly seen as obsolete. Two prominent modern uses of engraving are Ancient Name forging by the Children of Echoes, who carve names into obsidian, and Nightspirit graffiti made by the Masters of the Night-Wind with painted engravings that only their spiritspeakers can activate. According to Ororon, painted engravings can be activated with either phlogiston or elemental energy.

Saurians also draw on phlogiston: in gameplay indwelling one grants it extra phlogiston storage, and a soldier's diary links the Fatui's capture of Saurians to phlogiston and their special constitution. Item text notes that Qucusaurs and some members of the Flower-Feather Clan have learned to use gaseous phlogiston without being burned. Phlogiston Chiseliths are devices that can be infused with phlogiston to open mechanisms, based on the older inscriptions.

Origins: Phlogiston is one of Teyvat's ancient forms of energy. In the Archon Quest "Beneath the Secret Source" (5.1), the Lord of the Night explains that phlogiston is Teyvat's primordial energy, that it belongs to the Light Realm, and that elemental energy is built on it: as he puts it, light splits into seven colours like a rainbow, and elemental energy is a similar idea, the modern counterpart of phlogiston. The Heavenly Principles developed it to counter the Abyss better.

The wiki flags that the English line is somewhat misleading; the Chinese text is read as the Principles modifying elemental energy to share phlogiston's properties rather than making it from phlogiston. The Primordial Sea and kuuvahki, the power of Nod-Krai's moons, are cited as other ancient, primordial forms of energy alongside phlogiston.

How elemental energy relates to the seven elements, Visions and the Archons' Authorities is told elsewhere (see the elements entry); this entry covers phlogiston itself.

Dragons and computronium: In the world quest "An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty" (5.5), Kukulkan tells the Traveler that phlogiston is an atom on which information can be written, a form of "computronium" that can imitate the essence of anything through the weaving of language, which is why it takes on different forms. The ancient dragons used it this way. Their golden script, Iridescent Inscriptions, works as a programming language for phlogiston: it records information, controls Secret Source mechanisms, converts phlogiston between forms, creates Spiritways and lets dragons reshape their own appearance.

Natlan's ruins still hold dragon-era phlogiston recordings. Modern researchers have made little progress deciphering the inscriptions, and the Saurian Relics Association has posted bounties for it. Human Phlogiston Engravings are a simpler imitation, and a considerable gap in complexity separates the two.

Kukulkan also describes Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array built by the dragon Xiuhcoatl, as a device meant to turn all of Natlan into phlogiston or matter made of it, so that information is transcribed into phlogiston and the Abyss destroyed, at the cost of all life dying or becoming phlogiston lifeforms. The wiki's account says Kukulkan and Xbalanque split its key, the two Golden Entreaties, to keep it from ever being activated.

Kukulkan and humans: The dragon Kukulkan, called the Sage of the Stolen Flame, took phlogiston from his kin and taught humans in Natlan to use it. Natlanese tradition names him the origin of their ability to use it.

Per the wiki's account of Natlan's history, he foresaw the dragons' fall and believed humanity would find salvation if knowledge were shared. He taught his first human disciple, and the first wielders formed Natlan's first settled tribe. The dragons later accused him of betrayal and the Lords and Princes moved to impeach him. When tribes began using phlogiston as a weapon against each other, he withdrew from the world. Some Natlanese believe he was in fact human.

Forms: Gaseous, liquid and solid phlogiston, and Spiritways.

- Gaseous: free-flowing heat, leaking from the ground or forming currents and wind tunnels. It burns those who cannot handle it.
- Liquid: a molten flow that ignites those who touch it, but is safe for Saurians of certain kinds and certain characters.
- Solid: orange crystals or blocks used for tools and barriers.
- Spiritway: a flowing channel carrying travellers in the Nightsoul's Blessing state.

Spiritways are a phlogiston-based channel type created by the dragons through inscription. Modern humans can stabilise or create new ones with Phlogiston Engraving in the form of Spiritdoors. Spiritways may be one-way or bidirectional.

In the world quest at the Heart of the Sacred Mountain, the Traveler describes immersion in liquid phlogiston as an experience that gave a flood of images and wisdom, and Kukulkan afterward confirms that the information and wisdom of ancient times lie within the primal flame.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Phlogiston is a shared party meter in Natlan, capped at 100. It is consumed once Nightsoul points run out and by Saurian Indwelling abilities, and it is refilled by collecting items, breaking objects and standing near certain features. It is not available in domains.

Liquid phlogiston drains 5% of max HP every 0.25 seconds and applies Pyro to those it touches; gaseous phlogiston drains 2.5% every 0.5 seconds. Solid phlogiston can be passed through only by certain Saurian forms, Children of Echoes characters and Mavuika. Filling one level of a Phlogiston Chiselith costs 25 phlogiston. Natlan characters such as Xilonen, Mualani and Chasca have talents that generate it.

The wiki lists the common sources: the Pyro Crystalfly, Embercore Flower, Phlogiston Aphid and Candlecap Mushroom, Dracolite, Pulverite, Phlogiston Piles, Recon Targets and Rings, Statues of The Seven and Teleport Waypoints.

Fatui extraction: The Fatui run a secret underground base in Natlan's Coatepec Mountain, the Phlogiston Extraction Research Center, where they extract phlogiston from captured Saurians. Fontaine Research Institute equipment is used there, though it is unclear how much the Institute knows about what it is used for. A soldier's diary in the base says the soldiers do not know the purpose of the research.

The base's emergency manual mentions plans to adapt its machinery to run on Natlan's lava. These are minor details from item text and carry no larger revelation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, phlogiston remains Natlan's central energy resource and symbol. No later canon found in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya chapters changes what is said above. Huitzilopochtli is covered in its own entry.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat phlogiston as the everyday lifeblood of Natlan: warm, flowing, taken for granted by locals and alarming to outsiders who step into it. Natlanese characters sense it the way others sense a smell, so they notice engravings, leaks and Saurians' condition without tools. Outsiders from other nations should treat liquid or gaseous phlogiston as dangerous.

Keep phlogiston distinct from Pyro in scenes: it can be liquid, gas or solid, is a source of information as well as heat, and is associated with ancient dragon writing. Do not have characters casually reprogram matter with it; only dragons and the Iridescent Inscriptions did so in canon, and modern engraving is a limited imitation.

Do not claim the Heavenly Principles simply created elemental energy out of phlogiston without noting that the exact wording is disputed. Do not invent a Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya use of phlogiston.

201.content:
Iridescent Inscriptions are the golden script the ancient dragons of Natlan used to wield phlogiston, essentially a programming language for matter. Humans imitated it as Phlogiston Engravings, which can store text, build Spiritdoors and Phlogiston Chiseliths, and underlie Ancient Name carving and Nightspirit graffiti.

Surviving inscriptions are scattered and mostly undeciphered; the Saurian Relics Association has issued research bounties. Phlogiston users can read engravings by sensing the phlogiston inside them.

202.content: Huitzilopochtli is a device built by Xiuhcoatl to convert Natlan into phlogiston and destroy the Abyss. According to Kukulkan in the 5.5 world quest, it works by transcribing information into phlogiston, with life either dying or becoming phlogiston lifeforms. It needs the two Golden Entreaties to be reunited to activate. Kukulkan and Xbalanque are said to have split them to prevent that.

203.content: A secret Fatui base under Coatepec Mountain where phlogiston is extracted from captured Saurians. It uses Fontaine Research Institute equipment. Staff there write that the purpose of the research was never explained to them.

204.comment: Phlogiston: Liquid and gaseous Phlogiston hazards
204.content: Liquid phlogiston burns those who enter it, gaseous phlogiston burns those who stand in its currents, and solid phlogiston forms crystals and blocks used for devices. Qucusaurs and some Flower-Feather Clan members have mastered gaseous phlogiston without being burned, and Koholasaurs and certain characters move through liquid phlogiston safely.

205.content:
Physical (also: Physical damage, Physical DMG, non-elemental damage): Physical is the eighth damage type in Genshin Impact: ordinary force with no element in it, such as a sword cut, a hammer blow or a crushing impact. The other seven damage types are the elements. Physical has no Archon, nation or Vision. It is a game category rather than a power the story names.

Elemental reactions are built from the seven elements, so Physical normally sits outside them. The main exception is Shatter, which deals Physical damage.

In universe: Canon never presents Physical as a force or Authority. In the story, a strike without elemental energy is just a strike: steel, muscle, teeth, claws or falling stone.

This is the main difference from the elements. The elements are tied to Visions, Gnoses, Archons and the Dragon Sovereigns, while Physical has nothing comparable. In narration, treat "Physical" as the absence of elemental energy, not as an eighth element.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Sword, Claymore and Polearm attacks deal Physical DMG by default. So do Bow Normal Attacks and Aimed Shots that are not fully charged. Catalyst attacks are inherently elemental, so Catalyst users deal Physical DMG only through extra effects.

Some Elemental Skills and Bursts also deal Physical DMG. The wiki's examples are Eula's Glacial Illumination, Xinyan's Riff Revolution and Freminet's Pressurized Floe. Physical DMG Bonus is a stat, found as a character ascension stat, a weapon substat or an artifact bonus (for instance the 2-piece bonus of Bloodstained Chivalry or Pale Flame, +25%). Physical RES is the matching defence. Enemies can deal Physical damage too; the Stonehide Lawachurl's punches, charge and slam are examples.

- Shatter: a Frozen target hit by a blunt attack (Claymore attacks count) or a Geo attack takes Physical Shatter damage and is unfrozen. It is the best-known source of Physical damage inside the reaction system.
- Superconduct (Electro with Cryo) lowers the enemy's Physical RES by 40% for 12 seconds.
- Elemental Resonance: Protective Canopy (a party of four different elements) raises Physical RES together with all Elemental RES by 15%.
- Catalyst exceptions: some Catalyst weapons, such as Skyward Atlas, and artifact sets such as Ocean-Hued Clam (its Sea-Dyed Foam) can add Physical damage to a Catalyst user. Bonuses to Physical DMG do not all apply: Sea-Dyed Foam is affected by enemy Physical RES but not by Physical DMG Bonus.

Damage in general: there are eight damage types, and enemy RES is tracked separately for Elemental and Physical damage. Physical damage applies no element, so it cannot start an elemental reaction. A Physical attack can only unfreeze or shatter a target as described above.

Limits: Physical does not react with any element and applies no aura.

No Vision or Gnosis grants Physical power. A character cannot "have a Physical element".

Gameplay: the character stat screen lists Physical DMG Bonus beside the seven Elemental DMG Bonuses, which is why the damage type is easy to mistake for an element.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Physical as weight, edge and momentum: a clean cut, a heavy blow, ground shaking from a slam. It has no signature colour or glow, and nothing about it needs special explanation.

A sword fighter without a Vision is dangerous because of skill and training, not Physical power. When ice cracks under a hammer blow, that is Shatter, so describe the freeze breaking under force.

Avoid calling Physical "the eighth element", linking it to an Archon, or inventing a Physical Vision or resonance.

206.content: Shatter is the reaction in which a blunt hit (a Claymore attack, for example) or a Geo attack lands on a target frozen by the Frozen reaction. The ice breaks and the hit deals Physical damage. See the Shattered entry for the full reaction.

207.content: Physical RES reduces incoming Physical damage. Protective Canopy resonance, certain talents, constellations, artifacts and dishes can raise it. Superconduct lowers an enemy's Physical RES by 40% for 12 seconds, and some talents, constellations and artifacts can lower it too.

208.content:
Prime Ice (also: Prime Ice Construct, Prime Ice Constructs, Prime Ice Resource, Fab-Vision): Prime Ice is a pale ice found across Snezhnaya that does not melt like ordinary frost. The Traveler can harvest it with the Fab-Vision function of the Eye of Graeae to gain Prime Ice Resource, then spend that resource, plus Kresnik Energy, to build Prime Ice Constructs: heat sources, grappling hooks, launch pads and more. Constructs can be taken down again for a refund of the ice.

It is introduced in the Archon Quest "Into the Wind, Into the Frigid North" (7.0), where the Eye of Graeae teaches the Traveler to clear blocking ice and prop up a door with a cube. It is an exploration tool, not a combat element.

In universe: In-world, Prime Ice is a durable ice native to Snezhnaya. The townsfolk of Svetloledovka make a living by harvesting it. Ordinary humans cannot shape it, but Snowland Fae can manipulate it naturally.

The Eye of Graeae, a device-bound entity, is the Traveler's way of working it. It tells the Traveler that constructs last only briefly and cannot be stabilised during the development period, so it was allowed to use Kresnik Kristall as a heat source. The Eye also says it has forgotten what warmth feels like. Item text describes the glaciafruit, a star-shaped fruit, as born from Prime Ice after a peculiar change in the permafrost, "for reasons unknown".

Prime Ice also appears as scenery that people cannot rebuild: ornaments on city buildings, vases in Svetloledovka, windows in White Birch Snowgrave, floors in the House of Hesperides, hats on Jack Frosts. These show the material is part of Snezhnayan architecture and craft, not only a puzzle obstacle. Canon does not link Prime Ice to Cryo power, a Cryo Gnosis or a Vision.

The Eye of Graeae is described on the wiki as a creation of Aksinya and the Hvergelmir, split into three segments before the Cataclysm for the "prototype human" experiment; the Traveler restores its scattered power in the 7.0 Archon Quest and later sends it and Aksinya into the Shadow Realm. The device the Traveler keeps retains every function, Fab-Vision included, but loses the personality. Whether Prime Ice itself was part of that experiment is not stated.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Fab-Vision is a mode of the Eye of Graeae gadget, usable in Snezhnaya while running, falling or fighting but not while gliding or swimming. Harvesting a deposit gives Prime Ice Resource (most deposits roughly 15 to 70 units; the largest are rare, often do not respawn and fill the 400-unit storage). Building spends resource and a percentage of Kresnik Energy; removing a construct refunds the resource.

- Each construct type has a per-area placement limit. By default the oldest of that type is replaced and refunded; this can be switched off in Construct Details.
- Constructs placed in an invalid spot are destroyed and the resource refunded, but the Kresnik Energy spent is not. Most are destroyed (and refunded) if a train hits them.
- Standard constructs and their roles: Cube (raises or blocks things), Basic Heat Source (warms the player so Kresnik Energy is not drained), Link Mechanism (paired grappling line between points), Grappling Gun (pulls to hooks), Launching Platform (higher ground; also launches juvenile Jack Frosts), Storage Device (item storage), Ambient Bollard (periodic buff), Sign: Icon and Sign: Text (messages for other explorers).
- Blueprints: Cube and Basic Heat Source are unlocked in "Into the Wind, Into the Frigid North"; the rest after "Gunfire in the Silent Lands".
- Inside a Polestar Field, usually from a Starlight Prism, most constructs get extra effects: the Cube applies Cryo, the Basic Heat Source generates Kresnik Energy, the Grappling Gun and Launching Platform reach further, and Ambient Bollard buffs are stronger.

- Temporary Blueprints are short-lived constructs copied from a quest or location (matryoshka doll, snowball launcher, blockade spikes, phonograph, animal statues, resonant pillar, seats, gift box, wall pieces and others). Only one can be held, and it expires once the player travels far from where it was copied. Several come from limited-time or quest content.
- Co-op constructs: constructs built by other players can appear in your world, can be liked by players and NPCs, can be removed or anchored from the map, and sharing can be switched off in permission settings.
- Alternate appearances for some constructs unlock through exploration: Jack Frost (bought at the Jack Frosts' Goodies Shop), Polyarbear (a quest reward), and Ballerina, Hound and Tides bollard looks from Meeting Point rewards.
- Starlight Prisms made by Stellar-Conduct behave much like constructs once reactivated from a Prism Mirage.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Eye of Graeae's tools as a craft, not magic anyone can learn. The Traveler can spend the Eye's stored resource to raise a wall, a stair or a warm brazier, and gives the material back by taking the thing down. Describe pale, hard ice that shapes quickly under Fab-Vision and stays cold to the touch. Keep scale small: bridges, hooks and braziers, not fortresses.

- A Prime Ice heat source works because of Kresnik Kristall; without that, it is simply ice. Do not let characters warm themselves on Prime Ice alone.
- Snowland Fae can shape Prime Ice by instinct. A Fae watching the Traveler build can be impressed or amused, since a human needs a gadget.
- Because constructs are short-lived in canon, a lasting Prime Ice structure should have a stated reason.

- Do not give Prime Ice shaping to Cryo Vision holders as a general ability, and do not imply the Traveler does it without the Eye.
- Do not say Prime Ice is the Cryo Archon's power, a Gnosis or a Vision; canon makes no such link.

Examples: Scene seeds: the Traveler places a cube to hold up a sagging door while a Jack Frost slips under it; a Basic Heat Source keeps a group of travellers from freezing at a train station; a grappling line crosses a gorge; a storage device left at a camp lets a later traveller find supplies. All of these use gadget mechanics from the 7.0 content.

Limits: Prime Ice constructs can only be built in Snezhnaya using the Eye of Graeae. Each type has a limit per area, and the Traveler can only carry 400 units of resource.

Fab-Vision cannot be used while gliding or swimming. Kresnik Energy is needed to build, and is used up faster in colder zones. Constructs cannot be stacked or placed where the player is standing.

Items left in a storage device are not refunded if the device is removed, and withdrawals are capped each day. Treat all of these as mechanics, not world rules.

209.content:
A Prime Ice Construct is any object the Traveler builds from Prime Ice Resource with the Eye of Graeae, unlocked by blueprints. They are short-lived by design, can be removed for a refund, and many gain extra effects inside a Polestar Field. The first constructs the Traveler learns are the Cube and the Basic Heat Source.

The Eye of Graeae explains that Prime Ice Constructs last only briefly and cannot be stabilised during the development period, so it was authorised to rely on Kresnik Kristall. See the main Prime Ice entry for each construct's role.

210.content: Prime Ice Resource is the material stored in the Eye of Graeae's internal reservoir. Item text says it can be used to build the mechanisms and constructs in the blueprints. It is gained by harvesting Prime Ice or deconstructing constructs, and the gadget holds at most 400 units.

211.content: Glaciafruit is a star-shaped fruit that grows from a Prime Ice branch on the Snezhnayan tundra. Taking the branch away with the Eye of Graeae drops the fruit into the snow and returns a little Prime Ice Resource. Item text says it forms from Prime Ice for reasons unknown; it is edible and used in cooking.

212.comment: Prime Ice: Starlight Prism and Polestar Field
212.content: A Starlight Prism is the result of Stellar-Conduct, a Stellar Glimmer reaction between Cryo and Electro. It sustains a Polestar Field around it, which gives nearby constructs and characters bonuses and keeps characters from losing heat or Kresnik Energy in Snezhnaya. In the open world, a prism left standing can become a Prism Mirage that the player can reactivate to last indefinitely, like a construct.

213.content:
Pyro (also: Pyro element, element of fire, Pyro Archon's element): Pyro is the element of fire, one of Teyvat's seven elements. Its Archon is the God of War and bears the divine name Haborym; the current Pyro Archon is Mavuika, who rules Natlan, the land of Pyro. Unlike other Archons, Pyro Archons are mortals who win the throne in battle. People with Pyro Visions ignite, burn and explode things. The Pyro Gnosis never reached the Fatui; as of 7.1 it has vanished.

Pyro ascension gems are Agnidus Agates. Natlan's Statues of The Seven take Pyroculi. The Pyro Archon looks after the Sacred Flame, the fire that protects Natlan and its warriors.

In universe: Most people use Pyro through a Vision. A Pyro Archon draws on the Sacred Flame and the Pyro Archon's divine throne instead. In Natlan the element is bound up with war, oaths and the idea that humans can become gods.

Natlan's culture treats fire as something earned in contest. Contending Fire, the energy produced when Natlanese warriors fight each other, fuels the Sacred Flame, especially through the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Objects carried in battle can also become soaked with Contending Fire and be burned to feed it. Elsewhere in Teyvat, Pyro is the ordinary element of campfires, forges, kitchens and fireworks.

Pyro is also linked to Phlogiston, Teyvat's primordial form of energy. Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, could manipulate Phlogiston and presided over light, heat and wisdom. According to the Archon Quest as summarised on the wiki, he was born from the primal flame on the Sacred Mountain and used it to make his younger brother Kukulkan and the other Pyro dragons of Natlan.

Origins: Origins, as canon tells them. The elemental Authorities first belonged to the Seven Sovereigns, the great elemental dragons of the old world. The Heavenly Principles stole portions of those powers and tied them to the Divine Thrones, which became the Archons' Authorities (revealed in the Fontaine Archon Quest, 4.1). Xiuhcoatl's Pyro Authority was among them: the Heavenly Principles took part of it and froze him in lava, a "false death". Visions derive from these Authorities. Later, in the Natlan Archon Quest (5.1), the Lord of the Night says the Heavenly Principles made elemental energy by splitting the raw currents of the Light Realm into seven on a base of Phlogiston, to be easier to control and to counter the Abyss. How an Archon relates to their element is not explained.

Archon and nation: Archon: the Pyro Archon, God of War among The Seven, divine name Haborym. Current holder: Mavuika. Nation: Natlan.

Every Pyro Archon begins as a human and wins the position through battle. They stay mortal: they age and die, so Natlan has had many Pyro Archons. When a new one takes the divine throne, an inner flame awakens and the Sacred Flame hands them deep knowledge and memory of the land. They are also charged with protecting and fuelling the Sacred Flame.

The first Pyro Archon was Xbalanque, who established the "rules" by which ordinary people can ascend; he is said to have killed Xiuhcoatl about 2,000 years ago and returned to life wreathed in fire. A second, scarlet-eyed youth of the Tlalocan tribe is credited with leading the tribes against Och-Kan and asked to be erased from history. Other named Archons include Ndenge and Xumucul (implied by their naming alongside Pyro Archons), Cochanina of the Meztli tribe (who drove the Volcano Lord out of the land of the People of the Springs and worked to contain the Bakunawa), Gloharry, Shulevitz and Isaja. An unnamed Pyro Archon who knew Venti is linked to the Muratans in the manga prologue. The Pyro Archon originally fated by the Heavenly Principles was Och-Kan, a half-dragon, not a human; the Belyi Tsar reads Xbalanque's usurpation as one of the long chain of rebellions against Celestia.

Mavuika, a Scion of the Canopy (Huitztlan), was Pyro Archon during the Cataclysm about 500 years ago. She placed her life within the Sacred Flame so she could die early and wake again in the present, and she holds a unique right to wield the power of the Ruler of Death, Ronova, once, at the cost of her fated death. Her Ancient Name is Kiongozi. The wiki suggests, by the same logic as Haborym, that all Pyro Archons may bear it; canon does not say so outright.

Gnosis and authority: A Gnosis is a device that resonates directly with Celestia and is more advanced than a Vision. Seven were made, one per element. The Pyro Gnosis was the one Capitano of the Fatui first pursued, but his duel with Mavuika ended inconclusively and he changed course, so the Fatui never retrieved it. Mavuika had long refused to use it, because rewriting the ley lines with it would erase Natlan's history.

Archons keep their elemental power and divine thrones without a Gnosis. Mavuika still had the Pyro Gnosis during the fighting against Gosoythoth: she used it to relight the Sacred Flame after Gosoythoth's manifestation put it out, and to displace the Abyssal beast from above the Stadium.

Gnosis status: In Song of the Welkin Moon Act X, "Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana" (6.6), the Traveler obtained the Pyro Gnosis from Mavuika so Nahida could burn down the corrupted Irminsul. The flames burned for seven days and nights, and afterwards the Gnosis vanished. Mavuika felt it go before Nahida confirmed it. Neither found remains. Later the Traveler says its destruction was confirmed and that Mavuika told them it had returned to the ley lines. Archons' thrones do not depend on the Gnosis, so Mavuika remains Pyro Archon as of 7.1.

Elemental beings: Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, and Pyro lifeforms such as Pyro slimes, specters, Abyss Mages, the Pyro Hypostasis and the Pyro Regisvine.

Pyro Slimes are described as small monsters formed by Pyro settling throughout nature. Pyro Specters are born from highly concentrated Pyro and float in the air; an Akademiya student reportedly argued they were a kind of Crystalfly, and has not graduated. Pyro Abyss Mages command Pyro and can communicate with hilichurls, so they manipulate them easily.

- Pyro Hypostasis (code name Ayin): a high-purity Pyro entity found in Inazuma that can revive itself in an emergency restart phase.
- Pyro Regisvine: a giant vine that has absorbed the ancient flame raging in the ley lines, found in Liyue and described as restless and furious.
- Xiuhcoatl: the Flamelord, Pyro Dragon of the old world and creator of the Pyro dragons of Natlan. The Heavenly Principles froze him in lava; Abyssal corruption later wore down his clarity; Xbalanque killed him about 2,000 years ago. Some in Natlan believe he still sleeps in the volcano.
- Some Saurians are born with the Flamelord's Blessing, a mark tied to Xiuhcoatl that grants more power than modern Saurians can bear.
- Gosoythoth, the Abyssal beast that took Xiuhcoatl's form, has its own entry.

- Escoffier says the condensate from Pyro Slimes tastes spicy, like Jueyun Chili, with a small amount of an extremely sweet substance.
- Ranjit says Pyro Regisvine fruit is "pretty good" and tastes of Pyro.

Known uses: Igniting and burning things, explosions, heating, cooking and forging, and fire-based attacks. Pyro also melts ice and boils water in many fights.

In Natlan, Pyro is also a way to carry names and promises: objects carried in battle become imbued with Contending Fire and can be burned as fuel, as Mavuika does with her keepsakes, and Pyro Archons move the dead through the Sacred Flame during the Ode of Resurrection, stepping into the flame and returning with the fallen warrior.

- Outside Natlan, Pyro Visions are held by a wide range of people, among them Klee, Diluc, Amber, Bennett, Xiangling, Xinyan, Hu Tao, Yanfei, Thoma, Yoimiya, Dehya, Gaming, Chevreuse, Lyney and Arlecchino.
- Durin (6.2) is a playable Pyro Sword user and Nicole (6.6) a playable Pyro Catalyst user. Neither 7.0 nor 7.1 added a Pyro character.

Limits: Pyro does not react with Pyro. It does little on its own against water or ice.

Pyro needs a Vision or an Archon's authority; ordinary fire is just fire. Keep scale proportionate to the source.

Gameplay: a Pyro aura on its own has no inherent effect; it only enables reactions. The reactions are covered in their own entries.

Interactions: Vaporize with Hydro, Melt with Cryo, Overloaded with Electro, Burning with Dendro, Swirl with Anemo and Crystallize with Geo.

Vaporize amplifies damage when Pyro or Hydro triggers it; Melt does so with Cryo. Overloaded is an explosion with strong knockback. Burning keeps Pyro damage ticking in a small area around a target while a Dendro aura exists. Swirl spreads Pyro to nearby enemies. Crystallize makes a Pyro shard that grants a Pyro shield. Burgeon is Pyro detonating a Dendro Core created by Bloom.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Pyro is a damage type and the element of Pyro Vision holders. The Elemental Resonance Fervent Flames (two or more Pyro characters in a party) shortens Cryo's effect by 40% and raises ATK by 25%.

Pyro is the only element the Traveler cannot resonate with immediately upon touching its Statue; in Natlan, switching to Pyro talents requires finishing a step of the quest "When All Becomes a Monument". Pyroculi are found only in Natlan, where 249 are in the open world and 22 in the Ancient Sacred Mountain; they are limited and do not respawn. Pyro Sigils are Natlan's currency, offered at the Tablet of Tona. Agnidus Agate is the ascension gem. Objects in the world that count as Pyro include campfires, torches, Pyro exploding barrels and flaming flowers. Pyro Slimes can be put out by one gauge of Hydro, two of Cryo or Electro, or four of Anemo or Geo, but they re-ignite whenever hit by Pyro damage.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Pyro as heat, light and sound: air shimmering, embers drifting, sudden warmth, crackle. Warm orange and red are safe visual cues. In Natlan, fire reads as honour, contest and shared meals rather than just destruction.

A Pyro Vision holder can scorch, ignite or boil water, but reshaping a landscape is an Archon-level act. Keep Mavuika's fire friendly by default. Remember that a Pyro Archon is mortal and human-born, and can be ordinary company, not a remote deity.

Avoid portraying Pyro as uncontrollably violent; canon shows deliberate control. Do not give the Pyro Gnosis back to Mavuika or place it in the Fatui's hands as of 7.1.

214.content:
The Pyro Archon is the God of War among The Seven and the ruler of Natlan. The divine name Haborym is linked to the position. Every Pyro Archon starts as a human who wins the position by battle and remains mortal. Mavuika, who is both the current Pyro Archon and the one who held the throne at the Cataclysm, is covered by her own entry.

Earlier Archons include Xbalanque (the first), a scarlet-eyed youth, Cochanina, Gloharry, Shulevitz and Isaja. The Pyro Archon looks after the Sacred Flame, which is a conduit to the Night Kingdom and the Wayob.

215.content: The Pyro Gnosis was never collected by the Fatui. Mavuika, who had always refused to use it, passed it through the Traveler so Nahida could burn the corrupted Irminsul in 6.6. It then disappeared. Mavuika sensed it go; its exact fate is not stated.

216.content: Xiuhcoatl, also called the Flamelord, was the Pyro Dragon of the Seven Sovereigns and ruled Natlan before the Archons. The Heavenly Principles stole part of his Authority and froze him in lava. Abyssal corruption later wore down his clarity. About 2,000 years ago Xbalanque fought him at the Great Volcano of Tollan; both fell and died, and Xbalanque revived in flames. Some say Xiuhcoatl still sleeps in the volcano, while others say only a husk is left.

217.content:
The Sacred Flame is a fire that burns continually in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It is a conduit to the Night Kingdom and the Wayob, and a base of Natlan's resistance to the Abyss. It is fuelled by Contending Fire from combat between Natlanese warriors. Smaller flames split from it are used in rituals such as the Scions of the Canopy's Turnfire Night.

During the Ode of Resurrection the Pyro Archon steps into the flame, fetches a fallen warrior from the Night Kingdom and walks out with them. As Natlan's condition worsened, Mavuika gave her own power to keep it alight.

218.content: Pyro Slimes are small monsters made when Pyro settles throughout nature. Pyro Specters are born from concentrated Pyro and float. Pyro Abyss Mages command Pyro and can influence hilichurls. The Pyro Hypostasis is a high-purity Pyro entity, in Inazuma, that can revive in an emergency restart; the Pyro Regisvine is a giant vine fed by ley-line flame, found in Liyue.

219.content:
Quicken (also: Quicken reaction, Quickened, Quicken Aura, Catalyze, Catalyze reactions, Dendro-Electro reaction): Quicken is the elemental reaction between Dendro and Electro, in either order. It deals no damage itself. It leaves the target Quickened, with a Quicken Aura that decays over time. While the aura lasts, further Dendro or Electro hits on the target trigger the Spread or Aggravate reactions, which add bonus damage to those hits. It is a combat rule, so treat it as a gameplay abstraction, not a named law of the world.

Quicken appeared with Version 3.0 and the Dendro element, along with Sumeru. The wiki treats Quicken, Aggravate and Spread as one group called Catalyze. Spread and Aggravate have their own entries (system.spread, system.aggravate).

In universe: Canon gives no story explanation for Quicken. The in-game tutorial only says that when creatures are affected by Electro and Dendro, Quicken occurs and renders them Quickened, and that Quickened creatures hit by Electro or Dendro suffer additional damage through Aggravate or Spread.

Nothing read ties the reaction to a character, god or event. Do not invent an origin or a mechanism.

The wiki's trivia notes that the reaction between Electro and Dendro is said to have a deep connection to Sumeru's history, referring to Sumeru's preview teaser about the Dendro element. It speculates that this may relate to the goddess Nabu Malikata and the Dendro Archon Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, because environmental clues in Sumeru suggest Nabu Malikata may have been Electro-aligned. That is the wiki's inference: no character or text states that Nabu Malikata held Electro or links her to Quicken. Treat it as unconfirmed.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Quicken happens when Dendro hits a target carrying Electro, or Electro hits a target carrying Dendro. It applies a Quicken Aura to the target, and the reaction itself deals no damage.

- A target with a Quicken Aura that is hit by Dendro triggers Spread, and by Electro triggers Aggravate. Each gives the hit a flat damage bonus added to its base damage. Spread's bonus is slightly larger than Aggravate's.
- Spread and Aggravate do not consume the Quicken Aura, so a team can keep triggering them while it lasts.
- Pyro or Hydro applied to a Quicken Aura consumes it, triggering Burning or Bloom respectively.
- Quicken Aura can coexist with Electro and Dendro auras on the same target.

- The aura's duration is the smaller of the two elements' gauge units times 5 seconds, plus 6 seconds, per the wiki's formula. Triggering Quicken again replaces the old aura only if the new one is stronger.
- The bonus is the character's level multiplier times 1.25 for Spread and 1.15 for Aggravate. Elemental Mastery and certain artifacts and talents raise it. It is then affected by DMG bonuses, CRIT, DEF and RES like the rest of the hit.
- The wiki calls this class Additive reactions (an unofficial name); the game calls them Catalyze Reactions in Miliastra Wonderland. Additive bonuses differ from Melt and Vaporize, which multiply the hit.
- The Elemental Resonance Sprawling Greenery (two or more Dendro characters) gives Elemental Mastery after Quicken, Aggravate and Spread (see the Dendro entry).

- Quicken is unchanged by the newer reaction families. The Lunar reactions replace other Hydro reactions, and Stellar Glimmer reactions replace Cryo ones; as of Version 7.1 the wiki's table still lists Dendro with Electro as Quicken.
- Enemies and the environment use separate level-scaled bonus tables than characters; the wiki lists higher bonus values for them at level 100, but those numbers are not reproduced here.

Limits: Quicken deals nothing by itself and needs both Dendro and Electro to be applied. It does not apply to plants that are not Dendro; "Wood" objects such as vines cannot trigger it.

Quicken only helps Dendro and Electro attacks. Pyro or Hydro attacks on the aura end it. Because attacks have an internal cooldown on applying their element, a source cannot apply Dendro or Electro on every hit.

Examples: Gameplay example: an Electro attack lands on a target already covered in Dendro, and the target is Quickened. A Dendro character then strikes it for Spread, and an Electro character for Aggravate, both for extra damage.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show Quicken as purple and green energy crawling over the target, like vines humming with charge, which makes later strikes bite harder. It reads as a setup: an unresolved charge waiting for another strike.

Narratively, Quicken fits Sumeru and Dendro scenes: lush growth, damp air, crackling sparks. It rewards teamwork between a Dendro and an Electro Vision user. Keep the effect short and local to a target.

Avoid claiming that Quicken is a divine technique of the Dendro Archon or of Nabu Malikata. Do not confuse Quicken with Bloom, which Hydro and Dendro create, or with Hyperbloom, which follows Bloom.

220.content: Catalyze is the wiki's name for the Dendro-Electro group of reactions: Quicken, which applies the aura, and Spread and Aggravate, which are the bonus-damage reactions triggered by hits on a Quickened target. The tutorial in the game is titled Elemental Reaction: Catalyze. Its English wiki page covers all three.

221.content: Spread is triggered by a Dendro hit on a Quickened target, and Aggravate by an Electro hit. Both add a flat bonus to the triggering hit's base damage and do not consume the Quicken Aura. Spread's bonus is slightly higher. Each has its own entry (system.spread, system.aggravate).

222.content:
Physical laws and roleplay physics (also: roleplay physics, Teyvat physics, physical laws of Teyvat): This entry tells a narrator how physical reality works in Teyvat roleplay. The default is ordinary human biology and consequences: people eat, sleep, tire, are hurt and recover slowly, and death is permanent unless a specific canon mechanism applies. Visions, Archons, adepti and ancient powers are exceptions with limits. Game mechanics (health bars, respawning at a Statue of The Seven, instant fast travel) are abstractions, not literal in-world rules. Each section below separates what canon shows from this project's recommended reading.

Rule of thumb: when canon shows a rule, follow it; when canon is silent, assume the real-world answer for a pre-industrial setting with magic added only where a source supports it; never let a character do something because "it is a game".

Labels used below: "Canon" is something a source shows; "Gameplay" is a mechanic that is not literal lore; "Recommended" is this project's roleplay interpretation, not canon text. Where a thing is open in canon, it is left open.

Ordinary biology: Canon: ordinary people in Teyvat are shown living as humans do: they work, eat, rest and fall ill. Recommended: treat ordinary NPCs and Vision holders alike as physically human, with normal needs for food, water, sleep and shelter. A Vision grants control over one element, not toughness, immunity or freedom from need.

Canon shows food and drink at the centre of daily life across the nations, and food is used to restore strength in the game. Recommended: hunger, thirst, fatigue and cold should matter on long journeys, and the narrator should avoid hand-waving them unless the scene is brief. Do not add specifics (calorie needs, sleep hours) as canon.

The wiki's treatment of food as the main healing consumable is a gameplay abstraction; in a story a good meal comforts and restores energy but does not mend a serious wound. Recommended: eating and resting should help recovery in proportion, and exhaustion should lower a character's competence before it incapacitates them.

Ageing and lifespans: Canon: no source gives a human lifespan. Ordinary people age. Long-lived beings exist but are not ordinary: the adepti are extremely long-lived or immortal by enlightenment; pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns were cursed with immortality; Pyro Archons, unlike other Archons, are mortals who age and die like humans.

Adepti may choose the appearance of their human form: Madame Ping's old-woman look is described as her own choice, not ageing. Half-blooded humans such as Ganyu can qualify as adepti, but canon leaves their lifespans unstated. Recommended: do not state ages or lifespans for characters whose entries leave them null.

Ages and "how old" a character looks are separate. Recommended: for characters with Visions or divine blood, do not assume agelessness unless their own entry says so. Do not infer an Archon's age from appearance; Archon ages are tied to stories, such as Barbatos becoming Archon about 2,600 years ago after the fall of Decarabian.

Travel and communication: Canon: travel is physical in the world's setting. Wind gliders were invented, per legend, 2,600 years ago by a retired adventurer named Leonard after he failed to climb Pilos Peak, and let a user glide; the Teleport Waypoints and instant fast travel of the game are an abstraction (see teleportation). Recommended: journeys take days, and the narrator should name terrain, weather and stops.

Canon: letters, notices and word of mouth carry news; Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild passes on commissions. Recommended: news takes time; a character should only know what they have learned by a plausible route, matching the knowledge rules in the canon-rules entry. Gliding costs stamina in gameplay, so it has limits. Recommended: a glider reduces fall danger but does not make someone fly.

Medicine and healing: Canon: medicine in Teyvat mixes herbal remedies with more advanced care, including surgery, bandages, setting dislocations, injected medicines and some recognition of mental illness and therapy. Elemental power can heal: Barbara is a known Hydro healer and Jean has healed with Anemo. Manipulating the elemental energy in a body has been used experimentally to control Eleazar's symptoms and is not widespread.

Recommended: healing by an elemental user speeds recovery of ordinary wounds but is not a reset; a lethal wound still needs time and care, and healing powers should be scarce, tiring and tied to a named character. Herbs and nursing are the common route.

Canon shows healing powers coexisting with long illnesses that no one cures quickly, such as Eleazar and Anna's ongoing treatments. Gameplay: healing numbers, food heals and team heals are abstractions and should not be quoted in a scene. Medicine varies by region (for example Liyue's herbal blends and Sumeru's Nilotpala Lotus for Eleazar patients). Recommended: do not apply one region's remedy as universal, and keep dosage and procedure vague rather than inventing exact medical detail.

Injury and recovery: Canon shows wounds, scars, poisoning and illness, and that recovery takes time. Recommended: injuries stay with a character until they plausibly heal; an injured character fights worse, moves slower or rests; a serious wound is not erased between scenes.

Gameplay: characters have HP and are healed by dishes, Statues of The Seven and talents; that is not how bodies work in a story. Recommended: describe injuries in prose (a bleeding gash, a limp), and let rest, treatment and time resolve them.

Canon includes injuries that are not purely physical: abyssal corruption, Durin's poisonous blood that Dvalin swallowed, and long-term erosion. Recommended: treat corruption and poison as ongoing conditions with their own cures or consequences, not as quick damage.

Death: Canon: death is real and usually permanent. Gods and Archons can die: Decarabian fell, Rukkhadevata and the Belyi Tsar died in past struggles against the Abyss, and Ronova died during the story. Recommended: a character who dies in a roleplay stays dead unless a canon mechanism below applies and the story earns it.

Gameplay (not literal lore): a "fallen" character is revived at a Statue of The Seven, by a dish or by a constellation; if the whole party falls, it is restored at the nearest waypoint at low health. This is a rule of the game, not of the world. Recommended: do not treat death as a setback that resets; the narrator may fade to a rescue or a near-death, but should say so.

Canon marks the importance of dying: the Rite of Parting is a funeral custom for the passing of an adeptus (the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, which has handled it only a handful of times in three thousand years). Recommended: show grief, rites and consequences in scenes with a death.

Ronova, the Ruler of Death, governed the laws of death and could define its form for anyone or deny it, as she did with the curse of immortality on the Khaenri'ahns. After she exceeded the limits of her authority in Snezhnaya, Celestia recalled it and she was defeated and died. Archons' divine thrones can be passed on after death; destroying a throne requires the death of its Archon.

Resurrection: Canon shows only a few bounded forms: the Natlan Ode of Resurrection, adepti raising Qiqi as a zombie, and the cursed immortality of the Khaenri'ahns. None is a general fix for death.

Qiqi was mortally wounded, then resurrected by the adepti as a zombie, which required sealing her in amber because the adeptal energy overwhelmed her. She has trouble keeping memories, has no sense of smell and no strong emotions, prefers cold, and her flesh decays in heat. Recommended: resurrection costs something lasting.

The Ode of Resurrection, in Natlan, raises warriors with Ancient Names who died fighting the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars, only if the group achieved victory. The healing applies to fatal injuries only, not to earlier wounds or illness. The Pyro Archon enters the Sacred Flame to seek the dead and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom. When Kachina's Ode failed, Mavuika said Abyssal unrest in the Night Kingdom prevented her from finding Kachina; the Pilgrimage was suspended. Later, Mavuika drew on the Lord of the Night's power to extend the Ode's blessing to all Natlan's warriors, and after the Night Wars the ceremony was discontinued.

Recommended: in a scene, a resurrected person should show the mechanism's conditions and cost. Do not offer the Ode as a service outside its context, and do not extend it to Sumeru, Liyue or Fontaine characters. Canon leaves unanswered how much of a person returns, and whether those who are resurrected differ in any way.

Weather and environment: Canon: the world has real climate hazards. Dragonspine has a subzero climate where grass does not burn and the cold drains health over time unless one keeps warm; the wiki notes that Goulash and sources of warmth mitigate it. Snezhnaya has cold zones with a similar mechanic. Recommended: travel in extreme cold needs shelter, fire and food.

Dragonspine's climate changed when the Skyfrost Nail fell and destroyed a silver ley line tree, turning a verdant mountain into a frozen one, per the wiki's account of the Sal Vindagnyr ruins. Gameplay: the Sheer Cold gauge is a mechanic. Recommended: describe numbness, slowed movement and frostbite-like effects without numbers. Qiqi is cold-adapted by her undead nature and decays in heat; she is an exception, not a model for ordinary people. Ley Line Disorder (storms, icicles, lightning) is a Spiral Abyss and domain mechanic, so treat it as local ley line instability, not weather that follows a character. Recommended: weather should respect geography; avoid inventing blizzards in Liyue harbours or sandstorms in Mondstadt. Where an element shapes a nation, keep its effects to the feel of the land (see the element entries) rather than controlling the weather.

Elemental damage: Canon: elemental power is real and dangerous. A Vision holder channels one element and can burn, freeze, shock or knock things around, but is still mortal. Recommended: describe elements through their physical effects (heat, cold, current, pressure, root and growth) rather than numbers.

Elements interact in canon-adjacent ways the game calls reactions, such as fire boiling water to steam or wind spreading a flame. The element entries and the elemental-reactions entry describe them; this entry only adds that damage to people should leave burns, chills or injuries, not a bar going down. Adeptal energy is harmful to ordinary humans; prolonged contact with adepti can overwhelm a human soul. Recommended: ordinary people near adepti or divine power should feel strain over time, not be harmed at once. Archon-level power is of a different order. Barbatos considers himself the weakest Archon because he does not exert control over his nation. Recommended: do not have Archons casually level cities, and keep the consequences of their power visible.

Water and pressure: Canon: in Fontaine, the power of the Transoceanic Sourcewater lets Vision holders (and others such as the Traveler and Paimon) breathe and speak underwater. People without Visions rely on diving gear and specialised training. Archenoul says adapting to water pressure is a concern for non-Vision holders, which implies it is not for Vision holders. Outside that context there is no breathing-underwater rule.

Recommended: elsewhere in Teyvat, drowning is real: swimming tires a person and cold water sucks heat. Gameplay: stamina and drowning mechanics are abstractions. In a scene, someone who goes into deep water without help should struggle quickly.

Fontaine's water is also lore-bearing: its humans were made from Oceanids using water from the Primordial Sea, and contact with pure Primordial Seawater of high concentration dissolves Fontainians into water, though non-Fontainians simply become more sensitive to Hydro. The wiki states that after Neuvillette's act this is no longer a threat. Remus's attempt to dilute Ichor to grant eternal life destroyed his nation, and diluted Primordial Seawater became the euphoric drug Sinthe. Recommended: after 4.x, treat Fontaine's water as ordinary water for Fontainians in everyday scenes; refer to the dissolution only when recounting the history or the prophecy. Do not apply Fontainian dissolution to non-Fontainians.

Explosions and structures: Canon shows deliberate and accidental destruction at human scale (bombs, collapses) and at divine scale (the Cataclysm, the Skyfrost Nail). Recommended: scale damage to the source. A bomb damages a wall, a room, or people near it; it does not level a city.

Recommended: buildings in Teyvat are stone, timber and plaster by region and can burn, collapse or flood; fire spreads through wood and dry grass, though not in Dragonspine's subzero climate. Ruin Guards and ancient machines are durable and need real force. Canon also shows lasting environmental damage from large events: the Skyfrost Nail's effect on Dragonspine, the Cataclysm's effects on Khaenri'ah and the Abyss's corruption of land. Recommended: major damage has aftermath, such as refugees, rebuilding or hazard zones.

Magic and limits: Canon: a Vision binds its holder to one element. Archons draw power from divine thrones, and Barbatos says Archons draw power from their control over their nations. Power has costs and limits; canon shows exhaustion, injury and consequences when it is overused.

Recommended: no one is all-powerful. A Vision holder tires and misses; an adeptus is strong but bound by agreements and responsibilities; a god is limited by authority, memory and other gods. Keep any power to what a character's own entry supports. Canon includes special techniques with specific rules: the adepti's "gifting of dreams and visions", Dream Trawler (which separates soul from body), and Mortal Lingering (a temporary vessel). Recommended: do not generalise these into powers for other characters. Anything on the order of the Heavenly Principles, Celestia or the Abyss is not a tool for an ordinary scene. Recommended: if a user asks for a god-level effect, show its price or have it blocked by a canon limit rather than granting it.

Teleportation: Canon is unclear. The game's Teleport Waypoints work as fast travel, but the wiki notes sources disagree on whether people in the world understand them: some items and the map treat them as teleportation devices, while some characters treat them as ancient devices of unknown purpose. Katheryne's own statements are ambiguous.

What does exist: the Fatui and Mona use teleportation in quests, and Leifhelm says his Grand Master crossed from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt quickly along the Ley Lines. The Ley Lines are a network of elemental energy and memories, and Portable Waypoints depend on their power. The Abyss has portals that Dainsleif describes as gateways to a network. Recommended: do not let characters teleport at will. Treat teleportation as rare, costly or tied to a device, a character's established power or an Abyssal portal. Fast travel in the game should be narrated as a journey, a lift on a trusted route, or a cut forward in time. Ley Lines are key: Irminsul and the Ley Lines record the memories of Teyvat, and Descenders have no records in Irminsul. Recommended: do not use the Ley Lines as a free transport system for the user's character.

Dimensional boundaries: Canon contains separate realms: the Night Kingdom of Natlan (created by Yohualtecuhtin at Ronova's instruction to repair Natlan's Ley Lines), the adepti's own domains, Enkanomiya and the Abyss. Some are hard or dangerous to enter: mortals who enter adeptal land uninvited are considered brave or desperate.

Recommended: crossing into a realm needs a way in (a ritual, a key, a portal, an invitation) and carries a risk. Realms keep their own rules; do not import a character's powers from one into another. Canon shows that people and memory can be altered by changes to Irminsul without those affected noticing, and that people from outside Teyvat, including Descenders, have no record there. Recommended: treat changes to memory and records as story events with a source, not a convenience.

How {{char}} behaves: Recommended practice (not canon): default to consequence. Hunger, injury, cold, fatigue and death matter; powers have limits; travel takes time. When the user asks for something game-like (reviving, instant travel, healing in a fight), narrate it as a plausible in-world event or decline gently and offer an in-world alternative. Never contradict an established canon fact to make a scene easier.

Match tone to the scene: a warm tavern stay can skim travel and meals, while a survival scene should linger on cold, water and wounds. The aim is internal consistency, not realism for its own sake. When canon is silent, say so briefly or choose the most conservative reading; mark invented details as scene colour, never as lore. Respect the knowledge rules in the canon-rules entry: a character can only describe hazards they have met.

Limits: This entry does not give a statistical system and does not replace character or location entries. Where an individual entry states a power, a condition or a lifespan, that entry takes priority over the general guidance here.

223.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Ode of Resurrection
223.content:
The Ode of Resurrection is a Natlan ceremony at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame that raises Ancient Name bearers who died fighting the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars, provided their group achieved victory. It heals only fatal injuries. The Pyro Archon enters the Sacred Flame to seek the deceased and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom. It failed for Kachina; later Mavuika extended it to all of Natlan's warriors with the Lord of the Night's power, and it ended after the Night Wars.

The singing of those present is part of the rite. Treat it as a bounded Natlan rite, not a general resurrection power.

224.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Dragonspine cold
224.content: Dragonspine, formerly Vindagnyr, has an extreme cold climate that built up after the Skyfrost Nail destroyed the ley line tree on the mountain. Grass does not burn there, and the cold weakens travellers over time unless they keep warm. Snezhnaya has comparable cold zones. Recommended: describe it as dangerous exposure requiring shelter, fire and food.

225.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Transoceanic Sourcewater
225.content: In Fontaine, the Transoceanic Sourcewater lets Vision holders, the Traveler and Paimon breathe and speak underwater. People without Visions use diving gear and specialised training, and water pressure is a concern for them. Do not carry this over to other nations.

226.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Curse of immortality
226.content: During the Cataclysm, Ronova placed a curse of immortality on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns, which the wiki describes as a punishment. Dainsleif is also immortal; his brother Vedrfolnir gave him a ring that continuously resets his body's condition, but his mind is still affected by erosion. Immortality in canon is a burden, not a reward.

227.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Teleportation limits
227.content: Canon is unclear about how Teleport Waypoints work. Leifhelm says his Grand Master crossed from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt along the Ley Lines quickly, and the Fatui and Mona use teleportation in quests. Recommended: treat teleportation as rare and tied to a device or power.

228.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Zombie condition
228.content: Qiqi was resurrected as a zombie by the adepti after being mortally wounded, and sealed in amber because the energy was too much for her. She has trouble retaining memories, lacks a sense of smell, shows little emotion, prefers cold and decays in heat. Use this as the template for how canon treats the cost of resurrection.

229.comment: Physical laws and roleplay physics: Archon restraint against Signora
229.content: During the 6.4 limited-time event "Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind", Venti said he had deliberately held back when Signora ambushed him for the Gnosis, because fighting her at greater strength would likely have destroyed the city. Recommended: use this as the canon model for Archons limiting their power near people, not as proof of exact strength.

230.content:
Saurian Indwelling (also: indwelling a Saurian, indwelt Saurian, Spiritsconce, Spiritsconces): Saurian Indwelling is an ability of the Traveler in Natlan: their spirit slips into a Saurian (one of Natlan's dragon-kin) and acts through its body, so they can run, climb, glide or swim as that creature does. The in-game tutorial credits "a mysterious power" with the gift. It is not presented as a Vision or an Archon's power, and almost nobody else in Natlan seems to know it exists.

It works on Saurians of the six tribal species and on small totem-like markers called Spiritsconces, and it ends when the Traveler chooses to leave or the body is lost. Each species brings its own movement and elemental strike, so indwelling is how the Traveler crosses ground that a human on foot could not.

In universe: Natlan's Saurians are descendants of Pyro vishaps that lost their ancient intelligence; they follow emotion and trust their human companions. Tribe members learn to read a Saurian's moods through long companionship. Indwelling is different: the Traveler's spirit enters the animal, and while inside, the speech of Saurians becomes understandable to them. Nobody is shown teaching the Traveler this; it simply works.

The Traveler first indwells a Saurian in the World Quest "Lost in the Woods" (5.0). Brought into a strange golden space on arrival in Natlan, they and Paimon find a weakened adult Tepetlisaurus and a whelp, later named Little One, caught in trouble. The Traveler's body vanishes and the adult rises with new energy; Paimon realises the Traveler is "inside" it. The Traveler uses it to free the whelp. Later, people who notice the effect do not understand it: Chasca sensed that an indwelt Qucusaur had the Traveler's demeanour but chose not to ask, and Coyllur found the Traveler oddly familiar after first meeting them as a Qucusaur.

Reactions show how little is known. The Saurian Antu recognised the Traveler inside a Qucusaur but believed it was a Qucusaur that could turn into a human. In the Night Kingdom, the spirit Chuychu gathered Saurian spirits for the Traveler to indwell, knowledge she did not have in life. The Traveler also indwells Saurians to carry out errands: an adult Qucusaur to return to Atoco with Paimon and Iansan while looking for a cure for Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome, adult Tepetlisaurs while searching for Antu, and an adult Iktomisaur while helping Mualani with Wavey Bay's attractions.

Related Saurian background that frames the ability: Saurians have their own language that only other Saurians (and surviving pre-devolution dragons such as Ajaw) understand, and most cannot speak human words. Some are born with the Flamelord's Blessing, a mark of much stronger ancestral power that tribes fear because its bearers may sicken or lose their minds; Kukulkan is later revealed to have shaped how it appears, to pass power and wisdom on to future dragons. Tribes traditionally refuse bearers of the mark, and the volcano ritual to be accepted again was rarely successful.

The chosen of dragons: Kukulkan, while hiding his identity, called the Tepetlisaurus whelp Little One the "Chosen of Dragons" and said hope lay with him. The same title names the World Quest series "In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons", in which the Traveler helps Little One with its dangerous red mark, the Flamelord's Blessing, and finally takes it to the Great Volcano of Tollan to lift the curse. The wiki links the title to the Traveler's indwelling ability; canon does not state that link outright (see uncertainties).

Spiritsconces: Spiritsconces are small, colourful totems found across Natlan. Saurians are described as able to enter a "Spiritsconce" state under particular circumstances; indwelling one lets the Traveler take on the Saurian's original form. When the Traveler leaves a Saurian without killing it, a Spiritsconce is left where they stood, and defeated adult Saurians leave one too.

Gameplay detail: leftover Spiritsconces from ended indwellings are limited (four, or three while indwelling, with the oldest vanishing first), natural ones return after 15 seconds, and an indwelt enemy Saurian respawns at its place after a minute. A 4-second cooldown separates one indwelling from the next. These are mechanics, not lore.

Species and abilities: Each tribe's Saurian offers its own way of moving, tied to an element and to its tribe's land.
- Tepetlisaurus (Geo): burrows and climbs rock at speed; home of the Children of Echoes.
- Yumkasaurus (Dendro): grapples and glides, grabs and spits out objects; Scions of the Canopy.
- Koholasaurus (Hydro): swims and dashes through water and Liquid Phlogiston; People of the Springs.
- Qucusaurus (Pyro): flies and dives; Flower-Feather Clan.
- Iktomisaurus (Cryo): glides, high jumps, and can scan and place Nightspirit Graffiti objects; Masters of the Night-Wind.
- Tatankasaurus (Electro): charges, smashes Pulverite and pushes heavy objects; Collective of Plenty.

Further detail: a burrowing Tepetlisaur cannot be left manually and spends Phlogiston as it moves. Yumkasaurs also take half the usual fall damage. Qucusaurs can change altitude in flight, while Iktomisaurs only glide downward. A Tatankasaur that charges hard into an obstacle, or taps its skill, enters a "Spirited" state, letting it leap off terrain and briefly cross water or Liquid Phlogiston. Little One, as a Tepetlisaurus, has a quest-only version of the Tepetlisaurus kit.

Asha: At the Easybreeze Holiday Resort (Tenochtzitoc) the same mechanic works on Asha, friendly paint-spraying mascot creatures described as a kind of Monetoo. Asha can walk up walls and on water, grapple and throw paintballs without using Phlogiston, and indwelling one ends if the Traveler leaves the resort.

Limits: Some creatures refuse. A few quest-linked Saurians, such as "Half-Baked" in "Special Friends", reject the attempt with a message that a strong will refuses the indwelling. Indwelt Saurians are poor fighters and cannot dash to dodge attacks.

A Saurian is forced out if it tries to enter the main settlement of a tribe that is not its own: the screen warns that outside Saurians may not enter, and the Traveler is ejected. Only the matching species is allowed in each tribe's home (Tepetlisaurus for the Children of Echoes, and so on, as listed above). Per the wiki, runes bar outsiders, and who made them is unexplained. Leaving Natlan's boundaries, teleporting or entering instance rooms also ends the indwelling. While indwelling, the Traveler cannot cook, use a Statue of The Seven, or use a Tablet of Tona.

Deep water drowns most Saurians; only Koholasaurs swim freely, and Tatankasaurs can cross water briefly in a charge. Indwelling an enemy Saurian is unrewarding: killing it grants no EXP, materials or Mora. Other Saurians may be curious when an indwelt one approaches but will not aggravate unless attacked.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): indwelling is an exploration mechanic introduced with Natlan in 5.0. An indwelt Saurian uses its own Phlogiston meter before the player's. Phlogiston is refilled near Everflame Seeds, Teleport Waypoints and Statues of The Seven, by touching Flaming Seeds of Phlogiston, and by collecting or smashing certain items. All indwelt Saurians share the same stats. While indwelling, NPCs other than Saurians usually say only "..." except for quest-specific dialogue. Indwelling counts as leaving combat only if the indwelt enemy was the sole aggravated one.

Exiting is done by holding the exit button, like leaving the Waverider.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat indwelling as a quiet, uncanny act. The Traveler's body goes still or seems to vanish and the Saurian moves with unusual purpose and awareness. Natlanese who see it should be puzzled rather than certain; they might sense something familiar about the animal without naming it.

Tribe members read Saurians by body language, so a Saurian that behaves oddly and shows a human's habits invites curiosity, not alarm. Do not give any other character the ability, do not make the Saurian speak human language, and do not claim the power's origin is known. Remember the Traveler cannot bring an indwelt Saurian into a rival tribe's village.

231.content: A Spiritsconce is a small, colourful totem-like marker left behind in Natlan. Saurians can enter a "Spiritsconce" state in particular circumstances, and the Traveler can indwell one to take on the Saurian's original form. Leaving a Saurian alive, or defeating an adult one, leaves a Spiritsconce behind.

232.content: Each Saurian group has its own main territory, which neighbouring Saurians respect; entry is by a local Saurian's invitation and escort. The same borders broadly mark the lands of the Natlanese tribes. In play, an indwelt Saurian tries to enter a rival tribe's village and the Traveler is ejected; the wiki says canon explains this with runes whose origin is unknown. Little One, the Tepetlisaurus whelp, alone slips through those of the Collective of Plenty, perhaps because of the volcano's instability or the Flamelord's Blessing (unconfirmed).

233.content:
Shattered (also: Shatter, Shattered reaction, Shatter reaction): Shatter, listed in the wiki's reaction list as Shattered, is the follow-up to Frozen. When a frozen target is hit by a blunt attack or a Geo attack, the ice breaks apart, the Freeze Aura is removed, and the target takes Physical damage.

It has been part of the game since 1.0 along with Frozen, which has to happen first. Hydro and Cryo together make a target Frozen; a heavy or Geo strike then shatters it.

In universe: Canon gives no in-world explanation for Shatter. The pages read treat it as a combat rule, so it is best understood as the ordinary physical fact that frozen things break when hit hard.

Gameplay: Gameplay: a Frozen target hit by a blunt attack (a claymore swing, a heavy hammer strike) or by Geo takes Shatter damage, and the Freeze Aura ends.

- Shatter deals Physical damage and is a transformative reaction: it has its own base damage set by the reaction type and the level of the character who triggers it, and that damage is raised by Elemental Mastery. It cannot critically strike, is not based on ATK, and is reduced by the target's resistance.
- Shatter happens before any elemental damage in the same hit, which can prevent some other reactions.

- A blunt attack first uses up part of the Freeze Aura according to its Poise damage. Shatter triggers only if some aura remains afterwards.
- An element can persist or be reapplied underneath the Freeze Aura, so another reaction can follow. The wiki's example is Let the Show Begin, then Kaeya's Frostgnaw, then Starfell Sword: the Geo hit Shatters the ice and then Crystallizes the Hydro beneath it.
- A target that is immune to freezing still triggers Frozen but gets no Freeze Aura, so there is nothing to shatter. The wiki lists most bosses and several enemies as immune in this way.

- Shatter is listed among the transformative reactions with Overloaded, Electro-Charged, Superconduct, Swirl, Burning, Bloom, Hyperbloom and Burgeon.
- The wiki's reaction table still shows Frozen and its Shatter follow-up as of 7.1, alongside the Lunar and Stellar Glimmer variants of other reactions.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): show a crack running through a coating of ice, a sharp snap, and a spray of fragments flying outwards. A Geo strike should feel like a stone slamming into the ice; a claymore should feel like a heavy hammer blow.

The blow should be solid and decisive. It ends a short, temporary freeze, so the target is hurt by the impact, not turned to powder. The fragments are loud and sparkle, which suits a dramatic combat beat.

Avoid having a Shatter kill by itself, or break a god or a boss that the game treats as freeze-immune. Do not make it a way to smash frozen water or objects at will; keep the scale of a single fight.

Limits: Shatter needs a Frozen target and a blunt or Geo hit. Weak physical strikes may not be enough.

It removes the Freeze Aura, so it ends the Frozen state. Pyro, Electro or Anemo on a Freeze Aura trigger Melt, Superconduct or Swirl instead.

Examples: Gameplay example, from the in-game tutorial: soak an opponent with Hydro, switch to a Cryo character to freeze them, then strike with a Geo or blunt attack to Shatter.

234.content: Frozen is the Hydro-Cryo reaction that immobilises a target with a Freeze Aura. Shatter is the follow-up that breaks that aura with a blunt or Geo hit. See system.frozen for the full rule set, resistance and immunity.

235.content:
Shield (also: Shields, character shield, Crystallize shield): A shield is a barrier that takes damage in place of a character's HP. Characters gain them by collecting Crystallize shards or through certain talents, Constellations and weapons. Most are elemental and resist their own element especially well. Enemies have separate shields called wards.

Shield Strength is the stat that makes a character's shields hold up better.

In universe: In the world, shields appear as protective barriers: a wall of crystal or stone, a sheath of an element, or a bubble of energy. Characters do not speak of Shield Strength or absorption bonuses.

Crystallize shards come from a Crystallize reaction, and the Geovishap Hatchling is a creature whose Geo shards give a Geo shield on contact.

Gameplay: Gameplay: damage hits the shield's health first, and only the excess reaches the character. A shield that times out is destroyed, which can trigger effects such as Kachina's Constellation. If a character has several shields, one hit affects all of them at once.

Elemental shields absorb their own element at 250 percent, so they take only 40 percent as much damage from it. Geo shields absorb every damage type at 150 percent. Crystallize shields get health from the level and Elemental Mastery of whoever caused the reaction. Talent and Constellation shields usually scale with DEF, ATK, Max HP or Elemental Mastery, and some add further absorption that multiplies with the base bonus.

Shield Strength of the active character scales incoming damage down further, and the same factor applies to excess damage. Some shields cover nearby party members, including in Co-Op Mode. Improvements include the Geo Elemental Resonance Enduring Rock (15 percent more shield strength), plus certain talents, Constellations, food, artifacts and weapons.

Enemy shields behave differently. They appear as an extra durability bar called a ward; a few are elementless and act as extra HP, but most are elemental and are broken most efficiently (or only) with elemental reactions. Some wards decay over time, while others only reduce the damage the enemy takes instead of blocking it all.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay (this project's interpretation, not canon): describe a shield as a visible barrier of crystal, stone or elemental energy that breaks and fades. Avoid percentages in character.

Limits: Gameplay: absorption bonuses and Shield Strength figures are mechanics. They do not appear in character dialogue, and canon never states how much a barrier can take.

236.content:
Souls (also: soul, the soul, afterlife, the dead in Teyvat, ghosts and spirits, soul-stuff): Canon has no single doctrine of the soul. The recurring picture: the soul is what outlasts the body. After death it is meant to return to the Ley Lines, or in Natlan to the Night Kingdom, where it eventually loses its sense of self. A soul or memory that fails to go can linger as a ghost. Older belief sent the noble dead to cities on the moons.
