In universe: A Vision links a person to an element (Pyro, Hydro, Anemo, Electro, Dendro, Cryo or Geo). Venti told the Traveler in the Prologue that Vision holders are allogenes who might ascend one day. A bearer has some elemental sensitivity and can sense their element more keenly than other people.

Bearers are not automatically skilled: ability varies from Shenhe freezing a tsunami to young Yaoyao channelling power through a device. Overuse causes exhaustion that only rest cures.

Skill varies widely. Shenhe, who trained in the adeptus arts, can freeze a tsunami; the young Yaoyao has only been shown to channel her power through a device. Bearers can channel energy through ordinary objects, as Charlotte does with her camera. Everyday uses are plausible and canon shows them: Keqing cooks fish with Electro, Pyro lights fires, Hydro waters plants, Geo raises barriers. Bearers also resist things that harm others: they can stay in the Withering Zones of Sumeru far longer than a person without elemental ability, and they breathe underwater in Fontaine, where non-bearers need a diving suit.
Cutscenes and official media show more than gameplay does. Ningguang teleports and summons the Guizhong Ballistae of the Jade Chamber with Geo energy, Mona can teleport herself and those she touches using Hydro, and Tartaglia uses a Hydro shield and a huge whale in his boss fight. Bearers have a degree of elemental sensitivity, and a Vision glows when it resonates with a nearby source of elemental energy. When Fischl received hers she subconsciously manifested Oz, whose look is based on a character from her favourite novel series.

Nicole is among the very few people who understand how a Vision works, and Albedo senses there is a deeper secret behind them. A "helix-shaped divine ladder" is said to be visible within a Vision, and also to those who ascend; it has not been shown in the game.

Origins: Canon's account, pieced together: the Vision system is a comparatively new rule of Teyvat, set up by the Heavenly Principles at an indeterminate time after the War of the Funerary Flame. Before that war Celestia ruled humanity directly through Angels; afterwards the link to the heavens was severed, the Angels (now Seelies) fell from grace, and the Heavenly Principles were left weakened. To compensate, they worked with an unidentified entity known only as "the one who came after" to build a new order of Archons. Seven Gnoses were made from the remains of the Third Descender, and the Archon War selected seven victors who each received a Gnosis and an elemental Authority taken from the Dragon Sovereigns. Once established, the Seven were bound by duty to give a shard of their mastery as a Vision to anyone whose desire grew strong enough to "step into the threshold of the sacred."

Neuvillette's Vision story implies that the gods collect a gift "more abundant still" when a Vision bearer fulfils their duty; the gift is never specified, and the Seven are not allowed to speak freely about it. Neuvillette also says constellations are merely the Heavenly Principles' way of playing with the living beings of Teyvat. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo held that taking a Vision is to sell oneself to the fate of this world.

Allogenes: Allogene is the in-universe term for a person who is fit to hold a Vision. In the original Chinese, Japanese and Korean the word is the same as the game's title and means roughly "primordial god" or "original god". Allogenes may ascend to Celestia, though most do not.

Venti, in Ending Note, calls Vision holders allogenes who could one day ascend. The Archons are not the givers, so an allogene is not a favourite of their own nation's god, although many believe otherwise. Allogenes who achieve their goals are said to cause the gods to receive an abundant gift (Neuvillette's Vision story).

Some people attribute their Vision to their nation's Archon even when the element does not match, others to the Archon of their element even when they come from another nation, and others to the gods in general. People who never receive a Vision sometimes feel ignored by the Archons despite their deeds. One character wonders how Liyue's old soldiers stayed loyal to Rex Lapis without Visions, and another compares living without one to living like an outsider in one's own world. Both attitudes rest on the mistaken belief that the Seven control distribution.

Receiving: There is no sure way to get a Vision. They arrive during crises and fights, at moments of resolve or revelation, after major accomplishments, or on an otherwise ordinary day. Survival alone is not enough.

The wiki sorts the cases into three groups. Some bearers receive it directly before or on them while conscious, in a crisis, a resolution or after an accomplishment. Some notice it nearby, or find it later among their belongings, after making a resolution. Others receive it while asleep or unconscious, during or after a crisis, unrelated to one, or after reacting in a dream. A person worthy of a Vision either receives a new one or reactivates a nearby Masterless Vision.

Most humans receive theirs between childhood and early adulthood, as children hope for one and adults may decide none will come. Confirmed ages at receipt include Shenhe (6), Diluc (10), Hu Tao (13) and Fischl (14). Kaveh received his after raising funds to rebuild the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Citlali got hers after turning 70, and Ganyu, a half-adeptus, got hers after the Archon War ended 2,000 years ago. Lauma received her Moon Wheel shortly after birth, which she finds troubling.

Non-human beings including Xiao, Yae Miko, Kirara, Xianyun and Sigewinne can receive Visions, though the narrative questions whether theirs are the same as humans'. Artificial humans such as Albedo, the Wanderer and Ineffa can too. The Traveler's Vision story says they cannot receive one since they are an outsider to Teyvat; Yae Miko suggests they simply lack a strong enough ambition, one that transcends the world below and the starry sky above. There are no known cases of a person with more than one permanently active Vision.

Wearing: Most bearers wear their Vision openly, usually at the waist or back, or attached to a belonging such as a diary or pouch. It does not have to be visible to work: Diluc uses his Pyro Vision in his Red Dead of Night disguise. Visions can be customised with tassels, ribbons and charms.
There seems to be a point beyond which a person can no longer connect to their Vision. Tartaglia left his with the Traveler so it would not run out of control again; the item text says it has lost its glow now that its owner left it. Visions taken from their owners under the Vision Hunt Decree and installed in the Statue of the Omnipresent God likewise looked dulled. Visions share a regional shape and differ in finish, size and personal decoration.

Losing: Visions cannot be destroyed, according to Keqing's research, but they can be separated from their owners, willingly or by force. A person parted from their Vision may lose the ambition that drove them, and sometimes memories too; others show no ill effect.

Under the Vision Hunt Decree, Tejima and Kurosawa Kyounosuke lost memories that defined their past actions, while Domon hallucinated the people he had beaten until he spoke with Anzai. Arataki Itto stayed as rowdy after losing his in a duel with Kujou Sara, and Kuki Shinobu gave hers up willingly and was not much troubled. Nobumori, who surrendered his to Kamisato Ayato, says his old obsessions all disappeared. Jiangxue, who had already won the justice he sought, calls himself free of desire. Those who regain a Vision regain their drive, sometimes muted: Domon felt he had changed too much and left his dream to his disciples. People who have given up a Vision still seem to keep some elemental sensitivity.

Diluc's aspirations, which burned bright in his Vision, were extinguished after Crepus's death; he left Mondstadt and his Vision, and used a Delusion with no apparent ill effect. He returned and resumed using his Vision once his ambition was restored. Many who lost Visions to the Decree did not despair and joined the Watatsumi Army.

Masterless: When an allogene dies, their Vision goes dull, losing colour and power, and becomes a Masterless Vision. A Masterless Vision rarely resonates with someone new.

A Masterless Vision wakes when a person's desire matches the original owner's, and takes on the same element as before. Kaedehara Kazuha briefly woke his late friend's Electro Vision while deflecting the Raiden Shogun's Musou no Hitotachi, using it alongside his own Anemo Vision. It went dormant again afterwards. Most people think two Visions at once is impossible.

Mona and Ningguang are among those who have reawakened Masterless Visions. Separately, counterfeit Visions exist: Venti's fake Vision, which can turn into his lyre, is the only fake known to have a use beyond deception. In a related oddity, in the play "The Little Oceanid", when Furina replaced the actress in the role of Clio, a genuine Hydro Vision appeared before her instead of the prop.

Distribution: Contrary to popular belief, the Archons do not control who receives a Vision. Giving away a shard of their Authority is part of their duty, and they do not know the recipient or the desire. Visions come from whoever holds the elemental Authority, who need not be one of the Seven: after regaining his full Hydro Authority, Neuvillette willingly set aside a portion of it for humans to claim.
After the Vision Hunt Decree began, Electro Visions stopped appearing in Inazuma; scholars at the Sumeru Akademiya who studied this concluded that the Archons' wills decide who gets one. Kazuha likewise guesses that each Archon has their own criteria. But Ei had been sealed in the Plane of Euthymia for about 400 years and was surprised to hear from the Traveler that new Electro Visions had stopped, so the scholars' conclusion is a belief, not settled fact; the true reason is unknown.

Appearance: Visions are orbs set in a regional frame, mostly gold or polished bronze with a few in silver or grey. Mondstadt: a pair of tri-feathered wings. Inazuma: a bow ring with three round studs. Sumeru: a teardrop or leaf frame. Fontaine: ribbon and clamshell ornament in two Arkhe-aligned variants. Natlan: a saltire with meander patterns. Snezhnaya: an orb with angled protrusions top, bottom and sides. For Nod-Krai and Fatui Visions a silver or grey finish is the norm.
Venti's "Vision" is an ordinary glass orb he uses to avoid suspicion, and Zhongli's is probably not a real Vision either. Furina's borrows from both Arkhe-aligned designs, matching her ability to switch alignment. Nicole, an angel who kept her form, has a unique flame-and-wing frame. Aloy's four-pointed star design is of unknown canonicity, since it may be a collaboration feature. The Snezhnayan shape resembles a military badge. The Fatui's Delusions look the same but carry the Fatui emblem in place of the element symbol.

Related objects: Delusions, Gnoses, Moon Wheels and Stellar Linchpins are separate things; do not call them Visions.

A Gnosis is a chess-piece-like object that embodies the Heavenly Principles' control of Teyvat, with only seven made. Archons use their powers without needing it, while humans usually depend on a Vision. A Delusion is a Fatui device that lets anyone wield elements, more powerfully than a Vision and at serious cost, such as lost vitality. Bearers of a Vision or elemental ability resist the effects better.

Moon Wheels (Nod-Krai) look like a Nod-Krai Vision and Stellar Linchpins (Snezhnaya) are four-pointed star objects. The wiki notes that Nod-Krai Visions are indistinguishable from Moon Wheels, which serves as a lore explanation for who cannot enable Lunar reactions via a Moonsign Benediction passive. Vesna's element source in 7.1 is a Stellar Linchpin rather than a Vision.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): each playable character's element corresponds to their Vision, shown in the element icon of their character card. The Traveler has no Vision but resonates with Statues of The Seven to use elements. Vision bearers may use Portable Waypoints.
Gameplay (not literal lore): Elemental Sight is the game's name for sensing elemental sources, and Visions glow near them.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat a Vision as a personal symbol of an unmet or fulfilled ambition. Characters may touch or glance at it when they speak of their goals. Do not make it a mere weapon permit: mention how its owner received it, and let characters differ in attitude, from pride to unease.

A Vision glows faintly when its holder uses or senses the element. Someone who has lost theirs may seem dulled or forgetful about a goal, but canon shows great variation, so not everyone suffers. Never have an Archon say they gave someone a Vision, and do not let an ordinary person know the Celestia link in detail unless the character plausibly learned it.

Avoid showing a Vision as granting unlimited power, as freely transferable between living people, or as destructible. Keep Fatui Delusions distinct from Visions. Do not give the Traveler a Vision.

278.content: An allogene is a person with a desire strong enough to hold a Vision and, in principle, to ascend to Celestia. Venti defines Vision holders this way in Ending Note. The word is the same in Chinese, Japanese and Korean as the game's title.

279.content: A Vision whose owner has died. It loses its colour and elemental power and is an empty husk until someone with the same desire resonates with it. Kazuha's temporary use of his friend's Electro Vision is the best-known case.

280.content: Inazuma's decree under the Raiden Shogun collected Visions from their holders. Losing a Vision had varied effects on memory and ambition, and Electro Visions stopped appearing during it. Full details belong to the Decree's own entry.

281.content: Visions come in a decorative casing set by the nation the person was in when they received it, usually with the same basic shape for the whole region. The finish is usually gold or bronze, and personal decorations such as tassels and charms are added by the owner. Whether the original casing can be altered is not stated, though Yelan's outfit changes the finish.

282.content: Because Vision bearers are matched to constellations, they are said to each hold the power of a tiny cosmos; Liyue's thaumaturges call this the "Microcosmic Orbit" or "Microcosmos". This comes from a challenge in the limited-time Hyakunin Ikki event (2022), so not everyone will know the term.

283.content:
Witchcraft (also: witch magic, Hexenzirkel magic): Witchcraft in Teyvat is not a single taught discipline. The word points at the witches and mages of the Hexenzirkel, the circle of powerful women founded by the adventurer Alice, whose members practise astrology, alchemy and other arts, and at titles such as Lisa's "Witch of Purple Rose". Their powers are shown through individuals, from a near-omnipotent sorceress to members with no magical training at all. The game also uses "Hexerei" as a team-bonus label for characters tied to the circle.

This entry describes the magic the witches use. The circle itself (history, members, island) belongs in the Hexenzirkel faction entry, and the individual practices have their own entries: Alchemy, the Art of Khemia and Mystic Arts in Teyvat (for astrology and hydromancy).

In universe: Hexenzirkel members are called witches or mages, but the label is loose. Alice, the founder, is a long-lived polymath with alchemy, astrology, engineering, magic and medicine among her skills. Barbeloth reads fate by astrology. Rhinedottir practises the Art of Khemia. Nicole is an angel who survived the fall of her kind. Octavia travels the Sea of Stars. Two members, Andersdotter and I. Ivanovna N., never had any magical or combat training.

Members use code letters and epithets: Alice (A, the Merry-Witch), Barbeloth (B, the Seer-Witch), I. Ivanovna N. (J, the Tricksy-Witch), Andersdotter (M, the Story-Witch), Nicole (N, the Memory-Witch), Octavia (O, the Wander-Witch) and Rhinedottir (R, the Sage-Witch). Alice's criterion for inviting members was that they be "interesting"; moral virtue was not required. Members appear in several forms, notably as Dodoco-shaped dolls in witch hats with individually coloured tails, and some voices reach the world through phonographs, teacups or lanterns.

The circle's work is world-scale. It is credited with creating Simulanka (a mirror of Teyvat) and the Imaginarium Theater. It explores the Irminsul, and Alice is described as the Sustainer of the World's Borders who maintains Teyvat's borders and is wary of anyone interfering too much in its affairs. The Hexenzirkel once challenged the Anemo Archon Barbatos, who managed to pacify them and bring the conflict to a peaceful resolution. More recently, at Grand Master Varka's request, Barbatos arranged the Tripartite Conference between himself, the Hexenzirkel and Mondstadt's Knights and Church, and the circle agreed to help Mondstadt in its time of greatest need.

Mystic arts and witchcraft overlap but differ in scope: the Mystic Arts overview groups regional traditions, whereas witchcraft is tied to one circle of individuals whose powers are not regional and some of whom rival gods. Alice is the member most often shown doing physical wonders (lifting or shaping island systems on command) while Barbeloth's reach is informational: she reads the fortunes of nations, Teyvat and the world.

Members: Seven founding members are named in canon. Alice and Barbeloth are the circle's best-known active practitioners; Nicole is a playable angel; Octavia created the pocket realm Miliastra Wonderland and has visited at least 1,896 planets; Rhinedottir is one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah and, after merging with Naberius, the Ruler of Life among the Four Shades. Andersdotter (deceased) was an acclaimed writer; I. Ivanovna N. (deceased) became a powerful Snezhnayan politician and the first Mayor of Snezhnograd.

- Successors: becoming a member's successor does not guarantee membership. Scarlett is the successor of J.
- Mona calls Barbeloth her master and Scarlett calls her Barbeloth's student, not successor; after Alice's explanation in the 3.5 event Mona was surprised that so many mysterious women all knew one another, so her own membership is unclear.
- Not all witches are members: Lisa denies interest, and Signora, once the Crimson Witch of Flame, has no known ties and takes offence at being called a witch.
- Klee is Alice's daughter but has not learned Alice's magic; Alice has hinted that she will teach her when she is ready.

Practices: - Divination: Barbeloth pioneered hydromancy (a subclass of astrology) and is said to be able to read the fates of whole nations and the world; Mona practises it as her student. Barbeloth's case of oracles is tied to the Lunar Arcana.
- Alchemy and life-making: Alice practises alchemy; Rhinedottir's Art of Khemia creates life and does not entirely conform to Teyvat's rules.
- Life extension: Alice can extend a human's lifespan through magic (Andersdotter refused).
- Realm-making: Simulanka, the Imaginarium Theater and Miliastra Wonderland are all creations of members, and members are said to rewrite fate in some cases. Andersdotter helped Simulanka's creation and rewrote fate for her child, Durin.

Rhinedottir's creations were involved in the Cataclysm and she served the Khaenri'ahn dynasty; she is a Hexenzirkel mage and a Sinner at once. Members also invent: Alice's inventions include a phonograph, the Temari game, explosive Dodoco dolls and a long-distance instant communication device.

Status 7 1: As of 7.1, Rhinedottir is alive and merged with Naberius. In the 7.1 Archon Quest "Black Feathers Scattered at Parting" she told Anastasya (the Tsaritsa) that, as a representative of the Hexenzirkel, she was pleased with Snezhnaya's growth. Earlier, Alice and Nicole appeared in person in the Nod-Krai Archon Quest "Ripples That Will Never Reach" (6.2). The circle's wider goals remain unrevealed.

Little hexenzirkel: In the 6.6 event Phantasmal Pals (limited-time, May 22 to June 8, 2026) Klee founded the Little Hexenzirkel with imaginary friends: Qiqi (Tuantuan), Sayu (Gena), Yaoyao (Yuegui) and later Prune (Descartes), with Paimon joining without an imaginary friend. It is a playful event group that borrows the circle's name, not part of the original circle.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): "Hexerei" is a team-bonus label. After completing Witch's Homework, a character becomes a Hexerei character, and the Hexerei: Secret Rite team bonus applies when the party has two or more of them. The Little Witch's Dictionary, received from Alice, is the item that issues the homework. The wiki lists Albedo, Klee, Mona, Venti, Durin, Varka, Nicole, Lohen, Fischl, Razor, Sucrose and Prune among them.

The unlock requires owning the character at level 70 or higher, then completing their quest. Each Hexerei character gets a Witch's Eve Rite Passive. The Witch's Revelation system is separate: it uses Barbeloth's case of oracles, tied to the Lunar Arcana, to give some characters (such as Wriothesley, Yae Miko, Cyno, Mizuki, Qiqi, Diona and Beidou) additional passives.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): present witchcraft as personality plus craft, not a spell list. A Hexenzirkel scene is playful on the surface, with teacups, tea parties and Dodoco-shaped messengers, while the power underneath is ancient and world-scale. Different witches should feel different: Alice's enthusiasm, Barbeloth's teasing way with fate, Nicole's silence, Rhinedottir's coldness and strictness (as Albedo remembers her).

Members rarely act in the open; they send messages, dolls and cryptic readings. Use hints (a tail-tip colour, a hat, a tea cup) to signal them. Magic has costs and consequences in fate, such as astrologers entangling their own destiny.

Do not turn Klee into a trained witch, treat every Mondstadt scholar as a Hexenzirkel member, or call Signora a witch to her face without consequence. Do not resolve the circle's goals or number of members. Do not let Hexerei, the gameplay label, imply a character is in the circle.

Limits: No unified rules exist. Each member's feats are personal, from Alice's island-moving to Barbeloth's readings; some members have no magic at all. Even the powerful are limited: Barbeloth, for instance, warns that revealing fate too readily spoils the future.

The circle acts by agreement, not command, and its members mostly pursue their own goals. Rhinedottir's merger with Naberius shows that even a member's choices have consequences: Naberius still voices her disapproval within their shared mind.

284.content: The Hexenzirkel is the circle of witches that Alice founded; its members use code letters A, B, J, M, N, O and R and epithets such as Merry-Witch, Seer-Witch and Sage-Witch. They gather for "formal tea parties" and have used a secret island above Falcon Coast. Their purpose is mysterious. See the Hexenzirkel faction entry.

285.content: Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus, the Seer-Witch (B), is the master hydromancer who taught Mona. She is Alice's friend and rival, and an elderly woman in blue witch attire. She mapped the fates of all living things in Simulanka and, according to Mona, can read the fortunes of nations and the world.

286.content: Alice (A) is a travel writer, adventurer and the founder of the Hexenzirkel, a long-lived elf-eared woman at least 500 years old, and Klee's mother. Albedo calls her a near-omnipotent sorceress. She appears chiefly as a voice in a Dodoco, phonograph or teacup, and first appeared in person in the 6.2 Nod-Krai quest. See her own entry.

287.content: Gameplay: the Hexerei team bonus rewards parties of characters who have completed Witch's Homework. Alice gives the player the Little Witch's Dictionary in the quest "Unexpected Commission". This is a game label, not proof of Hexenzirkel membership.

288.content:
Witch's Homework (also: Witch's Homework quests, The Little Witch's Dictionary, Witch's Eve Rite Passive, Witch's Eve Rite): Witch's Homework is a system from Version 6.2 in which The Little Witch's Dictionary hands out tasks, made by the Hexenzirkel's mages, to friends of the Traveler. Finishing a character's task makes them a Hexerei character and unlocks a bonus Talent for them, the Witch's Eve Rite Passive. In story terms the "homework" is the witches' long-range preparation to help Mondstadt in a future time of need.

The Traveler gets the dictionary in the world quest "Unexpected Commission", set at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters in Mondstadt.

In universe: Alice, a Hexenzirkel mage, wrote the dictionary with other mages. The title is a disguise: it claims to explain the storybook "The Little Witch and the Undying Fire", but the two books are unrelated and the dictionary is really full of tasks tailored to individual readers. The item text says it was made by the witches and is "actually filled with homework tailored by the Hexenzirkel for each reader."

Alice explains the reason in "Unexpected Commission": the Hexenzirkel promised Varka at the Tripartite Conference that in Mondstadt's greatest time of need the mages would return and help. Rather than appear out of nowhere, they chose to lay groundwork over time (a line she attributes to "M", the Hexenzirkel's Andersdotter). The tasks, drawn up after looking into Barbeloth's scryglass, are about striving toward a common goal, overcoming obstacles with trusted companions and becoming better people. Alice stresses this is preparation, not a warning that something is about to happen. Item and event text add the motto "To defy the current is to learn."

Alice hid the dictionary among a large donation of books to the Mondstadt library, because bringing it into Teyvat openly was risky; the donation was also what brought the Traveler and Paimon to the library, where Lisa asked them to sort it. When Paimon opens the dictionary the library turns grey and she and the Traveler enter a mage's domain, where Alice, in her Dodoco form, explains it. Paimon accepts on the understanding that the tasks go to the Traveler's friends, because the pool of people who count as "a friend to all in Mondstadt" is the Traveler.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): each Witch's Homework quest belongs to one character. The player must own that character and have them at level 70 or higher. Finishing it makes the character a Hexerei character and unlocks their Witch's Eve Rite Passive, which also changes some of their Talents and Constellations.

Most of these enhancements work only when at least two Hexerei characters are in the party, which switches on the Hexerei: Secret Rite Team Bonus (own entry, Hexerei). The dictionary is a gadget that lets the player view and accept the tasks; the same quest also invites Razor, Fischl or Sucrose to the party from the event menu.

The wiki's list of Hexerei characters, with each one's act, quest and Witch's Eve Rite Passive, as of 7.1:
- Albedo: Of Questions Beyond Questions; quest "Old Friends and New Knowledge"; Book of Blinding Light.
- Klee: Of Leaves That Spark; "The Great Mage's Journey of Trials"; Sparkborne Magic.
- Mona: Of Untested Insight; "A Dry Well Doth Not Reflect the Stars"; Genesis of Starsigns.
- Venti: Of the Waking of Wind; "Tales of Time and Wind"; Temporal Wind's Eulogy.
- Durin: Of This World; "A Child Wandering the World"; Ode to Ascension.
- Varka: The Untitled Question; "Stories to Sate the Glass and Scroll"; Dawn's Return.
- Nicole: The Role of a Guide...?; its own Witch's Homework quest; Light in the Darkness.
- Lohen: Of Various Foes; "Proof of Strength"; Unhealing Thorn.
- Fischl: Of the Unexpected; "Alan Smithee, Author of Fischl"; Phantasmal Nocturne.
- Razor: Of the Little Wolf Pack; "With Lupical..."; Surge of Lightning.
- Sucrose: Of Wonderland Flowers; "The Law of Boundaries"; Sevenfold Transmutation.
- Prune: Of What Is Contested; "A Proposition Beyond Refutation"; Witchseeker's Vow.

The wiki infobox files Witch's Homework under Mondstadt, and the system's quests are structured as one act and one quest per character, so each homework is a self-contained story. The list also includes characters with no particular Mondstadt link in the table, so treat the region label as a setting for the dictionary, not a requirement.

Release note: Witch's Homework arrived in Version 6.2, "A Nocturne of the Far North" (2025-12-03), together with the Hexerei Team Bonus. A later system with the same flavour, Witch's Revelation, followed in 6.7 (own entry).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the homework as the Hexenzirkel's gentle, slightly mischievous coaching, framed by Alice's cheer. A character who "has done their homework" has simply taken on a task from the dictionary with companions. Do not suggest Hexerei characters are all witches or Hexenzirkel members, or that a specific disaster is coming to Mondstadt.

Limits: Canon text seen names only the dictionary's framing, the Hexenzirkel's promise and the broad themes of the tasks. The system does not say who is a witch, and "Hexerei" is a gameplay label. Do not invent additional rules for what each homework contains beyond what each character's quest shows.

289.comment: Witch's Homework: The Little Witch's Dictionary
289.content: A 5-star gadget received from Alice in "Unexpected Commission" and reusable. Its item text calls it a dictionary created by the witches that claims to explain the storybook "The Little Witch and the Undying Fire" but is in fact filled with homework tailored by the Hexenzirkel for each reader, and ends with the words "To defy the current is to learn. Embark on your journey with your companions and seek the crown of elevation!" The dictionary's contents are not related to the storybook.

290.comment: Witch's Homework: Witch's Eve Rite Passive
290.content: The additional Talent a Hexerei character gains after finishing their Witch's Homework. Most of what it enhances, in the character's Talents and Constellations, applies when at least two Hexerei characters are in the party under Hexerei: Secret Rite.

291.content:
Witch's Revelation (also: Witch's Revelation Passive, Revelations by Chance): Witch's Revelation is a system from Version 6.7 in which the fortune-teller Barbeloth's Witch's Revelation Case holds oracles for particular characters. Completing a character's Witch's Revelation quest unlocks an extra Talent, the Witch's Revelation Passive, and enhances some of their Talents and Constellations. It is the sequel in spirit to Witch's Homework: Barbeloth and Alice are again behind it.

The Traveler gets the case in the Fontaine world quest "Revelations by Chance", near the Court of Fontaine.

In universe: Barbeloth, a powerful fortune teller, is running a small divination stand just outside the Court of Fontaine, and tells the Traveler that as a Descender from beyond the world the Traveler's own fate cannot be predicted by most fortune tellers, herself included. She recently glimpsed an omen, followed it and caught threads of fate and the faces of their owners, who are all people the Traveler knows.

Alice, who is helping with the divination, joins through Barbeloth's Dodoco-shaped stand-in and wants to hold a party for everyone involved. Barbeloth considers invitations delivered by messenger birds likely to disturb fate and refuses, but allows the Traveler to bring the people to the stall because their fates are already tied to the Traveler's. The case itself, per item text, once belonged to Barbeloth and contains every oracle, those already revealed and those still to come; she says she prefers a future with secrets still to unfold.

The Version 6.7 promotional material frames it as a new reading by the seer-witch: the warp and weft of fate emerge through an ancient spread of cards (the Lunar Arcanum). Barbeloth insists, in the promotional text, that hydromancy is "the one true legitimate art", and remarks that what used to be "fate" has long been disrupted by unforeseen events. After the quest, Barbeloth stays at the stand with her research and says a reminder will reach her when the person involved in an oracle arrives.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): each quest belongs to one character. The player must own that character at level 70 or higher. Finishing it unlocks the Witch's Revelation Passive and changes some Talents and Constellations. The Passive also lets the character enter the Radiance state under certain conditions.

The Passive allows a character to enter Radiance: Stellar-Conduct while inside a Polestar Field. A Polestar Field is created by the Starlight Prism that forms when the Stellar-Conduct reaction (Cryo with Electro, a Stellar Glimmer reaction) is triggered. The "Revelations by Chance" quest follows "Song of the Dragon and Freedom" and gives the player the case, 20 Primogems, Hero's Wit and Mora.

The seven eligible characters, with the quest and the Lunar Arcanum card attached to each, as of 7.1:
- Wriothesley: "Witch's Revelation: Warden's Instruction"; The Emperor (Upright); There Shall Be an Unveiling for Injustice.
- Yae Miko: "Witch's Revelation: Great Youkai's Instruction"; Justice (Reversed); Edict of Cleansing.
- Cyno: "Witch's Revelation: Duty's Instruction"; Temperance (Reversed); A Star With Which to Start the Journey.
- Yumemizuki Mizuki: "Witch's Revelation: Instruction Beyond Dreams"; The Moon (Reversed); Vast Be the Dream.
- Qiqi: "Witch's Revelation: Instruction of Curious Form"; The Hanged Man (Upright); Seven Sacred Treasures.
- Diona: "Witch's Revelation: Special Blend's Instruction"; The High Priestess (Reversed); Choice Treasures.
- Beidou: "Witch's Revelation: Voyaging Instruction"; Strength (Upright); Polaris.

The wiki's own description for the map marker reads "The witch's revelation awaits the one who will uncover it", and the event overview describes the seer-witch beginning "a new reading". Each quest title ends in "Instruction" and names its character by role or trait (Warden, Great Youkai, Duty, Beyond Dreams, Curious Form, Special Blend, Voyaging).

Release note: Witch's Revelation was introduced in Version 6.7, "Sunny Summer Fontinalia" (Luna VIII, 2026-07-01). Its announcements presented it as the witch's new divination, with an accompanying new reaction and Talents. Witch's Homework (6.2) is the earlier system of this kind.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): play Barbeloth as dry, teasing and unwilling to explain fate in full, and Alice as warmly enthusiastic about parties. A character with a Revelation has simply been "read" by Barbeloth; do not claim the reading predicts their death or doom, since canon seen here states no specific outcome. Do not claim Barbeloth can read the Traveler's fate.

Limits: Canon gives only the stand, the case, a rough sense that fate is being nudged, and the seven character quests. Do not invent contents of the oracles, the cause of the prophecy, or the nature of Radiance. Barbeloth stays out of the way of the Traveler's future, which she says she cannot see.

292.content: A 5-star reusable gadget obtained in "Revelations by Chance", used to view and accept Witch's Revelation tasks. Its text says the case once carried by Barbeloth has reached the Traveler, and holds all the oracles, both revealed and not yet opened, with Barbeloth declining to say whether they could steer fate.

293.content: The additional Talent unlocked by a Witch's Revelation quest. It enhances some of the character's Talents and Constellations and allows entry to the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state within a Polestar Field.
